# Phase C5: hardware as nodes - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for
> tracking.

**Goal:** An Everdrive N8 Pro in a real NES and a Novation Launchpad become ordinary graph nodes: `rp.n8.nes` takes the
same `midi` and `bytes` inputs as an emulated NES and pushes them at the host's cart link, `rp.launchpad.surface-in` /
`-out` carry the control surface's two directions, and memory, battery and ROM operations become `rp.system.memory/1`,
`.sram/1` and `.rom/1` capability jobs that an emulated core answers at a block boundary and a real cart answers on its
own thread. A node reaches a host-owned device through `rp.host.devices/1`, a host with no device gives it a handle that
is never connected, and the engine loses its cart mirror, its controller channel and its last console name.

**Architecture:** Per [modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md](modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md), which Task 7 lands as the
record of what was built. The hosts keep owning the serial port, MIDI ports, pairing and reconnecting; a node binds a
link by name and gets its streaming rings, connected state and, for a cart, its job runner. Placement is by setting,
not device state: a NES's `driveRealCart` places one `rp.n8.nes`, the controller setting places both surface nodes,
and a plug, reset or job never edits the graph. Capabilities are asynchronous: the control thread submits a job and
polls a completion queue, an emulated read completes from the snapshot registry at once, an emulated write at the next
block boundary, and an N8 job on the link's serial thread while streaming is paused. The surface is two nodes because
one node that both feeds a session and follows it is a node-level cycle. `buildGraph` fans a system's protocol outputs
into both the emulated and the real NES, stages UI MIDI at a node through `rp.stage/1`, and puts the cart menu on the
capability API. The old engine paths are then deleted.

**Tech stack:** C++20 with Catch2 (`retroplug-engine-graph-test`, `retroplug-graph-test`, `retroplug-audio-test`,
`retroplug-n8-test`, `retroplug-launchpad-test`), the in-tree Mesen fork, reflect-cpp, the graph layer of Phases A to
C4, and TypeScript for the control plane (`buildGraph`, the UI, the mock backend, the CLI harness). No submodule moves.

**Spec:** [modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md](modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md).

`proto/c5-hw` in this worktree, on top of the design commit 55042f5c: seven commits, one per task (Task 8 is the
acceptance run and commits nothing), with GCC 13.3 on linux-x64 (a Ryzen 9 9950X). A block that creates a file is that

**Where this plan departs from the design as committed (55042f5c).** The design was written before the prototype;
this plan follows what was built, and Task 7 lands the design with its Status line, sections 3 to 6 corrected, section
9's questions answered in a new section 10 ("As built"), and section 10 renamed "Left as it is". In short:
- **The surface is two nodes, `rp.launchpad.surface-in` and `-out`, not one.** One node that both feeds a session
  and follows it is a node-level cycle; the planner refuses it, and the only wire that breaks a cycle is a feedback
  wire, which delivers the previous block. Two nodes keep every stream in its own block, and the session's recorded
  digests and per-block LED stream are identical: Task 5 rewrites the goldens' documents for the new wiring, and the
  digests the protocol test records do not move.
- **The N8's battery goes through the SD card's save file, at the menu only.** The prototype first read the cart's
  own memory; on the real console a 64 KB read with a game running froze it, and a read at the menu left the menu
  deaf to its commands until a power-cycle. Chunking did not help. By the user's decision `sram.dump` lists
  `EDN8/gamedata/<rom>/bram.srm` and reads it in 512-byte blocks (62 s for 66,560 bytes on the hardware), and
  `sram.restore` writes it in 4 KB ones (716 ms), creating the folder and saying so in its result. The game loads it
  at its next boot, so a restore goes before a `rom.upload`. A running game refuses both jobs, and the direct
  cart-memory paths, the liveness probe and the test-only override went. The CLI's raw `n8` tools keep their own
  battery dump and are unchanged.
- **Pausing N8Link for a job is a real pause inside the serial thread, not a disconnect and reopen.** The thread
  sets `connected` false, writes what the ring already holds at its release times, waits (bounded) for the reliable
  link's outstanding frames to be acknowledged, runs the job on its own Edio, and resumes with the port and the
  sequence state untouched. A disconnect would lose the last lookahead's chunks, destroy the reliable sender's state
  and let another process take the port.
- **The node owes note-offs a pause dropped.** It keeps the notes the cart holds and, of those, ones whose note-off
  the link dropped, and re-sends them at frame 0 of the first block the link reads connected again, so no note is
  left sounding.
- **`N8Link::postControl` was replaced by the expansion volume's atomic and generation.** The block only clamps,
  stores and bumps a generation; the serial thread applies the standing value at the top of its turn, so a failed
  write retries and no lock or `std::function` is on the audio path. `N8Link::setOnControl` is the one callback set
  before connect.
- **`Engine::clearGraph` is the hosts' teardown seam.** Member order cannot put a host's devices before the engine
  (they read its config directory), so `~PluginDSP` and `~AppState` reclaim their plans first, while every device
  member is alive, then uninstall the links. Without it a node's destroy would give a handle back to a destroyed
  device.
- **`Engine::addNodePackage` is a TEST / HARNESS seam** so the `[devices]` cases can run a probe node on the real
  engine; it returns a bool with the refusal reason, like `putResource`, and is not a production registration path.
- **Uniqueness is a descriptor flag, not a type name in the engine.** `"unique":true`, true or absent, is parsed by
  `parseDescriptor`, carried by both surface types and `rp.n8.nes`, and checked by the planner, which refuses a
  second node of a unique type in a plan with code `unique`. TS's `defineNode` carries it too.
- **UI MIDI is staged at a node through `rp.stage/1`, and `Engine::stageSystemMidi` was deleted.** The command
  addresses a node of the running plan, not a system or a port: a system node hands the bytes to its core's ingress
  (the raw door where it has one), the cart node pushes them at the link. TS stages at `sys-<id>` and at `cart-<id>`
  when one is placed. `stageSystemMidi`, its command kind, invoker, RPC and registration all went in Task 6; its two
  behaviours live in `rp.stage/1`'s cases.
- **`rp.engine.host-io` moved from `/2` to `/3`.** The controller halves and the cart byte sink left the struct, and
  the id moved because a node built against `/2` would read past its end. Every node is in tree; there is no shim.
- **`driveRealCart` defaults ON, and at most one cart node is placed.** It is a NES role setting (additive, no
  migration), and `buildGraph` places one `rp.n8.nes` for the first NES in slot order whose setting is on, with id
  `cart-<system>`, fanned out from what feeds that system's `midi` and `bytes`. A second driving NES gets no node;
  turning it off hands the cart to the next NES that drives one. A project with no NES no longer forwards DAW MIDI
  to the cart: the old raw fallback would now arrive twice beside the fan-out, and restoring it would be a rule of
  the shape this phase removed, so it is recorded as a loss rather than invented.
- **`surface-in` discards what the link held when it bound it.** Traffic the device sent before the plan existed is
  not replayed into a session; a reactivate that keeps the handle does not discard again. `HarnessSurfaceLink`
  clears its own input per `renderBlocks` run for the same reason.
- **`HarnessSurfaceLink` is the harness's controller seam.** `stageControllerIn` and `renderBlocks`' controller
  field queue into a surface link the test host installs; a harness-facet host with no surface link refuses them
  instead of staging into nothing. It stores nothing on the way out, counts what it drops and reports `connected()`
  false.
- **Package versions stay `1.0.0`.** A version is a descriptor marker that never gates; a document naming a removed
  type is refused `unknown-type` by the planner at any version. `rp.n8` keeps `1.0.0` after losing
  `rp.n8.cart-mirror`, and `rp.host.io` keeps `1.0.0` after losing two node types.
- **The CLI's n8 tools are unchanged.** They run with no engine and no `N8Host` and need the raw link (peek, poke,
  the sniffer, FIFO reads, the battery dump) that the capabilities deliberately do not offer. The only n8 code that
  moves is the host's SD worker, which Task 6 deletes, and the manual `n8-sd-hwtest`, which is re-pointed through
  `submitCartJob` rather than deleted.
- **The emulated capabilities are narrower than the design's prose.** `rp.system.memory/1` lists one region,
  `"ram"`, the work RAM that `readRam` and `writeRam` reached; an emulated `sram.restore` is refused at submission,
  because a core's restore is the rebuild that seeds it and the snapshot registry answers reads, not writes, so
  `CoreSram::restores()` is false; and `rom.header` and `rom.title` answer from the image this host booted, and are
  refused after a power-cycle or a game the cart's own browser booted, since nothing can then say which image is
  running. The old `writeRam` RPC answers false when the command ring is full rather than blocking or dropping the
  write.
- **Task 3's hardware smoke is provenance, not an implementer step.** On the real NES and N8 Pro the prototype
  measured a pause that kept the reliable link continuous (resends 0, outstanding 0, no re-sync) and notes before
  and after it (A4 440.30 Hz, E5 657.66 Hz, silent after the note-off); a battery dump, restore and dump
  round-tripped byte for byte through the card's file (66,560 bytes restored through the job, the song table read
  off the screen against the save); and a ROM uploaded through the job booted in 2.8 s with the header matching the
  file. Those figures are the prototype's own scratch harnesses' (`/tmp/c5pro/hw/sd.cpp` and `smoke.cpp`), not
  `retroplug-n8-hwtest`'s: that harness's re-pointed `submitCartJob` path first runs on hardware in Task 8. The rig
  was left at a fresh menu with every scratch file deleted. Task 8 repeats the checks as acceptance, run by the
  controller.

**Ground rules for whoever executes this:**
- This plan lives at `docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-plan.md` and is committed before Task 1 (a docs commit of its own):
  the header's link to the design is relative to that location; every command and path in the steps is relative to
  the worktree root.
- Commit after each task (the commands are given; Task 8 commits nothing unless a step fails and is fixed, in a commit
  of its own). No `Co-Authored-By` or "generated with" trailer.
- Do not push, and do not open a PR.
- Never use an emdash character in code, comments, docs or commit messages; use " - ", ":" or ";". Some diffs below
  carry emdashes on lines the prototype did not write (context and removed lines of older code): leave those be.
- Run every command from the worktree root with absolute paths or a subshell (`(cd x && ...)`); never `cd` the session
  itself.
- Don't `rm -rf build` to fix CMake; investigate. Never use bare `git stash`, and never switch branches with uncommitted
  work in the tree. Never touch a submodule. `deps/sameboy` shows as modified after any configure: that is the tracked
  audio patch, expected, leave it.
- The derived bundle C arrays (`build/native/*bundle_data.c`) are never committed.
- Parity holds the engine's output to the bit, and no task re-records it: C5 changes no emulated audio path, so a
  strict parity failure is a real change. Stop and find it. Never set `RP_PARITY_UPDATE`. The one re-record this plan
  expects is Task 5's role and build-graph goldens, and there only.
- The fixture groups need `RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources` on the same command line; without it their
  cases skip. A shell `export` does not survive between commands.
- `pnpm test:n8` is not part of `pnpm test:plugin`: run it wherever a task touches `packages/native/src/host/n8`.
- The Catch2 binaries are `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL`: `cmake --build build` does not relink them, so a library edit needs the
  test target built by name before a run. A new test source needs `cmake -S . -B build` first.
- The sanitizer trees are their own: `build-tsan/` and `build-asan/` (configured with `-DRETROPLUG_SANITIZE=thread` or
  `=address`). Configure one only if its `CMakeCache.txt` is missing. Build the binary in that tree before running it
  there; a stale prototype binary proves nothing. The profile build is its own tree too (`build-prof/`).
- `pnpm check:docs` counts the tracked docs: 70 in the prototype, which had no plan file, so 71 once this plan is
  committed.
- Case counts are exact. A `test cases: N | P passed | S skipped` line, an `All tests passed (A assertions in N test
  cases)` line and a per-file count must match the quoted N/P/S. Assertion totals are exact too, with one exception: a
  run that includes `[capability]`, and so any run of the whole engine-graph binary, may report 2 or 4 more assertions
  than quoted. The device-thread case reports one progress entry per report, and a drain that lands between the final
  progress store and `Done` legitimately yields one more entry (2 assertions; two more entries make 4). Any other
  difference is a finding.
- The prototype branch `proto/c5-hw` is this plan's provenance. Task 5 Step 4's `git diff --stat f8db3f3b` reads the
  stage-5 commit on it, so keep the branch until Task 5 is committed; after that no step reads it, and it may be
  deleted once the plan has been executed and verified.
- While a Reaper check runs it uses `build/bin`: do not rebuild the plugin until it finishes. Run the Reaper checks one
  at a time, and before each make sure no Reaper or jackd of an earlier run is left (`pgrep -a reaper; pgrep -a jackd`).

### Task 1: `rp.host.devices/1`, the device links a node binds by name

Design sections 3 and 8 item 1. The host keeps owning the devices; a node binds one by name through
`rp_host.get_interface(host, "rp.host.devices/1")` and is handed a link for the life of its plan. A cart link (`"n8"`)
offers a push at an intra-block frame with the block's rate, its connected state, the pushes it lost and the
expansion-audio register; a surface link (`"launchpad"`) offers a drain into storage the caller owns, a lock-free
output queue, its connected state and its dropped count. The engine holds the links its host installs and answers every
name, including one no host owns, with a handle that is never connected and accepts and drops everything: never null,
so a document plans and runs the same in every host. The plugin installs the cart link over its `N8Host` and the SDL
standalone installs both; the CLI, the Node addon, the render host and the UI harness install none.

**Files:**
- Create: `packages/native/src/host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/devices/DeviceRegistry.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/launchpad/LaunchpadSurfaceLink.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/n8/N8CartLink.hpp`, `packages/native/test/engine-graph/Devices.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/launchpad/LaunchpadSurfaceLink.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/n8/N8CartLink.test.cpp`
- Modify: `packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake`, `packages/native/plugin/PluginDSP.cpp`, `packages/native/sdl/main.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/engine/Engine.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/engine/Engine.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/graph/HostServices.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/launchpad/LaunchpadLink.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/launchpad/LaunchpadLink.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/n8/N8Host.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/n8/N8Host.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/n8/N8Link.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/n8/N8Link.hpp`, `packages/native/test/launchpad/LaunchpadLink.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/n8/N8Host.test.cpp`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing cases**

`Devices.test.cpp` (new, tag `[devices]`) drives a probe node on the real `Engine`: it acquires both links in
`activate`, pushes and drains in `process` and releases in destroy, over fakes that record each push (frame, bytes,
flush, rate) and each surface message, script the surface's input and count acquires and releases. Six cases plus the
review's five: order, frames, flush and rate; the surface's input in order and its output recorded; a link whose
device goes away; a host with no device; acquire and release across a reactivate, a removal and a re-add; a 44100 Hz
push; an unknown name; a release after the links are cleared; the cart's full ring; and a warmed block that allocates
and frees nothing (`CountingAllocator`, 0/0). The N8 and Launchpad adapter files hold the transports to their bytes
and their drops, including the expansion volume from a second thread and a drain that allocates nothing.

Create `packages/native/test/engine-graph/Devices.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// The host's device links, rp.host.devices/1 (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md sections 3 to 5): a node binds the
// hardware it drives by name and is handed a link, which it borrows for the life of its plan and gives back when the
// plan's reclaim destroys it. Driven on a real Engine with a test node that does what rp.n8.nes and
// rp.launchpad.surface will: it acquires both links in its activate, pushes at the cart's frame offsets in its block,
// drains the surface into storage it owns and pushes one LED message back, and releases both in its destructor.
//
// The links here are fakes that record what a node did with them, and count how many nodes hold them: what reaches the
// device, its order and frames, the connected state a host with no device leaves in place, the balance of acquire and
// release across a plan replaced and a node removed, and a warmed block that allocates and frees nothing.
//
// Run via `pnpm test:plugin engine-graph`.

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <iterator>
#include <vector>

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "../graph/CountingAllocator.hpp"
#include "GraphDocs.hpp"
#include "graph/node.hpp"
#include "host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp"
#include "host/engine/Engine.hpp"
#include "host/graph/HostServices.hpp"

namespace {

using rp::host::CartLink;
using rp::host::DeviceMessage;
using rp::host::HostDevices;
using rp::host::SurfaceLink;

constexpr double        kRate   = 48000.0;
constexpr std::uint32_t kFrames = 64;

// One message the probe pushes at the cart, scripted by the test.
struct CartPush {
    std::uint32_t             frame = 0;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> data;
    bool                      flush = false;
};

// What the probe node reads and writes: a document cannot carry a pointer, and the engine hands a test no handle on a
// node's instance (NodeRig does), so the probe's script and what it saw live here. One case at a time, as the suite
// runs. `process` only reads the vector and writes the fixed members, so a counted block allocates nothing.
struct ProbeScript {
    std::vector<CartPush>              cart;         // pushed on the next block, in order
    std::array<DeviceMessage, 16>      drained{};    // what the last block drained from the surface
    std::size_t                        drainedCount = 0;
    double                             rate         = 0.0;  // the rate the last block pushed the cart at
    std::uint64_t                      cartDropped  = 0;    // the cart link's count of lost pushes, as the node sees it
    const char*                        cartName     = rp::host::kCartDeviceName;     // what the node asks for
    const char*                        surfaceName  = rp::host::kSurfaceDeviceName;  // what the node asks for
    bool                               destroyed    = false;  // the node's destroy ran
    std::uint64_t                      droppedAtDestroy = 0;  // a read of the cart's count from the destroy
};
ProbeScript script;

// The message the probe always pushes at the surface, so a case sees the node's own LED traffic beside what it drained.
constexpr std::uint8_t kSurfaceOut[] = {0xB0, 0x10, 0x7F};

// A node that binds both device links, the way the two hardware nodes will: acquire in activate, use in process, give
// the handles back from the destructor that the plan's reclaim runs (on the control thread).
struct DeviceProbe {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.test.device-probe";

    const HostDevices*   devices = nullptr;
    CartLink*            cart    = nullptr;
    SurfaceLink*         surface = nullptr;
    std::array<DeviceMessage, 16> in{};  // in the node's own storage, so the drain frees nothing on the block thread

    void bind_host(const rp_host* h) noexcept {
        devices = static_cast<const HostDevices*>(h->get_interface(h, RP_HOST_DEVICES_INTERFACE));
    }
    bool activate(double, std::uint32_t) {
        if (!devices) return false;
        // A reactivate (a sample-rate change, a block growth) runs activate again on this same instance: a handle
        // already held is kept, so one acquire here is one release in the destructor.
        if (!cart) cart = devices->acquireCart(devices->ctx, script.cartName);
        if (!surface) surface = devices->acquireSurface(devices->ctx, script.surfaceName);
        return cart != nullptr && surface != nullptr;
    }
    void process(const rp::Block& b) noexcept {
        script.rate = b.transport().sample_rate;
        for (const CartPush& p : script.cart)
            cart->push(p.frame, p.data.data(), p.data.size(), p.flush, script.rate);
        surface->pushOutput(kSurfaceOut, sizeof kSurfaceOut);
        const std::size_t n = surface->drainInput(in.data(), in.size());
        script.drainedCount = n;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) script.drained[i] = in[i];
        script.cartDropped = cart->dropped();
    }
    ~DeviceProbe() {
        if (!devices) return;
        // A host tears its plans down while its links are alive, so a node may use a handle here, not only give it
        // back: this reads the cart's drop count before releasing both.
        script.droppedAtDestroy = cart ? cart->dropped() : 0;
        if (cart) devices->releaseCart(devices->ctx, cart);
        if (surface) devices->releaseSurface(devices->ctx, surface);
        script.destroyed = true;
    }
};

const rp_package* deviceProbePackage() {
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<DeviceProbe>()};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.test.devices"})",
                                     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::size(kTypes)), kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

// A cart link that records every push and what a node asked of it, and counts the nodes holding it.
class FakeCartLink final : public CartLink {
public:
    // A slot of its own, so a recorded push copies bytes and never allocates: reserve(n) before a counted block.
    struct Push {
        std::uint32_t frame      = 0;
        double        sampleRate = 0.0;
        bool          flush      = false;
        std::uint16_t size       = 0;
        std::uint8_t  data[rp::host::kMaxDeviceMessage] = {};
    };

    void reserve(std::size_t n) { pushes.reserve(n); }

    void push(std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, bool flush,
              double sampleRate) override {
        if (!attached) {  // the device went away: the bytes go nowhere, as a real link's do
            ++drops;
            return;
        }
        Push p;
        p.frame      = frame;
        p.flush      = flush;
        p.sampleRate = sampleRate;
        p.size       = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(std::min(size, rp::host::kMaxDeviceMessage));
        std::memcpy(p.data, data, p.size);
        pushes.push_back(p);
    }
    bool          connected() const override { return attached; }
    std::uint64_t dropped() const override { return drops; }
    void          setExpansionVolume(int value) override { volume = value; }
    void          acquire() override { ++acquires; }
    void          release() override { ++releases; }

    bool              attached = true;
    std::uint64_t     drops    = 0;
    int               volume   = -1;
    int               acquires = 0;
    int               releases = 0;
    std::vector<Push> pushes;
};

// A surface link with a scripted input and a recorded output, likewise counted.
class FakeSurfaceLink final : public SurfaceLink {
public:
    struct Out {
        std::uint16_t size = 0;
        std::uint8_t  data[rp::host::kMaxDeviceMessage] = {};
    };

    void reserve(std::size_t in, std::size_t out) {
        input.reserve(in);
        outputs.reserve(out);
    }

    std::size_t drainInput(DeviceMessage* out, std::size_t capacity) override {
        std::size_t n = 0;
        while (next < input.size() && n < capacity) out[n++] = input[next++];
        return n;
    }
    void pushOutput(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) override {
        if (!attached) {
            ++drops;
            return;
        }
        Out m;
        m.size = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(std::min(size, rp::host::kMaxDeviceMessage));
        std::memcpy(m.data, data, m.size);
        outputs.push_back(m);
    }
    bool connected() const override { return attached; }
    void acquire() override { ++acquires; }
    void release() override { ++releases; }

    bool                       attached = true;
    std::uint64_t              drops    = 0;
    int                        acquires = 0;
    int                        releases = 0;
    std::vector<DeviceMessage> input;    // scripted: what the device sent, drained oldest first
    std::size_t               next = 0;  // how much of it a node has drained
    std::vector<Out>          outputs;
};

DeviceMessage message(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& bytes) {
    DeviceMessage m;
    m.size = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(bytes.size());
    std::copy(bytes.begin(), bytes.end(), m.data);
    return m;
}

using rp::host::test::DocExtras;
using rp::host::test::docNode;
using rp::host::test::graphRequest;
using rp::host::test::stereoDocument;

// A document holding the probe beside the host's stereo pair, and nothing else.
Engine::GraphRequest probeDocument() {
    return graphRequest(stereoDocument({}, DocExtras{{docNode("probe", DeviceProbe::id)}, {}}), {});
}

// The same document without the probe, so publishing it reclaims the plan that held the node.
Engine::GraphRequest noProbeDocument() {
    return graphRequest(stereoDocument({}, DocExtras{{docNode("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in")}, {}}), {});
}

// One block of the engine's stereo pair, into buffers the caller owns: a counted case sizes them before it starts
// counting, so the block's own output is not what it measures.
void block(Engine& e, std::vector<float>& l, std::vector<float>& r) {
    l.assign(kFrames, 0.0f);
    r.assign(kFrames, 0.0f);
    float* outs[2] = {l.data(), r.data()};
    e.processBlock(kFrames, outs, 2);
}

void block(Engine& e) {
    std::vector<float> l(kFrames), r(kFrames);
    block(e, l, r);
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("a node's cart pushes reach the installed cart link in order, at their frames and flush", "[devices]") {
    script = ProbeScript{};  // one case at a time: nothing a case scripted reaches the next
    FakeCartLink cart;
    Engine       e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(deviceProbePackage()));
    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, nullptr);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);

    script.cart = {{0, {0x90, 0x40, 0x7F}, false},
                   {5, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x01, 0xF7}, true},
                   {63, {0x80, 0x40, 0x00}, false}};
    block(e);
    script.cart.clear();

    // The node's own LED traffic went to the surface name, which this host has no link for: nothing reached the cart
    // but the three pushes, in order, each carrying the frame the block gave it and its flush flag.
    REQUIRE(cart.pushes.size() == 3);
    CHECK(cart.pushes[0].frame == 0);
    CHECK(cart.pushes[0].flush == false);
    CHECK(std::vector<std::uint8_t>(cart.pushes[0].data, cart.pushes[0].data + cart.pushes[0].size) ==
          std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x90, 0x40, 0x7F});
    CHECK(cart.pushes[1].frame == 5);
    CHECK(cart.pushes[1].flush == true);
    CHECK(std::vector<std::uint8_t>(cart.pushes[1].data, cart.pushes[1].data + cart.pushes[1].size) ==
          std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0xF0, 0x7D, 0x01, 0xF7});
    CHECK(cart.pushes[2].frame == 63);
    CHECK(std::vector<std::uint8_t>(cart.pushes[2].data, cart.pushes[2].data + cart.pushes[2].size) ==
          std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x80, 0x40, 0x00});
    // The rate the push's timing is computed at is the block's: the node takes it from the transport, not from its
    // settings.
    CHECK(cart.pushes[0].sampleRate == kRate);
    CHECK(script.rate == kRate);
}

TEST_CASE("the surface link's scripted input arrives in order, and its output is recorded", "[devices]") {
    script = ProbeScript{};  // one case at a time: nothing a case scripted reaches the next
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    surface.input = {message({0x90, 0x51, 0x7F}), message({0x90, 0x51, 0x00})};
    Engine e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(deviceProbePackage()));
    e.setDeviceLinks(nullptr, &surface);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);

    block(e);
    REQUIRE(script.drainedCount == 2);
    CHECK(script.drained[0].size == 3);
    CHECK(std::vector<std::uint8_t>(script.drained[0].data, script.drained[0].data + script.drained[0].size) ==
          std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x90, 0x51, 0x7F});
    CHECK(script.drained[1].size == 3);
    CHECK(std::vector<std::uint8_t>(script.drained[1].data, script.drained[1].data + script.drained[1].size) ==
          std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x90, 0x51, 0x00});

    // What the node pushed at the device, recorded as it queued it.
    REQUIRE(surface.outputs.size() == 1);
    CHECK(surface.outputs[0].size == sizeof kSurfaceOut);
    CHECK(std::vector<std::uint8_t>(surface.outputs[0].data,
                                    surface.outputs[0].data + surface.outputs[0].size) ==
          std::vector<std::uint8_t>(std::begin(kSurfaceOut), std::end(kSurfaceOut)));

    // Drained once, delivered once: the next block has nothing to take.
    block(e);
    CHECK(script.drainedCount == 0);
    CHECK(surface.outputs.size() == 2);  // the node pushes its LED frame every block, whatever the device sent
}

TEST_CASE("a link whose device goes away reads disconnected and counts what the node pushes", "[devices]") {
    script = ProbeScript{};  // one case at a time: nothing a case scripted reaches the next
    FakeCartLink    cart;
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    Engine          e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(deviceProbePackage()));
    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, &surface);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);

    script.cart = {{0, {0x90, 0x40, 0x7F}, false}, {7, {0x80, 0x40, 0x00}, false}};
    block(e);
    REQUIRE(cart.pushes.size() == 2);

    // Nothing edits the graph when the cart goes: the link says so and swallows the node's pushes, which the node reads
    // back as its device's drop count.
    cart.attached    = false;
    surface.attached = false;
    REQUIRE_FALSE(cart.connected());
    REQUIRE_FALSE(surface.connected());
    block(e);
    CHECK(cart.pushes.size() == 2);
    CHECK(cart.drops == 2);
    CHECK(script.cartDropped == 2);
    CHECK(surface.drops == 1);         // the node's LED frame, which the link dropped
    CHECK(surface.outputs.size() == 1);
}

TEST_CASE("a host with no device still plans and runs the node, whose pushes go nowhere and are counted", "[devices]") {
    script = ProbeScript{};  // one case at a time: nothing a case scripted reaches the next
    // No setDeviceLinks at all, as in the CLI, the Node addon, the render host and the UI harness: the names answer
    // with a handle that is never connected, never null, so the node needs no null check and this document is the same
    // one every host plans.
    Engine e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(deviceProbePackage()));
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);

    script.cart = {{0, {0x90, 0x40, 0x7F}, false}, {7, {0x80, 0x40, 0x00}, false}};
    block(e);
    block(e);
    script.cart.clear();

    CHECK(e.faultCount() == 0);
    CHECK(script.rate == kRate);  // the node ran: its block reached the device links it holds
    CHECK(script.drainedCount == 0);
    // A never-connected handle accepts every push and counts it as dropped, which is the count a node reads off its
    // device: two blocks, two pushes each.
    CHECK(script.cartDropped == 4);
}

TEST_CASE("acquire and release balance across a plan that keeps the node and one that removes it", "[devices]") {
    script = ProbeScript{};  // one case at a time: nothing a case scripted reaches the next
    FakeCartLink    cart;
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    Engine          e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(deviceProbePackage()));
    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, &surface);

    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);
    CHECK(cart.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(cart.releases == 0);
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 0);

    // A replace that keeps the node: the plan is republished with the same document, and the node runs on with the
    // handles it acquired, so nothing is acquired or released again. Both are counted: a destroy-then-recreate would
    // also leave one holder, and would show up here as two of each.
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);
    block(e);
    CHECK(cart.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(cart.releases == 0);
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 0);

    // A removal: the plan that held the node is reclaimed, and its destructor gives both handles back.
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(noProbeDocument()).ok);
    CHECK(cart.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(cart.releases == 1);
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 1);

    // And a node added back takes both again.
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);
    CHECK(cart.acquires == 2);
    CHECK(cart.releases == 1);
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 2);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 1);
}

TEST_CASE("a reactivate keeps the handles a node already holds, and destroy still releases once", "[devices]") {
    script = ProbeScript{};  // one case at a time: nothing a case scripted reaches the next
    FakeCartLink    cart;
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    Engine          e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(deviceProbePackage()));
    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, &surface);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);
    REQUIRE(cart.acquires == 1);
    REQUIRE(surface.acquires == 1);

    // A sample-rate change deactivates and activates every instance again (GraphHost::reactivate, which is also what
    // a block growth goes through). The node keeps the handles it holds, so neither link is acquired a second time.
    e.setSampleRate(44100.0);
    CHECK(cart.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(cart.releases == 0);
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 0);

    // A block growth is the other reactivate path.
    e.setMaxBlockFrames(Engine::kDefaultMaxBlockFrames + 1);
    CHECK(cart.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(cart.releases == 0);
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 0);

    // The node still runs on those handles, at the new rate.
    block(e);
    CHECK(script.rate == 44100.0);
    REQUIRE(cart.pushes.size() == 0);

    // And removing it releases each exactly once.
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(noProbeDocument()).ok);
    CHECK(cart.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(cart.releases == 1);
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 1);
}

TEST_CASE("a cart push carries the block's rate, not a fixed one", "[devices]") {
    script = ProbeScript{};  // one case at a time: nothing a case scripted reaches the next
    FakeCartLink cart;
    Engine       e(44100.0);
    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(deviceProbePackage()));
    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, nullptr);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);

    script.cart = {{3, {0x90, 0x40, 0x7F}, false}};
    block(e);
    REQUIRE(cart.pushes.size() == 1);
    CHECK(cart.pushes[0].sampleRate == 44100.0);
    CHECK(script.rate == 44100.0);
}

TEST_CASE("a device name this host has no link for answers with a never-connected handle", "[devices]") {
    script = ProbeScript{};  // one case at a time: nothing a case scripted reaches the next
    // The host's cart is named "n8" (kCartDeviceName); the node asks for another name, so it gets the registry's
    // never-connected fallback and the installed link is never touched. One behaviour for a typo and for a device the
    // host does not own, so a node needs no null check and a document plans wherever it runs.
    FakeCartLink    cart;
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    Engine          e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(deviceProbePackage()));
    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, &surface);
    script.cartName = "nes";
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);

    CHECK(cart.acquires == 0);  // the installed cart was not handed out
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 1);  // the surface's name was right

    script.cart = {{0, {0x90, 0x40, 0x7F}, false}};
    block(e);
    CHECK(cart.pushes.empty());
    CHECK(script.cartDropped == 1);  // the fallback counted the push it took nowhere
    CHECK(e.faultCount() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a release after the host clears its links reaches nothing and is harmless", "[devices]") {
    script = ProbeScript{};  // one case at a time: nothing a case scripted reaches the next
    FakeCartLink    cart;
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    Engine          e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(deviceProbePackage()));
    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, &surface);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);
    REQUIRE(cart.acquires == 1);

    // A host taking its links back before the objects they wrap go: the plans still alive hand their handles to a
    // registry that no longer names either link, so nothing is forwarded to a link that could already be gone.
    e.setDeviceLinks(nullptr, nullptr);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(noProbeDocument()).ok);
    CHECK(cart.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(cart.releases == 0);
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 1);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a host's teardown destroys its plans while the links are still alive", "[devices]") {
    script = ProbeScript{};  // one case at a time: nothing a case scripted reaches the next
    FakeCartLink    cart;
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    Engine          e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(deviceProbePackage()));
    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, &surface);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);
    REQUIRE(cart.acquires == 1);

    // What a host that owns both links does in its destructor body, before its device members go: reclaim the plan, so
    // every node's destroy runs while the link it borrowed is still alive (it reads the cart's count there).
    e.clearGraph();
    CHECK(script.destroyed);
    CHECK(script.droppedAtDestroy == 0);
    CHECK(cart.releases == 1);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 1);

    // Only then do the links leave the registry, and a later release nothing is left to reach.
    e.setDeviceLinks(nullptr, nullptr);
    CHECK(cart.releases == 1);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 1);
}

TEST_CASE("a warmed block touching both device links allocates and frees nothing", "[devices]") {
    script = ProbeScript{};  // one case at a time: nothing a case scripted reaches the next
    FakeCartLink    cart;
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    Engine          e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(deviceProbePackage()));
    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, &surface);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(probeDocument()).ok);

    // One block first, so every plan-side buffer exists, then the script and the fakes' room for the block's work,
    // which a counted block must not grow.
    script.cart = {{0, {0x90, 0x40, 0x7F}, false}, {4, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x01, 0xF7}, true}};
    surface.input = {message({0x90, 0x51, 0x7F}), message({0x90, 0x51, 0x00})};
    block(e);
    cart.pushes.clear();
    cart.reserve(2);
    surface.outputs.clear();
    surface.reserve(0, 1);
    surface.next = 0;
    surface.input = {message({0x90, 0x51, 0x7F}), message({0x90, 0x51, 0x00})};

    std::vector<float> l(kFrames), r(kFrames);  // the block's own output, sized before the window
    rp::test::beginCountingAllocations();
    block(e, l, r);
    const auto counted = rp::test::endCountingAllocations();
    CHECK(counted.allocations == 0);
    CHECK(counted.frees == 0);
    CHECK(cart.pushes.size() == 2);
    CHECK(script.drainedCount == 2);
}
````

````cpp
// Guards the surface device link rp.host.devices/1 hands rp.launchpad.surface
// (host/launchpad/LaunchpadSurfaceLink.hpp), over a real LaunchpadLink and its fake IMidiPort: the device's messages
// drain into the caller's own slots, in order, once each; the ring's bound drops and counts rather than truncating (a
// message wider than a slot, and a full ring); and the LED traffic a node pushes is queued for the host's main loop
// exactly as LaunchpadLink queues it.
//
// The slots are the point: the block thread copies out of fixed storage and frees nothing, where the standalone's
// vector drain hands it a vector per message to destroy. No rtmidi, no MIDI system, no hardware.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <array>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "../graph/CountingAllocator.hpp"

#include "host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp"
#include "host/launchpad/LaunchpadLink.hpp"
#include "host/launchpad/LaunchpadSurfaceLink.hpp"

using retroplug::IMidiPort;
using retroplug::LaunchpadLink;
using retroplug::LaunchpadSurfaceLink;
using rp::host::DeviceMessage;
using rp::host::kMaxDeviceMessage;

namespace {

// What the fake port saw and the receiver the test fires, kept outside the port so it survives its destruction.
struct PortLog {
    std::vector<std::vector<std::uint8_t>> written;
    IMidiPort::Receiver                    receiver;
};

struct FakePort final : IMidiPort {
    explicit FakePort(PortLog& log) : log_(log) {}
    ~FakePort() override { log_.receiver = nullptr; }
    void send(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) override { log_.written.emplace_back(data, data + n); }
    PortLog& log_;
};

LaunchpadLink::PortFactory factoryFor(PortLog& log) {
    return [&log](const std::string&, const std::string&,
                  IMidiPort::Receiver receiver) -> std::unique_ptr<IMidiPort> {
        log.receiver = std::move(receiver);
        return std::make_unique<FakePort>(log);
    };
}

std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytesOf(const DeviceMessage& m) { return {m.data, m.data + m.size}; }

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("LaunchpadSurfaceLink: the device's messages drain into the caller's slots, in order, once each",
          "[launchpad]") {
    PortLog       log;
    LaunchpadLink link(factoryFor(log));
    REQUIRE(link.connect("in", "out"));
    LaunchpadSurfaceLink surface(link);
    REQUIRE(surface.connected());
    REQUIRE(log.receiver);

    const std::uint8_t pad[3]     = {0x90, 0x51, 0x7F};
    const std::uint8_t release[3] = {0x90, 0x51, 0x00};
    log.receiver(pad, sizeof pad);
    log.receiver(release, sizeof release);

    std::vector<DeviceMessage> out(4);
    REQUIRE(surface.drainInput(out.data(), out.size()) == 2);
    CHECK(bytesOf(out[0]) == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x90, 0x51, 0x7F});
    CHECK(bytesOf(out[1]) == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x90, 0x51, 0x00});
    CHECK(surface.drainInput(out.data(), out.size()) == 0);  // drained once, delivered once
}

TEST_CASE("LaunchpadSurfaceLink: a drain with room for fewer messages leaves the rest queued", "[launchpad]") {
    PortLog       log;
    LaunchpadLink link(factoryFor(log));
    REQUIRE(link.connect("in", "out"));
    LaunchpadSurfaceLink surface(link);

    for (std::uint8_t i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        const std::uint8_t m[2] = {0x90, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0x10 + i)};
        log.receiver(m, sizeof m);
    }
    DeviceMessage out[2];
    REQUIRE(surface.drainInput(out, 2) == 2);
    CHECK(bytesOf(out[0]) == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x90, 0x10});
    CHECK(bytesOf(out[1]) == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x90, 0x11});
    REQUIRE(surface.drainInput(out, 2) == 1);
    CHECK(bytesOf(out[0]) == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x90, 0x12});
}

TEST_CASE("LaunchpadSurfaceLink: a message wider than a slot is dropped and counted, never truncated", "[launchpad]") {
    PortLog       log;
    LaunchpadLink link(factoryFor(log));
    REQUIRE(link.connect("in", "out"));
    LaunchpadSurfaceLink surface(link);

    // One byte past the bound: a device cannot produce one (its own replies are short), so it is a fault upstream, and
    // a truncated message would be worse than a lost one.
    const std::vector<std::uint8_t> huge(kMaxDeviceMessage + 1, 0x7F);
    log.receiver(huge.data(), huge.size());
    DeviceMessage out[1];
    CHECK(surface.drainInput(out, 1) == 0);
    CHECK(link.messagesDropped() == 1);

    // The exact bound still fits, in a slot of its own.
    const std::vector<std::uint8_t> big(kMaxDeviceMessage, 0x7F);
    log.receiver(big.data(), big.size());
    REQUIRE(surface.drainInput(out, 1) == 1);
    CHECK(out[0].size == kMaxDeviceMessage);
    CHECK(link.messagesDropped() == 1);
}

TEST_CASE("LaunchpadSurfaceLink: a full ring drops and counts what the device sent", "[launchpad]") {
    PortLog       log;
    LaunchpadLink link(factoryFor(log));
    REQUIRE(link.connect("in", "out"));
    LaunchpadSurfaceLink surface(link);

    // The ring holds LaunchpadLink's capacity less its one free slot: every message past that is dropped, not queued.
    constexpr std::size_t kSlots = 256;
    constexpr std::size_t kHeld  = kSlots - 1;
    const std::uint8_t    m[2]   = {0x90, 0x51};
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kSlots + 8; ++i) log.receiver(m, sizeof m);
    CHECK(link.messagesDropped() == kSlots + 8 - kHeld);

    // And what did fit comes out whole, oldest first.
    std::vector<DeviceMessage> out(kSlots);
    CHECK(surface.drainInput(out.data(), out.size()) == kHeld);
    CHECK(surface.drainInput(out.data(), out.size()) == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("LaunchpadSurfaceLink: a block thread's drain allocates and frees nothing", "[launchpad]") {
    PortLog       log;
    LaunchpadLink link(factoryFor(log));
    REQUIRE(link.connect("in", "out"));
    LaunchpadSurfaceLink surface(link);
    REQUIRE(log.receiver);

    const std::uint8_t pad[3] = {0x90, 0x51, 0x7F};
    // One warm drain first, so a counted one is the steady state: the messages stay in the link's slots until copied.
    log.receiver(pad, sizeof pad);
    std::array<DeviceMessage, 4> out{};
    REQUIRE(surface.drainInput(out.data(), out.size()) == 1);

    log.receiver(pad, sizeof pad);
    log.receiver(pad, sizeof pad);
    rp::test::beginCountingAllocations();
    const std::size_t n = surface.drainInput(out.data(), out.size());
    const auto        counted = rp::test::endCountingAllocations();
    CHECK(n == 2);
    CHECK(counted.allocations == 0);
    CHECK(counted.frees == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("LaunchpadSurfaceLink: the output a node pushes is queued for the host's main loop", "[launchpad]") {
    PortLog       log;
    LaunchpadLink link(factoryFor(log));
    REQUIRE(link.connect("in", "out"));
    LaunchpadSurfaceLink surface(link);

    const std::uint8_t led[3] = {0x90, 0x51, 0x15};
    surface.pushOutput(led, sizeof led);
    CHECK(log.written.empty());  // the block thread only queues; the host's pump writes

    link.pump();
    REQUIRE(log.written.size() == 1);
    CHECK(log.written[0] == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x90, 0x51, 0x15});
    CHECK(link.messagesSent() == 1);
}
````

Create `packages/native/test/n8/N8CartLink.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// Guards the cart device link rp.host.devices/1 hands rp.n8.nes (host/n8/N8CartLink.hpp), over a real N8Host and its
// N8Link: a push reaches the cart as the FIFO bytes the timed scheduler writes, timed at the block's rate; a push
// with no cart loses its bytes and is counted; the expansion volume a node's param drives goes out through the link's
// control path and again on every connect; and the connected state is the link's own.
//
// The fake serial port answers the Edio handshake and records every byte, as N8Host.test.cpp's does: no `serial` lib,
// no hardware. The link's reliable-link probe is off (setLinkAllowed), so the wire holds only what a push and a control
// write put there.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdint>
#include <deque>
#include <filesystem>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#include "host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp"
#include "host/n8/Edio.hpp"  // ISerialPort
#include "host/n8/N8CartLink.hpp"
#include "host/n8/N8Host.hpp"

using retroplug::Edio;
using retroplug::ISerialPort;
using retroplug::N8CartLink;
using retroplug::N8Host;
using retroplug::N8Link;
using retroplug::N8PortDto;

namespace {

// What every fake port written to one device shares: the bytes that reached the wire, mutex-guarded because the link's
// serial thread writes them while the test reads.
struct FakeDevice {
    void append(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> l(mu_);
        written_.insert(written_.end(), data, data + n);
    }
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> wire() {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> l(mu_);
        return written_;
    }

private:
    std::mutex                mu_;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> written_;
};

// The handshake (CMD_STATUS -> 0xA500) so connect succeeds, then the config block the host reads to decide the volume.
struct FakePort : ISerialPort {
    explicit FakePort(FakeDevice& dev) : dev_(dev) {
        toRead = {0x00, 0xA5};
        for (int i = 0; i < Edio::SIZE_CFG; ++i) toRead.push_back(0);  // map_idx 0: no expansion audio
    }
    std::size_t write(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) override {
        dev_.append(data, n);
        return n;
    }
    std::size_t read(std::uint8_t* b, std::size_t n, int) override {
        std::size_t i = 0;
        while (i < n && !toRead.empty()) { b[i++] = toRead.front(); toRead.pop_front(); }
        return i;
    }
    void flushInput() override {}

    std::deque<std::uint8_t> toRead;

private:
    FakeDevice& dev_;
};

N8Link::PortFactory factoryFor(FakeDevice& dev) {
    return [&dev](const std::string&) -> std::unique_ptr<ISerialPort> { return std::make_unique<FakePort>(dev); };
}

N8Host::PortLister noPorts() {
    return [] { return std::vector<N8PortDto>{}; };
}

std::string tempCfgDir() {
    const auto dir = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / "rp-n8-cart-link-test";
    std::filesystem::create_directories(dir);
    std::filesystem::remove(dir / "n8.cfg");  // start clean
    return dir.string();
}

// The 14 bytes an Edio one-byte memWR to `addr` puts on the wire, rebuilt from the protocol rather than hardcoded.
std::vector<std::uint8_t> memWrFrame(std::int32_t addr, std::uint8_t value) {
    const auto le32 = [](std::uint32_t v, std::vector<std::uint8_t>& out) {
        for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) out.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> (8 * i)));
    };
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> f{'+', static_cast<std::uint8_t>('+' ^ 0xFF), Edio::CMD_MEM_WR,
                                static_cast<std::uint8_t>(Edio::CMD_MEM_WR ^ 0xFF)};
    le32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(addr), f);
    le32(1, f);
    f.push_back(0);  // exec flag
    f.push_back(value);
    return f;
}

// The values written to the expansion-volume register, in wire order.
std::vector<int> expVolWrites(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& wire) {
    const auto full   = memWrFrame(Edio::ADDR_EXP_VOL, 0);
    const auto prefix = std::vector<std::uint8_t>(full.begin(), full.end() - 1);
    std::vector<int> values;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i + full.size() <= wire.size(); ++i)
        if (std::equal(prefix.begin(), prefix.end(), wire.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(i)))
            values.push_back(wire[i + full.size() - 1]);
    return values;
}

// Wait for the wire to hold `n` bytes: the serial thread writes each chunk at its scheduled moment, so a test reads
// after the block it pushed in rather than during it.
bool waitForBytes(FakeDevice& dev, std::size_t n) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) {
        if (dev.wire().size() >= n) return true;
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
    }
    return false;
}

bool waitForExpVolWrites(FakeDevice& dev, std::size_t n) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) {
        if (expVolWrites(dev.wire()).size() >= n) return true;
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
    }
    return false;
}

bool waitForExpVolValue(FakeDevice& dev, int value) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) {
        const auto values = expVolWrites(dev.wire());
        if (!values.empty() && values.back() == value) return true;
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
    }
    return false;
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("N8CartLink: a push reaches the cart as FIFO writes, timed at the block's rate", "[n8]") {
    FakeDevice dev;
    N8Host     host(factoryFor(dev), noPorts(), tempCfgDir());
    host.link().setLinkAllowed(false);  // no probe: the wire below is the pushes alone
    REQUIRE(host.link().connect("fake"));
    N8CartLink link(host);
    REQUIRE(link.connected());
    const std::size_t base = dev.wire().size();  // what connect put there: the pushes are the tail

    // Two one-byte pushes, the second 1 ms into the block at 48 kHz: the link's scheduler releases each at its offset,
    // so both are on the wire once the later one is due.
    const std::uint8_t first[1]  = {0x90};
    const std::uint8_t second[1] = {0x80};
    link.push(0, first, 1, false, 48000.0);
    link.push(48, second, 1, true, 48000.0);

    const auto firstFrame  = memWrFrame(Edio::ADDR_FIFO, 0x90);
    const auto secondFrame = memWrFrame(Edio::ADDR_FIFO, 0x80);
    REQUIRE(waitForBytes(dev, base + firstFrame.size() + secondFrame.size()));
    // The frames the pushes must put on the wire, after everything connect wrote (the status handshake, and the config
    // block the expansion volume's Auto reads off the running cart).
    const auto wire = dev.wire();
    REQUIRE(wire.size() == base + firstFrame.size() + secondFrame.size());
    CHECK(std::equal(firstFrame.begin(), firstFrame.end(), wire.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(base)));
    CHECK(std::equal(secondFrame.begin(), secondFrame.end(),
                     wire.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(base + firstFrame.size())));
    // `flush` is not a byte on the wire: on the physical side the arm byte is the barrier the emulated flag stands for.
    CHECK(link.dropped() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("N8CartLink: a push with no cart loses its bytes and says so", "[n8]") {
    FakeDevice dev;
    N8Host     host(factoryFor(dev), noPorts(), tempCfgDir());
    N8CartLink link(host);
    REQUIRE_FALSE(link.connected());

    const std::uint8_t bytes[3] = {0x90, 0x40, 0x7F};
    link.push(0, bytes, sizeof bytes, false, 48000.0);
    link.push(0, bytes, sizeof bytes, false, 48000.0);
    CHECK(link.dropped() == 2);
    CHECK(dev.wire().empty());
}

TEST_CASE("N8CartLink: the expansion volume goes out on a live link and again on every connect", "[n8]") {
    FakeDevice dev;
    N8Host     host(factoryFor(dev), noPorts(), tempCfgDir());
    host.link().setLinkAllowed(false);

    // Set before the link comes up: the connect path applies it, the way the project's knob reaches a cart plugged in
    // afterwards.
    N8CartLink link(host);
    link.setExpansionVolume(200);
    REQUIRE(host.link().connect("fake"));
    REQUIRE(waitForExpVolWrites(dev, 1));
    CHECK(expVolWrites(dev.wire()) == std::vector<int>{200});

    // Moved on a live link: posted through the serial thread, without tearing the stream down.
    link.setExpansionVolume(64);
    REQUIRE(waitForExpVolWrites(dev, 2));
    CHECK(expVolWrites(dev.wire()) == std::vector<int>{200, 64});

    // And a reconnect re-applies the standing value.
    host.link().disconnect();
    REQUIRE(host.link().connect("fake"));
    REQUIRE(waitForExpVolWrites(dev, 3));
    CHECK(expVolWrites(dev.wire()) == std::vector<int>{200, 64, 64});
}

TEST_CASE("N8CartLink: the expansion volume may be set from another thread while the link streams", "[n8]") {
    FakeDevice dev;
    N8Host     host(factoryFor(dev), noPorts(), tempCfgDir());
    host.link().setLinkAllowed(false);
    N8CartLink link(host);
    link.setExpansionVolume(64);  // an explicit standing value: this fake cart reports no expansion-audio mapper, so
                                  // Auto would write nothing and there would be no connect-time baseline below
    REQUIRE(host.link().connect("fake"));
    REQUIRE(waitForExpVolWrites(dev, 1));

    // The value is an atomic and a generation the serial thread consumes, so a knob on any thread (a node's param runs
    // on the block thread in stage 3) neither locks nor allocates here. Many changes from another thread, then a final
    // one: the serial thread must end on the final value, whatever it wrote on the way.
    std::thread writer([&link] {
        for (int v = 0; v < 64; ++v) link.setExpansionVolume(v);
        link.setExpansionVolume(200);
    });
    writer.join();
    REQUIRE(waitForExpVolValue(dev, 200));
    const auto values = expVolWrites(dev.wire());
    CHECK(values.back() == 200);
}

TEST_CASE("N8CartLink: a full ring loses and counts only the pushes it could not take", "[n8]") {
    FakeDevice dev;
    N8Host     host(factoryFor(dev), noPorts(), tempCfgDir());
    host.link().setLinkAllowed(false);
    REQUIRE(host.link().connect("fake"));
    N8CartLink link(host);

    // Every push is scheduled a second out, so the serial thread holds the first chunk and the ring fills behind it.
    // Each push the link refuses is counted by the adapter: a node reads the drops of ITS pushes, not every caller's
    // that shares the link.
    const std::uint8_t bytes[1] = {0x90};
    const auto         before   = link.dropped();
    for (int i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) link.push(48000, bytes, sizeof bytes, false, 48000.0);
    const auto after = link.dropped();
    REQUIRE(after > before);
    // The adapter counted exactly what the link would not take, and the link's own count is the same because nothing
    // else pushes at it here. The old paths pushing at the same N8Link (until stage 6) do not reach the adapter's.
    CHECK(after == host.link().pushesDropped());
}
````

- [ ] **Step 2: Add the interfaces, the registry and the engine's links**

`DeviceLinks.hpp` holds the two interfaces, their names, `kMaxDeviceMessage` = 560 (a 106-spec RGB bulk SysEx at five
bytes each plus the 8-byte frame is 538) and `DeviceMessage` with no arrival frame. `DeviceRegistry.hpp` is
header-only and control-thread only: it maps the two names to installed links, answers an unknown name with its own
never-connected `NoCart` / `NoSurface`, and forwards `acquire` / `release` only while the link it names is still
installed. `HostServices.hpp` gains the interface id and the four-pointer `HostDevices` struct. `Engine` gains
`setDeviceLinks`, `clearGraph` and `addNodePackage`, and its `Graph` holds the registry before the `GraphHost` so it
outlives every node's destroy.

Create `packages/native/src/host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The device links a node binds by name through rp.host.devices/1 (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md sections 3 to
// 5). The hosts own the devices - the serial port, the MIDI ports, reconnecting, the farewell - and a link is the whole
// of what a node may do with one: the streaming rings, the connected state and, for a cart, the expansion-audio
// register. The two interfaces live here, beside host/n8 and host/launchpad rather than inside either, because a node,
// a host's adapter and the tests all bind to them, and neither device's own headers are a node's business.
//
// The link outlives every plan whose nodes hold a handle: a host tears its plans down while its links are alive, and a
// reactivate keeps the handle across it. So a node may use its handle in destroy, not only give it back: a job it
// cancels, a queue it flushes, a connected() or dropped() it reads.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

namespace rp::host {

// What a node asks for. A host installs its link under the same name; a host that owns no such device answers with a
// link that is never connected, so a document plans and runs the same in every host (design section 3).
inline constexpr const char* kCartDeviceName    = "n8";
inline constexpr const char* kSurfaceDeviceName = "launchpad";

// The widest message one link carries in either direction: a bulk LED SysEx at its worst (the Pro MK3's 106 RGB colour
// specifications at five bytes each, plus the 8-byte frame, is 538). The device's own replies are far shorter; one
// bound serves both ways, and a message past it is dropped and counted, never truncated into something the other end
// would misread.
inline constexpr std::size_t kMaxDeviceMessage = 560;

// One message in storage the caller owns: a drain copies into the node's own array, so nothing the block thread drops
// is freed there. Also the slot a device link's own receive ring holds (LaunchpadLink's). There is no arrival frame:
// the device's traffic is not timed against the block, so a surface node places what it drains at frame 0, exactly as
// rp.host.controller-in places the host's staged pad traffic.
struct DeviceMessage {
    std::uint16_t size                     = 0;
    std::uint8_t  data[kMaxDeviceMessage] = {};
};

// A cart in a real console (rp.n8.nes): the same inputs an emulated NES takes, pushed at the cart's FIFO.
class CartLink {
public:
    virtual ~CartLink() = default;

    // [audio] Hand one message to the device at its intra-block `frame`, a sample offset `sampleRate` turns into the
    // moment the link releases it at. Lock-free, never allocates, never blocks; `flush` is the bytes port's barrier
    // flag, which the cart needs no separate byte for. A push while disconnected goes nowhere and is counted in
    // dropped().
    virtual void push(std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, bool flush,
                      double sampleRate) = 0;
    // [any] Whether the device is attached. Plain state, read afresh: a link may come up or go away between two reads.
    virtual bool connected() const = 0;
    // [any] The pushes that lost their bytes: the link was down, or the device's ring was full. An adapter counts its
    // own, so a node reads the pushes it made that went nowhere even while an old path pushes at the same device.
    virtual std::uint64_t dropped() const = 0;
    // [audio, any thread] The cart's expansion-audio master-volume register: 0..255, or -1 to leave the register to
    // the cart (N8Host::EXP_VOL_AUTO: unity for a mapper that carries the sound chip, otherwise whatever the device's
    // own menu set). The link keeps the value and a live one reaches the device through its own serial thread at that
    // thread's next turn, so a node's param may call this from the block (no lock, no allocation, no std::function on
    // the caller's side), and every connect re-applies the value.
    virtual void setExpansionVolume(int value) = 0;

    // There is deliberately no error string here: why a cart would not open is the host UI's (it reads N8Host's
    // lastError through Settings > N8), not something a document's node can act on.
    //
    // [control] A node took this handle, in its activate, and gave it back, in its destroy. The registry forwards
    // both, so a link that counts or acts on the nodes bound to it can; neither real adapter implements them. Acquire
    // runs more than once for one node when a sample-rate change or a block growth reactivates the plan
    // (GraphHost::reactivate), so a node that already holds its handles keeps them across deactivate / activate and
    // releases them once, in destroy: a link that arms or pauses something in acquire must see one release for one
    // acquire.
    virtual void acquire() {}
    virtual void release() {}
};

// A control surface (rp.launchpad.surface): the device's own MIDI in both directions, kept out of the musical stream.
class SurfaceLink {
public:
    virtual ~SurfaceLink() = default;

    // [audio] Copy the messages the device sent since the last drain into `out`, up to `capacity`, and answer how
    // many. Allocation-free and free-free: both ends keep every message in a fixed slot of their own, and one the
    // caller has no room for stays queued rather than being dropped or freed here.
    virtual std::size_t drainInput(DeviceMessage* out, std::size_t capacity) = 0;
    // [audio] Queue one message for the device (an LED frame, a mode change). Lock-free, never blocks; drops when
    // nothing is connected, the message is wider than kMaxDeviceMessage, or the ring is full.
    virtual void pushOutput(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) = 0;
    // [any] Whether the device is attached.
    virtual bool connected() const = 0;

    // As CartLink's: a node keeps a handle it holds across a reactivate, and releases it once in destroy.
    virtual void acquire() {}
    virtual void release() {}
};

}  // namespace rp::host
````

Create `packages/native/src/host/devices/DeviceRegistry.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The device links an engine's host installed, by the name a node asks for (rp.host.devices/1). An engine holds what
// its host gave it; a node holds a handle for the life of the plan it runs in. [control]: a host installs before the
// first graph, a node acquires in its activate and releases in its destroy, and both of those run on the control
// thread (a plan's reclaim included). A reactivate runs deactivate and activate again on one instance
// (GraphHost::reactivate, for a sample-rate change or a block growth), so a node that already holds a handle keeps it
// and does not acquire a second: the registry forwards each acquire a node makes, and the balance is the node's to
// keep. The links outlive every plan whose nodes hold a handle, so a node may use one in its destroy.

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string_view>

#include "host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp"

namespace rp::host {

class DeviceRegistry {
public:
    // [control] The links this host owns. Null installs nothing: that name then answers with a handle that is never
    // connected, as does every name this host has no link for, so a node needs no null check and a document plans the
    // same wherever it runs (design section 3).
    void install(CartLink* cart, SurfaceLink* surface) {
        cart_    = cart;
        surface_ = surface;
    }
    // [control] The host taking its links back, before the objects they are members of go. A node of a plan that is
    // still alive must have been destroyed already (Engine::clearGraph), or its release reaches nothing: the identity
    // check in release keeps that harmless, but a host tears its plans down first so a node may use its handle there.
    void clear() { install(nullptr, nullptr); }

    // [control] A handle for the device `name`, never null. `name` is a node's own string, so a C node's word for the
    // device has to be a link this host installed to get it.
    CartLink* acquireCart(std::string_view name) {
        CartLink* link = cart_ != nullptr && name == kCartDeviceName ? cart_ : &noneCart_;
        link->acquire();
        return link;
    }
    SurfaceLink* acquireSurface(std::string_view name) {
        SurfaceLink* link = surface_ != nullptr && name == kSurfaceDeviceName ? surface_ : &noneSurface_;
        link->acquire();
        return link;
    }
    // [control] A node is done with a handle it acquired here. The link is told only while it is still the installed
    // one: a host clears its links before the objects they wrap go, and the plans the engine frees afterwards hand
    // their handles back to a registry that no longer names them, so a release never reaches a freed link.
    void release(CartLink* link) {
        if (link != nullptr && link == cart_) link->release();
    }
    void release(SurfaceLink* link) {
        if (link != nullptr && link == surface_) link->release();
    }

private:
    // What a host that owns no cart answers with: never connected, taking every push nowhere and counting it (a node
    // reads that count as its device's drops), and an expansion volume it has nowhere to send.
    class NoCart final : public CartLink {
    public:
        void push(std::uint32_t, const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t size, bool, double) override {
            if (size != 0) dropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        }
        bool          connected() const override { return false; }
        std::uint64_t dropped() const override { return dropped_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }
        void          setExpansionVolume(int) override {}

    private:
        std::atomic<std::uint64_t> dropped_{0};
    };

    // And the same for a surface: nothing queued, nothing received.
    class NoSurface final : public SurfaceLink {
    public:
        std::size_t drainInput(DeviceMessage*, std::size_t) override { return 0; }
        void        pushOutput(const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t) override {}
        bool        connected() const override { return false; }
    };

    CartLink*    cart_    = nullptr;
    SurfaceLink* surface_ = nullptr;
    NoCart       noneCart_;
    NoSurface    noneSurface_;
};

}  // namespace rp::host
````

- [ ] **Step 3: Adapt the two transports, install the links in the hosts**

`N8CartLink` forwards a push, its drops, the expansion volume and the job seam to `N8Host`; `N8Link::push` returns
whether it took every chunk, and `pushesDropped()` is the adapter's own count. `LaunchpadLink`'s receive ring becomes
fixed `DeviceMessage` slots, its `drainInput` is the one drain, an oversized message is dropped and counted, and
`LaunchpadSurfaceLink` forwards the drain, the output queue and its drops. The plugin installs `N8CartLink` and no
surface (its DAW MIDI seam cannot carry SysEx); the SDL standalone installs both, before the control plane can publish
a graph, and both destructors call `clearGraph()` then `setDeviceLinks(nullptr, nullptr)`.

Create `packages/native/src/host/launchpad/LaunchpadSurfaceLink.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The surface device link rp.launchpad.surface binds through rp.host.devices/1, over a LaunchpadLink: the device's MIDI
// in both directions and its connected state. Opening and pairing the ports, the farewell the device needs before a
// host lets it go, and writing the queued LED traffic out on the main loop all stay the host's (LaunchpadHost and its
// pump). Header-only, as it is a few forwards over the link; the standalone is the only host that owns a Launchpad, and
// the only caller.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp"
#include "host/launchpad/LaunchpadLink.hpp"

namespace retroplug {

class LaunchpadSurfaceLink final : public rp::host::SurfaceLink {
public:
    explicit LaunchpadSurfaceLink(LaunchpadLink& link) : link_(link) {}

    // [audio] The messages the device sent since the last drain, copied straight out of the link's fixed slots: the
    // block thread allocates nothing and frees nothing, and a message the caller has no room for stays queued.
    std::size_t drainInput(rp::host::DeviceMessage* out, std::size_t capacity) override {
        return link_.drainInput(out, capacity);
    }
    void pushOutput(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) override { link_.pushOutput(data, size); }
    bool connected() const override { return link_.isConnected(); }

private:
    LaunchpadLink& link_;
};

}  // namespace retroplug
````

Create `packages/native/src/host/n8/N8CartLink.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The cart device link rp.n8.nes binds through rp.host.devices/1, over the N8Host a host already owns: the streaming
// ring, the connected state, the pushes it lost, and the expansion-audio master volume N8Host keeps for the project and
// re-applies on every connect. Nothing here opens the port or decides when the link comes up: that stays the host's
// (Settings > N8, the SD worker's pause and resume, the port being exclusive so one instance has it). Header-only, as
// it is a few forwards over what N8Host already does; the plugin and the standalone, which own the N8Host, are its
// only callers.

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp"
#include "host/n8/N8Host.hpp"

namespace retroplug {

class N8CartLink final : public rp::host::CartLink {
public:
    explicit N8CartLink(N8Host& host) : host_(host) {}

    // [audio] N8Link::push. `frame` is the intra-block sample offset and `sampleRate` the block's rate, which the link
    // turns into the moment it releases the bytes at, through its timed scheduler and lookahead. `flush` goes no
    // further: on the physical side the arm byte itself is the barrier the bytes port's flag stands for, so the link's
    // ring carries the barrier and no extra byte. A push the link did not take counts here, so the count a node reads
    // is the pushes IT lost: until the hosts' old paths go, they push at the same N8Link, and its own pushesDropped()
    // counts those too.
    void push(std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, bool flush,
              double sampleRate) override {
        (void)flush;
        if (!host_.link().push(frame, data, size, sampleRate))
            dropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    bool          connected() const override { return host_.link().isConnected(); }
    std::uint64_t dropped() const override { return dropped_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }

    // [audio, any thread] The cart's master-volume register: 0..255, or -1 to leave it to the cart
    // (N8Host::EXP_VOL_AUTO). N8Host keeps the value in an atomic and its serial thread writes it at its next turn
    // while streaming, without interrupting the stream, and applies it again inside every connect.
    void setExpansionVolume(int value) override { host_.setExpVol(value); }

private:
    N8Host&                    host_;
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t> dropped_{0};
};

}  // namespace retroplug
````

````bash
feat(host): rp.host.devices/1, the device links a node binds by name

The host keeps owning the devices; a node binds one by name through rp_host.get_interface
("rp.host.devices/1") and is handed a link for the life of its plan. A cart link ("n8") offers a push
at an intra-block frame with the block's rate, its connected state, the pushes it lost and the
expansion-audio register; a surface link ("launchpad") offers a drain into storage the caller owns,
which allocates and frees nothing on the block thread, a lock-free output queue and its connected
state. The two interfaces live in host/devices/, beside host/n8 and host/launchpad, because the
adapters, the nodes and the tests all bind to them.

The engine holds the links its host installs (Engine::setDeviceLinks) and answers every name,
including one no host owns, with a handle that is never connected and accepts and drops everything:
never null, so a node needs no null checks and a document plans and runs the same in every host. The
plugin installs the cart link over its N8Host and the SDL standalone installs both; the CLI, the Node
addon, the render host and the UI harness install none. Both hosts reclaim their plans first
(Engine::clearGraph), while every device member is alive, then uninstall the links: a link outlives
every plan whose node holds it, so a node may use its handle in destroy.

The expansion volume is an atomic and a generation the cart's serial thread consumes at its next turn,
so a node's param may set it from the block without a lock or an allocation, and every connect still
applies the standing value. Acquire is idempotent in the node: a reactivate (a sample-rate change, a
block growth) runs activate again on the same instance, and a handle already held is kept and released
once, in destroy.

The surface link needed LaunchpadLink's receive ring to stop handing the block thread std::vector
messages: the ring holds fixed slots of rp::host::DeviceMessage, the SDL host drains them into a fixed
array sized to the engine's controller-in capacity, and no vector drain is left to call. A message
wider than a slot is dropped and counted rather than truncated. N8Link::push reports whether it took
its bytes, so the cart adapter counts only its own lost pushes, not those of the old paths that share
the link.

Tests: test/engine-graph/Devices.test.cpp drives a probe node that acquires both links in activate,
pushes and drains in process and releases in destroy, on the real engine, over fakes that record and
count what a node does with them: order, frames, flush, a reactivate's balance, a non-default rate, an
unknown name, a release after the links are cleared, and a teardown that destroys the plan while the
links are alive, plus a warmed block that allocates and frees nothing. The adapter tests cover N8's
own drops and its full ring, the volume from another thread, and an allocation-counted drain of the
Launchpad ring. No audio path changes: strict parity is untouched, nothing re-recorded, and every
existing test case is unchanged.
EOF
````

### Task 2: memory, SRAM and ROM capabilities as asynchronous jobs

Design section 6 and section 8 item 2. The capability split on the emulated cores, and the job model the N8 node will
run its transfers on. `rp.system.memory/1` lists named regions and reads and writes them, `rp.system.sram/1` dumps and
restores the battery, and `rp.system.rom/1` answers the header bytes and the title; each is a nullable accessor on
`SystemBase`, like `channelTap()`, and all four consoles present them. A control thread submits a job through one engine
RPC and polls a completion queue; a read completes at once from the snapshot registry, a write at the block boundary
after it, and a job whose node, or core, left the plan fails rather than touching freed memory. At most 64 jobs are
outstanding, so every completion has room. The old system-id RPCs become thin wrappers over the same reads and writes.
TS gets `backend.capability`, `pumpJobs` and `rejectPendingJobs`; the UI pumps on the frame tick, a host running the
audio driver's thread pumps after each call that lets time pass, and a closed project rejects what is pending.

**Files:**
