````cpp
// The capability job model on the emulated cores (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 6): rp.system.memory/1,
// rp.system.sram/1 and rp.system.rom/1 through Engine::submitJob and Engine::drainJobs, held to what the system-id RPCs
// return for the same system (readRam, readSram, writeRam, and the ROM file's own prefix, which TS reads with
// readFilePrefix) bit for bit, on each console the suite builds (the GBA on its sibling fixture, which SKIPs, counted,
// when the resources tree is absent); a write that completes once the block after its drain has published it, and
// before submitJob returns while no audio thread runs; a job whose node leaves the plan, or that the engine discards,
// completing with an error; writes the audio thread's stop flushes, and writes a block that runs nothing leaves for the
// next; a full command ring; the job count's bound; every refusal; a job a device thread runs, reporting progress; and a
// warmed block with a write in flight that allocates and frees nothing.
//
// Run via `pnpm test:plugin engine-graph`, or `build/bin/retroplug-engine-graph-test "[capability]"`.

#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <optional>
#include <thread>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "../graph/CountingAllocator.hpp"
#include "GraphDocs.hpp"
#include "host/engine/CapabilityJobs.hpp"
#include "host/engine/DspCommand.hpp"
#include "host/engine/Engine.hpp"
#include "host/engine/EngineInvoker.hpp"
#include "host/rpc/EngineRpcService.hpp"
#include "system/SystemBase.hpp"

using rp::host::test::DocSystem;
using rp::host::test::readFile;

namespace {

constexpr double kRate = 48000.0;
const char* const kMemory = RP_SYSTEM_MEMORY_INTERFACE;
const char* const kSram = RP_SYSTEM_SRAM_INTERFACE;
const char* const kRom = RP_SYSTEM_ROM_INTERFACE;

std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytesOf(const rfl::Bytestring& b) {
    const auto* p = reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(b.data());
    return {p, p + b.size()};
}

std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytesOf(const std::string& s) { return {s.begin(), s.end()}; }

rfl::Bytestring bytestringOf(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& v) {
    const auto* p = reinterpret_cast<const std::byte*>(v.data());
    return rfl::Bytestring(p, p + v.size());
}

// An Engine with the system-id RPCs over it, as a host composes them, and the systems it places.
struct Rig {
    Engine                    e{kRate};
    QueuedInvoker             invoker{e};
    EngineRpcService          rpc{e, invoker};
    rp::host::test::Roms      roms;
    std::vector<float>        l = std::vector<float>(512), r = std::vector<float>(512);

    bool plan(std::vector<DocSystem> systems) {
        std::vector<SystemId> slots;
        for (const auto& s : systems) slots.push_back(s.id);
        rp::host::test::withRoms(e, systems, roms);
        return e.setGraph(rp::host::test::graphRequest(rp::host::test::stereoDocument(systems), slots)).ok;
    }
    void block(std::uint32_t frames = 512) {
        float* outs[2] = {l.data(), r.data()};
        e.processBlock(frames, outs, 2);
    }
    rp::host::JobSubmit submit(const std::string& node, const char* capability, const std::string& op,
                               std::string region = "", std::uint32_t offset = 0, std::uint32_t length = 0,
                               std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes = {}) {
        rp::host::JobRequest q;
        q.nodeId = node;
        q.capability = capability;
        q.op = op;
        q.region = std::move(region);
        q.offset = offset;
        q.length = length;
        q.bytes = std::move(bytes);
        return e.submitJob(std::move(q));
    }
    // The one completion of job `id` a drain hands back now, which must be there.
    rp::host::JobCompletion completion(std::uint32_t id) {
        auto all = e.drainJobs();
        REQUIRE(all.size() == 1);
        REQUIRE(all[0].id == id);
        REQUIRE(all[0].done);
        return std::move(all[0]);
    }
    // A job that completes at once, and the bytes it completed with.
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> now(const rp::host::JobSubmit& s) {
        INFO(s.error);
        REQUIRE(s.id != 0);
        auto c = completion(s.id);
        INFO(c.error);
        REQUIRE(c.ok);
        return std::move(c.bytes);
    }
};

// The bytes of a fixture the resources tree holds, or empty when it is not there (as CI runs).
std::vector<std::uint8_t> resourceFixture(const char* relative) {
    const char* root = std::getenv("RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR");
    if (!root) return {};
    return readFile((std::string(root) + relative).c_str());
}

// Every capability of system 1 against what the system-id RPCs answer for it, and against `rom`, the file it was built
// from. `title` is the ROM's title as its console's header stores it.
void checkAgainstTheRpcs(Rig& rig, const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& rom, const std::string& title) {
    for (int b = 0; b < 8; ++b) rig.block();
    const auto ram = rig.rpc.readRam(1);
    REQUIRE(ram);
    const auto wram = bytesOf(*ram);
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "regions")) ==
          bytesOf(R"([{"name":"ram","size":)" + std::to_string(wram.size()) + "}]"));
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram")) == wram);
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 16, 32)) ==
          std::vector<std::uint8_t>(wram.begin() + 16, wram.begin() + 48));
    if (const auto sram = rig.rpc.readSram(1)) {
        CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kSram, "dump")) == bytesOf(*sram));
    } else {
        const auto refused = rig.submit("sys-1", kSram, "dump");
        CHECK(refused.id == 0);
        CHECK(refused.error.find("publishes no battery") != std::string::npos);
    }
    // TS reads a header with readFilePrefix, a prefix of the file the resource was put from.
    for (const std::uint32_t length : {16u, 0x150u}) {
        INFO(length);
        CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kRom, "header", "", 0, length)) ==
              std::vector<std::uint8_t>(rom.begin(), rom.begin() + length));
    }
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kRom, "header")) == rom);
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kRom, "title")) == bytesOf(title));
    CHECK(rig.e.jobsOutstanding() == 0);
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("each capability answers what the system-id RPCs and the ROM file answer, on each console",
          "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    SECTION("Game Boy") {
        Rig rig;
        REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kGbType}}));
        const auto rom = readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH);
        std::string title;
        for (std::size_t i = 0x134; i < 0x144 && rom[i] != 0; ++i) title.push_back(static_cast<char>(rom[i]));
        REQUIRE(!title.empty());
        checkAgainstTheRpcs(rig, rom, title);
    }
    SECTION("NES") {
        Rig rig;
        REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kNesType}}));
        checkAgainstTheRpcs(rig, readFile(RP_BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PATH), "");
    }
    SECTION("Master System") {
        Rig rig;
        REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, "rp.mesen.sms"}}));
        checkAgainstTheRpcs(rig, readFile(RP_SMS_ROM_PATH), "");
    }
}

TEST_CASE("each capability answers what the system-id RPCs and the ROM file answer, on a GBA",
          "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    const auto rom = resourceFixture("/roms/nanoloop287d.gba");
    if (rom.empty()) SKIP("the GBA fixture ROM is absent from the resources tree");
    Rig rig;
    DocSystem gba{1, "rp.mesen.gba"};
    gba.rom = rig.e.putResource("rom", rom);
    REQUIRE(gba.rom != 0);
    REQUIRE(rig.plan({gba}));
    std::string title;
    // The game title field, $A0-$AB, which this homebrew cart leaves blank (as the ROM stores it, so empty).
    for (std::size_t i = 0xA0; i < 0xAC && rom[i] != 0; ++i) title.push_back(static_cast<char>(rom[i]));
    checkAgainstTheRpcs(rig, rom, title);
}

TEST_CASE("a write completes once the block after its drain has published it, and the next read sees it",
          "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kGbType}}));
    for (int b = 0; b < 4; ++b) rig.block();
    const std::vector<std::uint8_t> written = {0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef, 0x01, 0x23, 0x45, 0x67};
    const auto before = rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 0x40, 8));
    REQUIRE(before != written);
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);  // pushes queue for the block thread, which this thread is now
    const auto write = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0x40, 0, written);
    REQUIRE(write.id != 0);
    CHECK(rig.e.drainJobs().empty());  // in the ring
    rig.invoker.drainInto(rig.e);
    CHECK(rig.e.drainJobs().empty());  // applied, not yet published: a read now would see the old bytes
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 0x40, 8)) == before);
    rig.block();
    const auto done = rig.completion(write.id);
    CHECK(done.ok);
    CHECK(done.bytes.empty());
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 0x40, 8)) == written);
    // The system-id read agrees, at the same offset of the same region.
    const auto ram = bytesOf(*rig.rpc.readRam(1));
    CHECK(std::vector<std::uint8_t>(ram.begin() + 0x40, ram.begin() + 0x48) == written);
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
}

TEST_CASE("writes submitted while a real audio thread runs blocks complete, each visible to the read after it",
          "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    // A second thread drains and runs blocks as a host's audio thread does, while this one submits, polls and reads,
    // the old system-id write among them: what ThreadSanitizer holds the job records' hand-off to.
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kGbType}}));
    rig.block();
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    std::atomic<bool> stop{false};
    std::thread audio([&] {
        std::vector<float> l(256), r(256);
        float* outs[2] = {l.data(), r.data()};
        while (!stop.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
            rig.invoker.drainInto(rig.e);
            rig.e.processBlock(256, outs, 2);
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(200));
        }
    });
    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(20);
    for (std::uint8_t k = 1; k <= 16; ++k) {
        const std::vector<std::uint8_t> written = {k, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(k * 3), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(~k)};
        const auto write = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0x100 + k * 4, 0, written);
        REQUIRE(write.id != 0);
        CHECK(rig.invoker.writeRam(1, 0x200 + k, {k}));
        bool done = false;
        while (!done && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline) {
            for (const auto& c : rig.e.drainJobs())
                if (c.id == write.id && c.done) {
                    CHECK(c.ok);
                    done = true;
                }
            if (!done) std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(100));
        }
        REQUIRE(done);
        CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 0x100 + k * 4, 3)) == written);
    }
    stop.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
    audio.join();
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 0x201, 1)) == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{1});
    CHECK(rig.e.jobsOutstanding() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("while no audio thread runs, a write completes before submitJob returns, published for the next read",
          "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    // The CLI between renders: the push flushes inline and the engine republishes the region there and then.
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kNesType}}));
    rig.block();
    const std::vector<std::uint8_t> written = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    const auto write = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0x300, 0, written);
    REQUIRE(write.id != 0);
    CHECK(rig.completion(write.id).ok);
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 0x300, 5)) == written);
    // The system-id write takes the same path, landing on the core and queuing no completion.
    const std::vector<std::uint8_t> poked = {9, 8, 7};
    REQUIRE(rig.rpc.writeRam(1, 0x310, bytestringOf(poked)));
    auto live = rig.e.findSystem(1)->getMemory(rp::MemoryType::Ram, rp::AccessType::Read);
    CHECK(std::vector<std::uint8_t>(live.data() + 0x310, live.data() + 0x313) == poked);
    CHECK(rig.e.drainJobs().empty());
    CHECK(rig.e.jobsOutstanding() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a write whose node leaves the plan before it is published, or that the engine discards, completes with an "
          "error, touching no freed core",
          "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    Rig rig;
    const char* const gb = rp::host::test::kGbType;
    const std::vector<std::uint8_t> written = {0x5a, 0xa5};
    SECTION("the node removed") {
        REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, gb}, {2, gb}}));
        rig.block();
        rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
        const auto write = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0, 0, written);
        REQUIRE(write.id != 0);
        // Published behind the write, so the drain applies the write to system 1's core (alive: its plan is not yet
        // reclaimed) and then adopts the plan without it, which the block runs.
        REQUIRE(rig.plan({{2, gb}}));
        rig.invoker.drainInto(rig.e);
        rig.block();
        const auto c = rig.completion(write.id);
        CHECK_FALSE(c.ok);
        CHECK(c.error == "node sys-1 left the plan before the job completed");
        rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
        rig.e.reclaim();
        CHECK_FALSE(rig.e.coreLive(1));
    }
    SECTION("the plan replaced by one that rebuilds the system under a new id") {
        REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, gb}}));
        rig.block();
        rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
        const auto write = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0, 0, written);
        REQUIRE(write.id != 0);
        REQUIRE(rig.plan({{3, gb}}));  // a rebuild, as the stores make one: the same ROM under a fresh id
        rig.invoker.drainInto(rig.e);
        rig.block();
        CHECK(rig.completion(write.id).error == "node sys-1 left the plan before the job completed");
        rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    }
    SECTION("the plan replaced by one that keeps the node: the write completes") {
        REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, gb}}));
        rig.block();
        rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
        const auto write = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0, 0, written);
        REQUIRE(write.id != 0);
        REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, gb}, {2, gb}}));
        rig.invoker.drainInto(rig.e);
        rig.block();
        CHECK(rig.completion(write.id).ok);
        CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 0, 2)) == written);
        rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    }
    SECTION("discarded at teardown") {
        REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, gb}}));
        rig.block();
        rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
        const auto write = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0, 0, written);
        REQUIRE(write.id != 0);
        REQUIRE(rig.plan({{2, gb}}));
        rig.invoker.freePending();  // the audio thread stopped: the plan is adopted, the write dropped
        rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
        CHECK(rig.completion(write.id).error == "the engine stopped before the job ran");
    }
    CHECK(rig.e.jobsOutstanding() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("the jobs outstanding are bounded: a submission past the bound is refused until a drain makes room",
          "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kGbType}}));
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    // Reads completed and writes still in the ring count alike: each holds room for its completion.
    const auto write = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0, 0, {1});
    REQUIRE(write.id != 0);
    for (std::size_t k = 1; k < Engine::kMaxJobs; ++k) REQUIRE(rig.submit("sys-1", kRom, "title").id != 0);
    CHECK(rig.e.jobsOutstanding() == Engine::kMaxJobs);
    const auto refused = rig.submit("sys-1", kRom, "title");
    CHECK(refused.id == 0);
    CHECK(refused.error == "busy: 64 jobs are outstanding; drain their completions first");
    CHECK(rig.e.drainJobs().size() == Engine::kMaxJobs - 1);  // the write is still in the ring
    REQUIRE(rig.submit("sys-1", kRom, "title").id != 0);
    rig.invoker.drainInto(rig.e);
    rig.block();
    const auto rest = rig.e.drainJobs();
    REQUIRE(rest.size() == 2);
    CHECK(rest[0].done);
    CHECK(rest[1].done);
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    CHECK(rig.e.jobsOutstanding() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a submission is refused, at once and with the reason, for what it cannot do", "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kGbType}}));
    rig.block();
    const auto size = rig.e.ramSize(1);
    REQUIRE(size > 0);
    const auto refusal = [&](rp::host::JobSubmit s) {
        CHECK(s.id == 0);
        return s.error;
    };
    CHECK(refusal(rig.submit("sys-9", kMemory, "regions")) == "the running graph has no node sys-9");
    CHECK(refusal(rig.submit("out", kMemory, "regions")) == "node out presents no rp.system.memory/1");
    CHECK(refusal(rig.submit("split-1", kRom, "title")) == "node split-1 presents no rp.system.rom/1");
    CHECK(refusal(rig.submit("sys-1", "rp.system.video/1", "frame")) == "unknown capability rp.system.video/1");
    CHECK(refusal(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "erase")) == "rp.system.memory/1 has no operation 'erase'");
    CHECK(refusal(rig.submit("sys-1", kRom, "upload")) == "rp.system.rom/1 has no operation 'upload'");
    CHECK(refusal(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "vram")) == "node sys-1 has no memory region 'vram'");
    CHECK(refusal(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size), 0)) ==
          "the read runs past region ram (" + std::to_string(size) + " bytes)");
    CHECK(refusal(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0, 0, {})) == "an empty write");
    CHECK(refusal(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size) - 1, 0, {1, 2})) ==
          "the write runs past region ram (" + std::to_string(size) + " bytes)");
    CHECK(refusal(rig.submit("sys-1", kSram, "restore", "", 0, 0, {0})).find("restored by rebuilding it") !=
          std::string::npos);
    // A refusal takes no id and leaves no completion.
    CHECK(rig.e.drainJobs().empty());
    CHECK(rig.e.jobsOutstanding() == 0);
    // The ids count up from the last taken, refusals using none.
    const auto a = rig.submit("sys-1", kRom, "title");
    const auto b = rig.submit("sys-1", kRom, "title");
    CHECK(b.id == a.id + 1);
    CHECK(rig.e.drainJobs().size() == 2);
}

TEST_CASE("a warmed block with capability writes in flight allocates and frees nothing", "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    // The drain applies them (a job's and an old system-id one), the block runs and publishes, and the publish completes
    // the job's: the records and their bytes are the control thread's, made before the window and freed after it.
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kGbType}}));
    for (int b = 0; b < 4; ++b) rig.block(256);
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    const auto write = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0x20, 0, {1, 2, 3, 4});
    REQUIRE(write.id != 0);
    REQUIRE(rig.invoker.writeRam(1, 0x30, {5, 6, 7, 8}));
    rp::test::beginCountingAllocations();
    rig.invoker.drainInto(rig.e);
    rig.block(64);
    const auto counted = rp::test::endCountingAllocations();
    CHECK(counted.allocations == 0);
    CHECK(counted.frees == 0);
    CHECK(rig.completion(write.id).ok);
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 0x20, 4)) == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{1, 2, 3, 4});
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 0x30, 4)) == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{5, 6, 7, 8});
}

TEST_CASE("writes the audio thread's stop flushes complete at the next drain, published", "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    // Stopping the audio thread applies what is still queued on the stopping thread, with no block to publish it: the
    // next drain (or submission) republishes and finishes them, so neither waits for a render.
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kGbType}}));
    rig.block();
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    const auto a = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0x50, 0, {0x11, 0x22});
    const auto b = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0x60, 0, {0x33});
    REQUIRE(a.id != 0);
    REQUIRE(b.id != 0);
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    const auto done = rig.e.drainJobs();
    REQUIRE(done.size() == 2);
    CHECK(done[0].id == a.id);
    CHECK(done[1].id == b.id);
    CHECK(done[0].ok);
    CHECK(done[1].ok);
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 0x50, 2)) == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x11, 0x22});
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 0x60, 1)) == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x33});
}

TEST_CASE("a write a block that runs nothing leaves unpublished completes at the next block that runs",
          "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kGbType}}));
    rig.block();
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    const auto write = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0x70, 0, {0x44, 0x55});
    REQUIRE(write.id != 0);
    rig.invoker.drainInto(rig.e);
    rig.block(0);  // an empty block runs nothing, the publish included
    CHECK(rig.e.drainJobs().empty());
    // Longer than the plan's buffers: refused, silent, and nothing published.
    std::vector<float> l(Engine::kDefaultMaxBlockFrames + 1), r(Engine::kDefaultMaxBlockFrames + 1);
    float* outs[2] = {l.data(), r.data()};
    rig.e.processBlock(Engine::kDefaultMaxBlockFrames + 1, outs, 2);
    CHECK(rig.e.drainJobs().empty());
    rig.block();
    CHECK(rig.completion(write.id).ok);
    CHECK(rig.now(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "read", "ram", 0x70, 2)) == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0x44, 0x55});
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    rig.e.reclaim();  // reports the oversized block, once
}

TEST_CASE("a full command ring refuses a write, the job's and the system-id one alike", "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kGbType}}));
    rig.block();
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    DspCommand bpm;
    bpm.kind = DspCommand::Kind::SetBpm;
    bpm.setBpm = {120.0};
    std::size_t pushed = 0;
    while (rig.e.pushCommand(bpm)) ++pushed;
    CHECK(pushed > 0);
    CHECK(rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0, 0, {1}).error == "busy: the command ring is full");
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.invoker.writeRam(1, 0, {1}));
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.rpc.writeRam(1, 0, bytestringOf({1})));
    CHECK(rig.e.jobsOutstanding() == 0);  // a refused write keeps no record
    rig.invoker.drainInto(rig.e);
    const auto write = rig.submit("sys-1", kMemory, "write", "ram", 0, 0, {1});
    CHECK(write.id != 0);
    rig.invoker.drainInto(rig.e);
    rig.block();
    CHECK(rig.completion(write.id).ok);
    rig.invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
}

TEST_CASE("a job a device thread runs reports its progress once per change, then its result or its error",
          "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    // The engine plays its part of a device's job (CapabilityJobs.hpp) with this test as the device: a record adopted on
    // the control thread, written by another thread (progress, then the result or the error, then the final state, last
    // and with release), drained here. What ThreadSanitizer holds the device thread's hand-off to.
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kGbType}}));
    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(20);
    const auto run = [&](bool succeed) {
        auto job = std::make_unique<rp::host::Job>();
        rp::host::Job* record = job.get();
        record->total.store(4, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        const auto adopted = rig.e.adoptJob(std::move(job));
        REQUIRE(adopted.id != 0);
        std::atomic<std::uint32_t> acknowledged{0};
        std::thread device([&] {
            for (std::uint32_t k = 1; k <= 3; ++k) {
                record->progress.store(k, std::memory_order_release);
                while (acknowledged.load(std::memory_order_acquire) < k) std::this_thread::yield();
            }
            if (succeed) {
                record->result = {0xca, 0xfe};
                record->progress.store(4, std::memory_order_relaxed);
                record->state.store(rp::host::Job::Done, std::memory_order_release);
            } else {
                record->error = "the cart did not answer";
                record->failure.store(rp::host::Job::Device, std::memory_order_relaxed);
                record->state.store(rp::host::Job::Failed, std::memory_order_release);
            }
        });
        std::vector<std::uint32_t> seen;
        std::optional<rp::host::JobCompletion> final;
        while (!final && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline) {
            for (auto& c : rig.e.drainJobs()) {
                CHECK(c.id == adopted.id);
                if (c.done) {
                    final = std::move(c);
                    continue;
                }
                CHECK(c.total == 4);
                seen.push_back(c.progress);
                // A second drain before the device moves on reports nothing: once per change. (The final progress is
                // stored just before the result, so a drain between the two reports it too; the device does not wait
                // for that one.)
                if (c.progress <= 3) CHECK(rig.e.drainJobs().empty());
                acknowledged.store(c.progress, std::memory_order_release);
            }
            std::this_thread::yield();
        }
        device.join();
        REQUIRE(final);
        const std::vector<std::uint32_t> steps = {1, 2, 3}, stepsAndLast = {1, 2, 3, 4};
        CHECK((seen == steps || (succeed && seen == stepsAndLast)));
        CHECK(final->ok == succeed);
        if (succeed) {
            CHECK(final->bytes == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{0xca, 0xfe});
            CHECK(final->progress == 4);
        } else {
            CHECK(final->error == "the cart did not answer");
        }
        CHECK(rig.e.jobsOutstanding() == 0);
    };
    SECTION("its result") { run(true); }
    SECTION("its error") { run(false); }
}

TEST_CASE("a node that is no system node presents no capability yet", "[engine-graph][capability]") {
    // The device seam (Engine::submitDeviceJob): the refusal a node whose type presents none of the interfaces gets.
    Rig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.plan({{1, rp::host::test::kGbType}}));
    for (const char* capability : {kMemory, kSram, kRom}) {
        const auto refused = rig.submit("split-1", capability, "dump");
        CHECK(refused.id == 0);
        CHECK(refused.error == std::string("node split-1 presents no ") + capability);
    }
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/capability.test.ts`:

````ts
// Capability jobs over the real host (src/capability.ts, docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 6): a running
// Master System answers backend.capability() with exactly what the system-id calls answer for it (readRam, readSram,
// and readFilePrefix on the ROM it was built from), and a write through it and one through writeRam land in the same
// region, each visible to the other's read. Rendering on the calling thread (no audio thread), every job completes at
// its submission; with the audio driver's thread running, a write completes at a block boundary, and the submission
// waits through the driver's native sleep until it does, since this host fires no timer and has no frame tick. The queue, the block-boundary completion and the threading are held by
// retroplug-engine-graph-test "[capability]".
import { test, expect, skip } from "../testing/harness";
import { createRealBackend } from "../src/realBackend";
import { createAudioDriver } from "../src/audioDriver";
import { directGraph } from "../src/graph/directGraph";

const graph = directGraph();

declare const __REPO_RESOURCES_DIR__: string;

const ROM = __REPO_RESOURCES_DIR__ + "/roms/smsggdj_v0_45.sms";

test("capability() and the system-id calls agree on a running system, reads and writes alike", async () => {
  const be = createRealBackend();
  if (!be.fileExists(ROM)) skip(`capability: missing ${ROM}`);
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  const id = 1;
  expect(
    graph.add(
      { romPath: ROM, platform: "sms", core: "mesen", embeddedRom: "", savPath: null, statePath: null, coreConfig: { enableFm: false } },
      id,
    ),
  ).toBeTruthy();
  audio.renderAudio(500);
  const node = `sys-${id}`;

  const ram = be.readRam(id)!;
  expect(await be.capability(node, "memory.regions")).toEqual([{ name: "ram", size: ram.length }]);
  expect(await be.capability(node, "memory.read", { region: "ram" })).toEqual(ram);
  expect(await be.capability(node, "sram.dump")).toEqual(be.readSram(id)!);
  expect(await be.capability(node, "rom.header", { length: 0x8200 })).toEqual(be.readFilePrefix(ROM, 0x8200)!);
  expect(await be.capability(node, "rom.title")).toBe(""); // a Sega header has no title field

  // A write through the job lands where readRam reads, at once on this host; one through writeRam lands where the job
  // reads, at the next block as it always has.
  const offset = 0x1f00;
  expect(await be.capability(node, "memory.write", { region: "ram", offset, bytes: Uint8Array.from([0xde, 0xad]) })).toBe(undefined);
  expect(be.readRam(id)!.slice(offset, offset + 2)).toEqual(Uint8Array.from([0xde, 0xad]));
  expect(be.writeRam(id, offset + 2, Uint8Array.from([0xbe, 0xef]))).toBeTruthy();
  audio.renderAudio(20);
  expect(await be.capability(node, "memory.read", { region: "ram", offset, length: 4 })).toEqual(Uint8Array.from([0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef]));

  let refusal = "";
  await be.capability(node, "sram.restore", { bytes: new Uint8Array(1) }).catch((e: Error) => (refusal = e.message));
  expect(refusal.includes("restored by rebuilding it")).toBe(true);
  expect(be.pumpJobs()).toBe(0);
  expect(graph.remove(id)).toBeTruthy();
});

test("with the audio thread running, capability() settles a write with no timer and no frame tick", async () => {
  const be = createRealBackend();
  if (!be.fileExists(ROM)) skip(`capability: missing ${ROM}`);
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  const id = 2;
  expect(
    graph.add(
      { romPath: ROM, platform: "sms", core: "mesen", embeddedRom: "", savPath: null, statePath: null, coreConfig: { enableFm: false } },
      id,
    ),
  ).toBeTruthy();
  audio.renderAudio(200);
  expect(audio.startAudio()).toBeTruthy();
  const node = `sys-${id}`;
  const offset = 0x1f10;
  // Held without awaiting first: a promise that never settled would hang an await, so its settling is checked after
  // two microtask turns, which is all a settled promise needs (the submission waited for the block itself).
  let state = "pending";
  const write = be.capability(node, "memory.write", { region: "ram", offset, bytes: Uint8Array.from([0x12, 0x34]) });
  write.then(() => (state = "resolved"), (e: Error) => (state = `rejected: ${e.message}`));
  await Promise.resolve();
  await Promise.resolve();
  expect(state).toBe("resolved");
  expect(await be.capability(node, "memory.read", { region: "ram", offset, length: 2 })).toEqual(Uint8Array.from([0x12, 0x34]));
  expect(audio.stopAudio()).toBeTruthy();
  expect(be.pumpJobs()).toBe(0);
  expect(graph.remove(id)).toBeTruthy();
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/capability/capability.test.ts`:

````ts
// Capability jobs as promises (src/capability.ts, docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 6), over the mock
// backend's model of the native job queue: a read resolves at its submission, a write while the audio thread runs once
// the block boundary has passed and the tick pumps, a refusal rejects at once with native's reason, a failed job
// rejects with its error, a long job's progress reaches its listener, and closing the project rejects what is still
// pending. The native half (the queue, the threading, the agreement with readRam / readSram) is held by
// retroplug-engine-graph-test "[capability]" and test-native/capability.
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";
import { MockBackend } from "../../testing/mockBackend";
import { ProjectStore } from "../../src/projectStore";
import { RecentStore } from "../../src/recentStore";
import { buildAppRegistry } from "../../src/appHost";
import { CapabilityJobs, pumpAllJobs, setJobWait, type JobCompletion, type JobRequest, type JobSubmitResult } from "../../src/capability";
import { gbRom } from "../systems/fixtures";

// The message `promise` rejects with, held to contain `text`; a promise that resolves fails the case.
async function rejectsWith(promise: Promise<unknown>, text: string): Promise<void> {
  let message: string | null = null;
  try {
    await promise;
  } catch (e) {
    message = (e as Error).message;
  }
  if (message === null) throw new Error(`expected a rejection containing "${text}", got a resolution`);
  expect(message.includes(text) ? text : message).toBe(text);
}

function cart() {
  const be = new MockBackend("/cfg");
  const project = new ProjectStore(be, new RecentStore(be), buildAppRegistry());
  const rom = gbRom();
  rom.set([0x52, 0x50, 0x54, 0x45, 0x53, 0x54], 0x134); // "RPTEST"
  be.seed("/roms/cart.gb", rom);
  const id = project.systems.addSystem("/roms/cart.gb")!;
  be.setRam(id, new Uint8Array(64).map((_, i) => i));
  return { be, project, id, node: `sys-${id}`, rom };
}

test("a read resolves at its submission, with what the system-id read returns", async () => {
  const { be, node, id, rom } = cart();
  expect(await be.capability(node, "memory.read", { region: "ram" })).toEqual(be.readRam(id)!);
  expect(await be.capability(node, "memory.read", { region: "ram", offset: 4, length: 3 })).toEqual(new Uint8Array([4, 5, 6]));
  expect(await be.capability(node, "memory.regions")).toEqual([{ name: "ram", size: 64 }]);
  expect(await be.capability(node, "sram.dump")).toEqual(be.readSram(id)!);
  expect(await be.capability(node, "rom.header", { length: 0x150 })).toEqual(rom.slice(0, 0x150));
  expect(await be.capability(node, "rom.title")).toBe("RPTEST");
  expect(be.pumpJobs()).toBe(0);
});

test("a write while the audio thread runs resolves once the block boundary has passed and the tick pumps", async () => {
  const { be, node, id } = cart();
  be.audioRunning = true;
  let settled = false;
  const write = be.capability(node, "memory.write", { region: "ram", offset: 8, bytes: new Uint8Array([0xaa, 0xbb]) });
  void write.then(() => (settled = true));
  await Promise.resolve();
  expect(settled).toBe(false);
  expect(be.pumpJobs()).toBe(1); // nothing completed: the write is still in the ring
  be.runBlock();
  expect(be.pumpJobs()).toBe(0);
  expect(await write).toBe(undefined);
  expect(be.readRam(id)!.slice(8, 10)).toEqual(new Uint8Array([0xaa, 0xbb]));
});

test("a refused job rejects at once with native's reason", async () => {
  const { be, node } = cart();
  await rejectsWith(be.capability("sys-99", "memory.read", { region: "ram" }), "the running graph has no node sys-99");
  await rejectsWith(be.capability(node, "sram.restore", { bytes: new Uint8Array([1]) }), "restored by rebuilding it");
  await rejectsWith(be.capability(node, "memory.write", { region: "ram", offset: 63, bytes: new Uint8Array([1, 2]) }), "the write runs past region ram (64 bytes)");
  expect(be.pumpJobs()).toBe(0);
});

test("closing the project rejects what is still pending, and a late completion is dropped", async () => {
  const { be, project, node } = cart();
  be.audioRunning = true;
  const write = be.capability(node, "memory.write", { region: "ram", bytes: new Uint8Array([1]) });
  project.newProject();
  await rejectsWith(write, "the project closed");
  be.runBlock(); // the native job still completes; nobody is waiting for it
  expect(be.pumpJobs()).toBe(0);
});

test("a job that fails rejects with its error, and a long job's progress reaches its listener first", async () => {
  // A scripted port: what a device's job looks like from here (progress, then a completion).
  const queue: JobCompletion[] = [];
  const requests: JobRequest[] = [];
  const jobs = new CapabilityJobs({
    submitJob: (r: JobRequest): JobSubmitResult => {
      requests.push(r);
      return { id: requests.length };
    },
    drainJobs: () => queue.splice(0),
  });
  const seen: string[] = [];
  const dump = jobs.run("n8-1", "sram.dump", {}, (p) => seen.push(`${p.progress}/${p.total}`));
  const write = jobs.run("sys-1", "memory.write", { region: "ram", offset: 2, bytes: new Uint8Array([7]) });
  expect(requests).toEqual([
    { nodeId: "n8-1", capability: "rp.system.sram/1", op: "dump" },
    { nodeId: "sys-1", capability: "rp.system.memory/1", op: "write", region: "ram", offset: 2, bytes: new Uint8Array([7]) },
  ]);
  const empty = new Uint8Array(0);
  queue.push({ id: 1, done: false, ok: false, error: "", bytes: empty, progress: 4096, total: 65536 });
  queue.push({ id: 2, done: true, ok: false, error: "node sys-1 left the plan before the job completed", bytes: empty, progress: 0, total: 0 });
  expect(jobs.pump()).toBe(1);
  await rejectsWith(write, "node sys-1 left the plan before the job completed");
  queue.push({ id: 1, done: true, ok: true, error: "", bytes: new Uint8Array([9, 9]), progress: 65536, total: 65536 });
  expect(jobs.pump()).toBe(0);
  expect(await dump).toEqual(new Uint8Array([9, 9]));
  expect(seen).toEqual(["4096/65536"]);
  await rejectsWith(jobs.run("sys-1", "video.frame" as never), "unknown capability operation video.frame");
});

test("a close that leaves native's bound full of owed completions does not wedge the next capability()", async () => {
  const { be, project, node } = cart();
  be.audioRunning = true;
  const writes = Array.from({ length: 64 }, (_, k) => be.capability(node, "memory.write", { region: "ram", offset: k % 64, bytes: new Uint8Array([k]) }));
  await rejectsWith(be.capability(node, "rom.title"), "busy: 64 jobs are outstanding");
  project.newProject();
  for (const w of writes) await rejectsWith(w, "the project closed");
  be.runBlock(); // native finishes all 64; nobody is waiting for them, and they hold its bound
  const id = project.systems.addSystem("/roms/cart.gb")!;
  be.setRam(id, new Uint8Array(8));
  expect(await be.capability(`sys-${id}`, "memory.read", { region: "ram", length: 2 })).toEqual(new Uint8Array(2));
  expect(be.pumpJobs()).toBe(0);
});

test("a battery-less cart's dump refuses, and a console without a title field answers an empty one", async () => {
  const { be, node, id } = cart();
  be.setNoBattery(id);
  await rejectsWith(be.capability(node, "sram.dump"), `node ${node} publishes no battery`);
  const be2 = new MockBackend("/cfg");
  const project2 = new ProjectStore(be2, new RecentStore(be2), buildAppRegistry());
  be2.seed("/roms/cart.nes", new Uint8Array([0x4e, 0x45, 0x53, 0x1a, 2, 1, 0, 0, ...new Array(0x8000 + 0x2000).fill(0x41)]));
  const nes = project2.systems.addSystem("/roms/cart.nes");
  expect(nes).toBeTruthy();
  expect(await be2.capability(`sys-${nes}`, "rom.title")).toBe("");
});

test("with an audio thread no tick pumps for, a submission waits through the installed sleep until its job settles", async () => {
  // The CLI's case (src/audioDriver.ts installs the wait between startAudio and stopAudio): no timer, no frame tick.
  let blocks = 0;
  const queue: JobCompletion[] = [];
  const jobs = new CapabilityJobs({
    submitJob: (): JobSubmitResult => ({ id: 1 }),
    drainJobs: () => queue.splice(0),
  });
  setJobWait(() => {
    if (++blocks === 3) queue.push({ id: 1, done: true, ok: true, error: "", bytes: new Uint8Array([5]), progress: 0, total: 0 });
  });
  let settled: Uint8Array | null = null;
  try {
    void jobs.run("sys-1", "memory.read", { region: "ram" }).then((b) => (settled = b));
  } finally {
    setJobWait(null);
  }
  await Promise.resolve();
  await Promise.resolve();
  expect(blocks).toBe(3);
  expect(settled).toEqual(new Uint8Array([5]));
  // And with none installed the promise stays pending until a pump, which pumpAllJobs reaches.
  const later = jobs.run("sys-1", "memory.read", { region: "ram" });
  queue.push({ id: 1, done: true, ok: true, error: "", bytes: new Uint8Array([6]), progress: 0, total: 0 });
  pumpAllJobs();
  expect(await later).toEqual(new Uint8Array([6]));
});
````

- [ ] **Step 2: Add the capability interfaces and the job model**

`SystemCapabilities.hpp/.cpp` define `MemoryCapability`, `SramCapability` and `RomCapability`, and the three core
adapters: `CoreMemory` over `MemoryType::Ram`, `CoreSram` whose emulated restore is refused, and `CoreRom` over the
`rom_` vector each core keeps. `SystemBase` gains `memory()`, `sram()` and `rom()`, and each console returns its three
members. `CapabilityJobs.hpp` defines the interface ids, `JobRequest`, `JobSubmit`, `JobCompletion` and the `Job`
record with its state, failure, progress and result. `Engine::submitJob`, `drainJobs`, `jobsOutstanding`, the public
`writeRam`, `kMaxJobs` = 64 and the private `applyJob`, `confirmApplied`, `settleQuiescent` and `sweepJobs` land; the
`WriteRam` command becomes a non-owning `CapabilityWrite { Job* }`, and `SnapshotRegistry` gains `publishRam`. The
RPCs `submitJob` and `drainJobs` join the emulator facet and `writeRam` returns the invoker's answer.

Create `packages/native/src/host/engine/CapabilityJobs.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "system/SystemTypes.hpp"  // SystemId

class SystemBase;

// The capability job model (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 6): the control plane asks a node of the
// running graph to do something to the system behind it, a read, a write, a dump, and the answer comes later. Every
// job has the same life whoever answers it: Engine::submitJob takes it or refuses it at once, and its completion is
// collected by Engine::drainJobs, from a bounded queue the control plane polls. A job completes in one of three ways:
//
//   - at once, on the control thread: a read of an emulated system, served from the snapshot registry's published
//     copy, or a read of its ROM, which never changes. The completion is queued before submitJob returns.
//   - at a block boundary: a write to an emulated system rides the command ring, in push order with the plans, is
//     applied by the block thread at the drain that reaches it, and completes once the block after it has published the
//     region, so a read the control plane makes after the completion sees it. While no audio thread runs, the push
//     flushes inline and the engine republishes the region there and then, so the job's state is final before
//     submitJob returns (as a write is in the CLI between renders) and its completion is queued by the next drain.
//   - later, on another thread, with progress: a job a device runs on its own thread (an N8 cart's dump or upload,
//     seconds of USB transfers). The record below carries what that thread reports: its progress, then its result
//     bytes or its error, then the terminal state, stored last with release, which is what the control thread acquires
//     before it reads the rest.
//
// A job's record is the control thread's: made by submitJob (or adopted from a device's node, adoptJob), freed once its
// state is terminal by the next sweep (drainJobs, submitJob and Engine::writeRam each sweep first), or by the engine's
// destruction. Another thread only writes the record's state (and, a device thread, its progress, result and
// error), never frees it, and never touches it after storing a terminal state. So the block thread allocates and frees
// nothing for a job: a write's bytes are allocated on the control thread with the record and freed back on it.
//
// Two rules a device's jobs keep, beside the engine's own bound (Engine::kMaxJobs outstanding, engine-wide, the
// back-pressure that keeps room for every completion):
//
//   - One job at a time per device. The device's node refuses a second at submission ("busy"), and one while its device
//     is not attached ("not connected"), synchronously, before the engine adopts a record; the engine's bound does not
//     know about devices.
//   - Progress overwrites. A device thread stores its latest progress in the record, and drainJobs reports a running
//     job once per drain whose progress changed since the last, with the value it finds then: a job that reports in a
//     tight loop while nobody drains accumulates nothing, and its listener sees the latest value, not every step.

namespace rp::host {

#define RP_SYSTEM_MEMORY_INTERFACE "rp.system.memory/1"
#define RP_SYSTEM_SRAM_INTERFACE "rp.system.sram/1"
#define RP_SYSTEM_ROM_INTERFACE "rp.system.rom/1"

// What the control plane asks for. The arguments an operation does not read are ignored.
struct JobRequest {
    std::string               nodeId;      // a node of the last published plan
    std::string               capability;  // one of the interface ids above
    std::string               op;          // memory: regions, read, write; sram: dump, restore; rom: header, title
    std::string               region;      // memory: the region's name
    std::uint32_t             offset = 0;  // memory: where a read or write starts in the region
    std::uint32_t             length = 0;  // memory read, rom header: how many bytes (0: to the end)
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;       // memory write, sram restore
};

// submitJob's answer: the job's id (counting up from 1, never reused), or 0 with the refusal in `error`.
struct JobSubmit {
    std::uint32_t id = 0;
    std::string   error;
};

// One entry of drainJobs: a finished job (`done`), or a running one that reported progress since the last drain.
struct JobCompletion {
    std::uint32_t             id = 0;
    bool                      done = false;
    bool                      ok = false;
    std::string               error;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;  // the result; the caller owns it once drained
    std::uint32_t             progress = 0;
    std::uint32_t             total = 0;
};

// A job not yet collected: the control thread's, as above.
struct Job {
    enum State : std::uint8_t {
        Queued,   // taken, not yet applied (a write in the ring, a device job not yet finished)
        Applied,  // a write the block thread has applied, waiting for the block that publishes it (block thread only)
        Done,     // finished: `result` holds its bytes
        Failed,   // finished: `failure` says why (and `error`, for one a device thread wrote)
    };
    enum Failure : std::uint8_t {
        None,
        OutOfRange,  // the region was smaller than the write by the time it applied (a model switch shrank it)
        Removed,     // the node left the plan before the job completed: its core is gone or about to go
        Discarded,   // the engine dropped the queued command at teardown, never applying it
        Device,      // a device thread failed it, the reason in `error`
        Overflow,    // more writes were applied than the engine's table of unpublished writes holds (a broken bound)
    };

    std::uint32_t id = 0;
    // A write the old system-id RPC (writeRam) made: it applies on the same path and nobody collects it, so it queues
    // no completion and is done once applied.
    bool          detached = false;
    std::string   nodeId;      // what its completion's error names
    SystemId      system = 0;
    std::size_t   region = 0;  // an index into the core's MemoryCapability::regions()
    std::uint32_t offset = 0;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;  // the write's: read by the block thread, owned and freed here
    // The core the write was applied to: the block thread's (or the control thread's while no audio thread runs), set
    // at the apply and only compared at the confirm, never followed, so a system id re-added with a new core between
    // the two cannot pass for the one written.
    SystemBase*   core = nullptr;

    std::atomic<std::uint8_t>  state{Queued};
    std::atomic<std::uint8_t>  failure{None};
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> progress{0};
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> total{0};
    std::uint32_t              reported = 0;  // the progress drainJobs last handed back (control thread)
    std::vector<std::uint8_t>  result;         // a device job's bytes, written before its terminal state
    std::string                error;          // a device job's reason, likewise

    bool finished() const {
        const std::uint8_t s = state.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        return s == Done || s == Failed;
    }
};

}  // namespace rp::host
````

Create `packages/native/src/system/SystemCapabilities.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "system/SystemCapabilities.hpp"

#include <cstring>

#include "system/MemoryAccessor.hpp"
#include "system/SystemBase.hpp"

namespace rp {

namespace {

// The work RAM, the one region the snapshot registry publishes every block (SnapshotRegistry::publishRam).
constexpr MemoryCapability::Region kCoreRegions[] = {{"ram", MemoryType::Ram}};

}  // namespace

std::span<const MemoryCapability::Region> CoreMemory::regions() const { return kCoreRegions; }

bool CoreMemory::write(std::size_t region, std::uint32_t offset, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
    if (region >= std::size(kCoreRegions) || !data || size == 0) return false;
    // ReadWrite, so a backend with a read-only view reports failure rather than dropping the write into a copy nobody
    // reads.
    MemoryAccessor acc = core_.getMemory(kCoreRegions[region].type, AccessType::ReadWrite);
    if (!acc.valid() || static_cast<std::size_t>(offset) + size > acc.size()) return false;
    std::memcpy(acc.data() + offset, data, size);
    return true;
}

std::string CoreRom::title() const {
    std::string out;
    for (std::size_t i = titleOffset_; i < titleOffset_ + titleLength_ && i < rom_.size(); ++i) {
        if (rom_[i] == 0) break;
        out.push_back(static_cast<char>(rom_[i]));
    }
    return out;
}

}  // namespace rp
````

Create `packages/native/src/system/SystemCapabilities.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <span>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "system/MemoryType.hpp"

class SystemBase;

// The capability interfaces a system presents to the control plane's jobs (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md
// section 6), each named by its versioned id and asked for through a nullable accessor on SystemBase, as ChannelTap
// is: rp.system.memory/1 through memory(), rp.system.sram/1 through sram(), rp.system.rom/1 through rom(). A caller
// branches on null, so the engine runs a job without naming the console. Each covers what the control plane does with
// a system and no more: the work RAM it reads and pokes (readRam / writeRam), the battery it dumps (readSram) and the
// ROM header it reads (readFilePrefix on the file the core was built from).
//
// The control plane never reads a live core: the engine serves every read of an emulated system from its snapshot
// registry's published copy (SnapshotRegistry), and applies every write on the block thread at a block boundary, or
// on the control thread while no audio thread runs. So an interface here holds the facts that are fixed for the
// core's life, which any thread may read, and the block-side half of a write. The system owns each object, and it
// lives as long as the core: the pointer an accessor returns is the same for the core's lifetime.

namespace rp {

// rp.system.memory/1: named regions of the core's memory, read and written by range. Reads are the registry's
// published copy of a region, so a region is listed only where the registry publishes it every block: the work RAM.
class MemoryCapability {
public:
    struct Region {
        const char* name;  // the name a job addresses it by
        MemoryType  type;  // the core's region behind it (SystemBase::getMemory)
    };

    virtual ~MemoryCapability() = default;

    // [any] The regions, fixed for the core's life. A region's size is the published copy's (the registry's), since a
    // live model switch can resize the region itself (SameBoy's DMG 8 KiB and CGB 32 KiB work RAM).
    virtual std::span<const Region> regions() const = 0;
    // [block, or control while quiescent] Copy `size` bytes into region `region` (an index into regions()) at `offset`
    // of the live core. False, writing nothing, for a range past the region's end: half a song block is not a song,
    // and a write past the end would corrupt whatever the core keeps after it. Allocates nothing.
    virtual bool write(std::size_t region, std::uint32_t offset, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) = 0;
};

// rp.system.sram/1: the cartridge's battery RAM, dumped whole and restored whole. An emulated core's dump is the
// registry's published copy; its restore is a rebuild that seeds the battery (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md
// section 5, SystemsStore.loadSram), never a live write, so the engine refuses that operation for a system node at
// submission. A core presents this to say it has a battery the registry publishes; there is nothing to call on it.
class SramCapability {
public:
    virtual ~SramCapability() = default;
};

// rp.system.rom/1: the ROM the core was built from. Its bytes are immutable for the core's life, so every member is a
// read any thread may make.
class RomCapability {
public:
    virtual ~RomCapability() = default;

    // [any] The whole ROM image, as the file the system was built from holds it: its header is a prefix of this.
    virtual std::span<const std::uint8_t> image() const = 0;
    // [any] The cartridge's title field as the ROM stores it, up to its first NUL, or empty for a console whose header
    // has none (a NES's iNES header, a Master System's).
    virtual std::string title() const = 0;
};

// The three, as every emulated core presents them: the work RAM through SystemBase::getMemory, a battery that is only
// dumped, and the ROM vector the core keeps. A console holds one of each as members and returns their addresses.
class CoreMemory final : public MemoryCapability {
public:
    explicit CoreMemory(SystemBase& core) : core_(core) {}
    std::span<const Region> regions() const override;
    bool write(std::size_t region, std::uint32_t offset, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) override;

private:
    SystemBase& core_;
};

class CoreSram final : public SramCapability {};

class CoreRom final : public RomCapability {
public:
    // `rom` is the vector the core keeps and never changes after construction; the title is the field of
    // `titleLength` bytes at `titleOffset` (0 bytes for a console with none).
    CoreRom(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& rom, std::size_t titleOffset, std::size_t titleLength)
        : rom_(rom), titleOffset_(titleOffset), titleLength_(titleLength) {}
    std::span<const std::uint8_t> image() const override { return rom_; }
    std::string title() const override;

private:
    const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& rom_;
    std::size_t                      titleOffset_;
    std::size_t                      titleLength_;
};

}  // namespace rp
````

````diff
+// --- capability jobs (CapabilityJobs.hpp) ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+const rp::host::SystemEntry* Engine::publishedSystem(const std::string& nodeId) const {
+    constexpr std::string_view prefix = "sys-";
+    if (!publishedTable_ || nodeId.size() <= prefix.size() || nodeId.compare(0, prefix.size(), prefix) != 0)
+        return nullptr;
+    std::uint64_t id = 0;
+    for (std::size_t i = prefix.size(); i < nodeId.size(); ++i) {
+        const char c = nodeId[i];
+        if (c < '0' || c > '9' || id > UINT32_MAX) return nullptr;
+        id = id * 10 + static_cast<std::uint64_t>(c - '0');
+    }
+    if (id == 0 || id > UINT32_MAX) return nullptr;
+    const auto* e = publishedTable_->find(static_cast<SystemId>(id));
+    // The canonical spelling only: "sys-01" is not the node of system 1.
+    return e && nodeId == "sys-" + std::to_string(e->id) ? e : nullptr;
+}
+
+std::size_t Engine::jobsOutstanding() const {
+    std::size_t n = completions_.size();
+    for (const auto& j : jobs_)
+        if (!j->detached) ++n;
+    return n;
+}
+
+rp::host::JobSubmit Engine::submitJob(rp::host::JobRequest r) {
+    using rp::host::Job;
+    using rp::host::JobCompletion;
+    const auto refuse = [](std::string why) { return rp::host::JobSubmit{0, std::move(why)}; };
+    settleQuiescent();
+    sweepJobs();
+    if (jobsOutstanding() >= kMaxJobs)
+        return refuse("busy: " + std::to_string(kMaxJobs) + " jobs are outstanding; drain their completions first");
+    if (!graph_->host->node(r.nodeId)) return refuse("the running graph has no node " + r.nodeId);
+    const rp::host::SystemEntry* entry = publishedSystem(r.nodeId);
+    if (!entry) return submitDeviceJob(r);
+    SystemBase* core = entry->core;
+    const auto presentsNo = [&] { return refuse("node " + r.nodeId + " presents no " + r.capability); };
+    const auto noOp = [&] { return refuse(r.capability + " has no operation '" + r.op + "'"); };
+    // A read answered from what is published (or from the ROM, which never changes): its completion is queued here.
+    const auto completeNow = [&](std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes) {
+        const std::uint32_t id = nextJobId_++;
+        JobCompletion c;
+        c.id = id;
+        c.done = c.ok = true;
+        c.bytes = std::move(bytes);
+        completions_.push_back(std::move(c));
+        return rp::host::JobSubmit{id, {}};
+    };
+
+    if (r.capability == RP_SYSTEM_MEMORY_INTERFACE) {
+        rp::MemoryCapability* memory = core ? core->memory() : nullptr;
+        if (!memory) return presentsNo();
+        const auto regions = memory->regions();
+        // A region's size is its published copy's; only the work RAM is published (SnapshotRegistry::publishRam).
+        const auto publishedSize = [&](const rp::MemoryCapability::Region& region) -> std::size_t {
+            return region.type == rp::MemoryType::Ram ? registry_.ramSize(entry->id) : 0;
+        };
+        if (r.op == "regions") {
+            std::string json = "[";
+            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < regions.size(); ++i) {
+                if (i) json += ",";
+                json += std::string("{\"name\":\"") + regions[i].name + "\",\"size\":" +
+                        std::to_string(publishedSize(regions[i])) + "}";
+            }
+            json += "]";
+            return completeNow(std::vector<std::uint8_t>(json.begin(), json.end()));
+        }
+        if (r.op != "read" && r.op != "write") return noOp();
+        std::size_t index = regions.size();
+        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < regions.size(); ++i)
+            if (r.region == regions[i].name) index = i;
+        if (index == regions.size()) return refuse("node " + r.nodeId + " has no memory region '" + r.region + "'");
+        const auto notPublished = [&] { return refuse("region " + r.region + " of node " + r.nodeId + " is not published"); };
+        if (r.op == "read") {
+            // One read of the published copy, which is its own bound: a block republishing it at a new size between
+            // a size query and the read would otherwise refuse a read that was in range.
+            auto ram = regions[index].type == rp::MemoryType::Ram ? registry_.readRam(entry->id) : std::nullopt;
+            if (!ram || ram->empty()) return notPublished();
+            const std::size_t size = ram->size();
+            const std::size_t length = r.length != 0 ? r.length : (r.offset < size ? size - r.offset : 0);
+            if (static_cast<std::size_t>(r.offset) + length > size || length == 0)
+                return refuse("the read runs past region " + r.region + " (" + std::to_string(size) + " bytes)");
+            if (r.offset == 0 && length == size) return completeNow(std::move(*ram));
+            return completeNow(std::vector<std::uint8_t>(ram->begin() + r.offset, ram->begin() + r.offset + length));
+        }
+        const std::size_t size = publishedSize(regions[index]);
+        if (size == 0) return notPublished();
+        // The answerable failures are answered here, from the published copy (race-free, no live-core read): the
+        // block thread re-checks the bounds as it applies, since a model switch could shrink the region between.
+        if (r.bytes.empty()) return refuse("an empty write");
+        if (static_cast<std::size_t>(r.offset) + r.bytes.size() > size)
+            return refuse("the write runs past region " + r.region + " (" + std::to_string(size) + " bytes)");
+        auto job = std::make_unique<Job>();
+        job->id = nextJobId_;
+        job->nodeId = r.nodeId;
+        job->system = entry->id;
+        job->region = index;
+        job->offset = r.offset;
+        job->bytes = std::move(r.bytes);
+        DspCommand c;
+        c.kind = DspCommand::Kind::CapabilityWrite;
+        c.capabilityWrite = {job.get()};
+        // Pushed before the record joins jobs_: a quiescent push applies it inline, which leaves it in applied_ for
+        // settleQuiescent below, and a refused one is freed here.
+        if (!pushCommand(c)) return refuse("busy: the command ring is full");
+        ++nextJobId_;
+        jobs_.push_back(std::move(job));
+        settleQuiescent();
+        return {jobs_.back()->id, {}};
+    }
+    if (r.capability == RP_SYSTEM_SRAM_INTERFACE) {
+        rp::SramCapability* sram = core ? core->sram() : nullptr;
+        if (!sram) return presentsNo();
+        if (r.op == "dump") {
+            auto bytes = registry_.readSram(entry->id);
+            if (!bytes) return refuse("node " + r.nodeId + " publishes no battery");
+            return completeNow(std::move(*bytes));
+        }
+        if (r.op == "restore")
+            return refuse("node " + r.nodeId + " restores no battery in place: an emulated system's battery is "
+                          "restored by rebuilding it with the bytes as its seed");
+        return noOp();
+    }
+    if (r.capability == RP_SYSTEM_ROM_INTERFACE) {
+        rp::RomCapability* rom = core ? core->rom() : nullptr;
+        if (!rom) return presentsNo();
+        if (r.op == "header") {
+            const auto image = rom->image();
+            const std::size_t n = r.length != 0 ? std::min<std::size_t>(r.length, image.size()) : image.size();
+            return completeNow(std::vector<std::uint8_t>(image.begin(), image.begin() + n));
+        }
+        if (r.op == "title") {
+            const std::string title = rom->title();
+            return completeNow(std::vector<std::uint8_t>(title.begin(), title.end()));
+        }
+        return noOp();
+    }
+    return refuse("unknown capability " + r.capability);
+}
+
+rp::host::JobSubmit Engine::submitDeviceJob(const rp::host::JobRequest& r) {
+    // A node that is no system node. The device nodes (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md sections 4 and 6) present
+    // their capabilities here: asked through the node for the interface, they accept the job (and the engine adopts its
+    // record, adoptJob) or refuse it synchronously, busy or not connected. No node type presents one yet.
+    return {0, "node " + r.nodeId + " presents no " + r.capability};
+}
+
+rp::host::JobSubmit Engine::adoptJob(std::unique_ptr<rp::host::Job> job) {
+    settleQuiescent();
+    sweepJobs();
+    if (!job) return {0, "no job"};
+    if (jobsOutstanding() >= kMaxJobs)
+        return {0, "busy: " + std::to_string(kMaxJobs) + " jobs are outstanding; drain their completions first"};
+    job->id = nextJobId_++;
+    job->detached = false;
+    const std::uint32_t id = job->id;
+    jobs_.push_back(std::move(job));
+    return {id, {}};
+}
+
+bool Engine::writeRam(SystemId id, std::uint32_t offset, std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes) {
+    sweepJobs();
+    if (bytes.empty() || !publishedTable_) return false;
+    const auto* entry = publishedTable_->find(id);
+    rp::MemoryCapability* memory = entry ? entry->core->memory() : nullptr;
+    if (!memory) return false;
+    const auto regions = memory->regions();
+    std::size_t index = regions.size();
+    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < regions.size(); ++i)
+        if (regions[i].type == rp::MemoryType::Ram) index = i;
+    if (index == regions.size()) return false;
+    auto job = std::make_unique<rp::host::Job>();
+    job->detached = true;
+    job->system = id;
+    job->region = index;
+    job->offset = offset;
+    job->bytes = std::move(bytes);
+    DspCommand c;
+    c.kind = DspCommand::Kind::CapabilityWrite;
+    c.capabilityWrite = {job.get()};
+    if (!pushCommand(c)) return false;  // full ring: drop the poke, freeing the record here
+    jobs_.push_back(std::move(job));
+    return true;
+}
+
+std::vector<rp::host::JobCompletion> Engine::drainJobs() {
+    settleQuiescent();
+    sweepJobs();
+    std::vector<rp::host::JobCompletion> out(std::make_move_iterator(completions_.begin()),
+                                             std::make_move_iterator(completions_.end()));
+    completions_.clear();
+    // A running job's progress, once per change: what a device thread reports through the record.
+    for (const auto& j : jobs_) {
+        if (j->detached) continue;
+        const std::uint32_t progress = j->progress.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        const std::uint32_t total = j->total.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        if (total == 0 || progress == j->reported) continue;
+        j->reported = progress;
+        rp::host::JobCompletion c;
+        c.id = j->id;
+        c.progress = progress;
+        c.total = total;
+        out.push_back(std::move(c));
+    }
+    return out;
+}
+
+void Engine::sweepJobs() {
+    using rp::host::Job;
+    for (auto it = jobs_.begin(); it != jobs_.end();) {
+        Job& j = **it;
+        if (!j.finished()) {
+            ++it;
+            continue;
+        }
+        if (!j.detached) {
+            rp::host::JobCompletion c;
+            c.id = j.id;
+            c.done = true;
+            c.ok = j.state.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) == Job::Done;
+            c.progress = j.progress.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+            c.total = j.total.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+            if (c.ok) {
+                c.bytes = std::move(j.result);
+            } else {
+                switch (j.failure.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
+                    case Job::OutOfRange: c.error = "the write ran past the region of node " + j.nodeId + " as it applied"; break;
+                    case Job::Removed:    c.error = "node " + j.nodeId + " left the plan before the job completed"; break;
+                    case Job::Discarded:  c.error = "the engine stopped before the job ran"; break;
+                    case Job::Overflow:   c.error = "the engine's table of unpublished writes was full"; break;
+                    default:              c.error = j.error.empty() ? "the job failed" : j.error; break;
+                }
+            }
+            completions_.push_back(std::move(c));
+        }
+        it = jobs_.erase(it);
+    }
+}
+
+void Engine::applyJob(rp::host::Job& job, const rp::host::SystemTable& table) {
+    using rp::host::Job;
+    const rp::host::SystemEntry* e = table.find(job.system);
+    rp::MemoryCapability* memory = e ? e->core->memory() : nullptr;
+    const auto fail = [&job](Job::Failure why) {
+        job.failure.store(why, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        job.state.store(Job::Failed, std::memory_order_release);
+    };
+    if (!memory) return fail(Job::Removed);
+    if (!memory->write(job.region, job.offset, job.bytes.data(), job.bytes.size())) return fail(Job::OutOfRange);
+    // An old write is collected by nobody, so it is done once applied; a job's write waits for the publish.
+    if (job.detached) {
+        job.state.store(Job::Done, std::memory_order_release);
+        return;
+    }
+    // The table has room: every job in it is one of at most kMaxJobs outstanding. A bound broken later must not let a
+    // write complete before its region is published, so a full table fails the write rather than finishing it.
+    assert(appliedCount_ < applied_.size());
+    if (appliedCount_ == applied_.size()) return fail(Job::Overflow);
+    job.core = e->core;
+    job.state.store(Job::Applied, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    applied_[appliedCount_++] = &job;
+}
+
+void Engine::confirmApplied(const rp::host::SystemTable& ran) {
+    using rp::host::Job;
+    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < appliedCount_; ++i) {
+        Job& job = *applied_[i];
+        // The id and the core both: an id re-added with a new core since the apply is not the core written.
+        const rp::host::SystemEntry* e = ran.find(job.system);
+        const bool published = e && e->core == job.core;
+        if (!published) job.failure.store(Job::Removed, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        // The job's last touch on this thread: the control thread may free it from here on.
+        job.state.store(published ? Job::Done : Job::Failed, std::memory_order_release);
+    }
+    appliedCount_ = 0;
+}
+
+void Engine::settleQuiescent() {
+    // Ownership first: applied_ is the block thread's while an audio thread runs.
+    if (graph_->host->audioThreadOwns() || appliedCount_ == 0) return;
+    const rp::host::SystemTable& table = currentTable();
+    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < appliedCount_; ++i)
+        if (const auto* e = table.find(applied_[i]->system); e && e->core == applied_[i]->core)
+            registry_.publishRam(*e->core);
+    confirmApplied(table);
+}
+
 std::optional<std::vector<std::uint8_t>> Engine::readState(SystemId id) {
     return registry_.readState(id);   // the owned published copy, never the live core
 }

+
+// A capability job (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 6, Engine::submitJob): the node it is for, the
+// interface ("rp.system.memory/1", "rp.system.sram/1", "rp.system.rom/1") and its operation, and the arguments that
+// operation reads. memory: `region` by name, `offset`, and `length` for a read (absent or 0: to the region's end) or
+// `bytes` for a write; sram: `bytes` for a restore; rom: `length` for a header (absent or 0: the whole image).
+struct RpcJobRequest {
+    std::string                    nodeId;
+    std::string                    capability;
+    std::string                    op;
+    std::optional<std::string>     region;
+    std::optional<std::uint32_t>   offset;
+    std::optional<std::uint32_t>   length;
+    std::optional<rfl::Bytestring> bytes;
+};
+// Its answer: `id` (the job was taken; its completion comes through drainJobs) or `error` (it was refused, and
+// why). Exactly one is present.
+struct RpcJobSubmitResult {
+    std::optional<std::uint32_t> id;
+    std::optional<std::string>   error;
+};
+// One entry drainJobs hands back: a job that finished (`done`, then `ok` with its result in `bytes`, or `error`), or
+// one still running that reported progress (`done` false, `progress` of `total`).
+struct RpcJobCompletion {
+    std::uint32_t   id;
+    bool            done;
+    bool            ok;
+    std::string     error;
+    rfl::Bytestring bytes;
+    std::uint32_t   progress;
+    std::uint32_t   total;
+};

     const std::size_t ram = engine_.ramSize(id);
     if (ram == 0 || static_cast<std::size_t>(offset) + bytes.size() > ram) return false;
     const auto* p = reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(bytes.data());
-    invoker_.writeRam(id, offset, std::vector<std::uint8_t>(p, p + bytes.size()));
-    return true;
+    return invoker_.writeRam(id, offset, std::vector<std::uint8_t>(p, p + bytes.size()));
+}
+
+RpcJobSubmitResult EngineRpcService::submitJob(RpcJobRequest request) {
+    rp::host::JobRequest r;
+    r.nodeId = std::move(request.nodeId);
+    r.capability = std::move(request.capability);
+    r.op = std::move(request.op);
+    r.region = request.region.value_or("");
+    r.offset = request.offset.value_or(0);
+    r.length = request.length.value_or(0);
+    if (request.bytes) {
+        const auto* p = reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(request.bytes->data());
+        r.bytes.assign(p, p + request.bytes->size());
+    }
+    const rp::host::JobSubmit submitted = engine_.submitJob(std::move(r));
+    RpcJobSubmitResult out;
+    if (submitted.id != 0) out.id = submitted.id;
+    else out.error = submitted.error;
+    return out;
+}
+
+std::vector<RpcJobCompletion> EngineRpcService::drainJobs() {
+    std::vector<RpcJobCompletion> out;
+    for (auto& c : engine_.drainJobs())
+        out.push_back({c.id, c.done, c.ok, std::move(c.error), toBytestring(c.bytes), c.progress, c.total});
+    return out;
 }
````
