````cpp
#include "host/graph/N8Nodes.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <bitset>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <iterator>
#include <limits>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>

#include "graph/node.hpp"
#include "host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp"
#include "host/engine/CapabilityJobs.hpp"
#include "host/graph/HostServices.hpp"
#include "host/graph/SystemNodes.hpp"  // kExpansionVolume*

namespace rp::host {

// Named, so its JSON Schema $defs key is the same under every compiler.
struct CartMirrorSettings {
    // The system the cart mirrors (a system id, as a system node's {"system": <id>}).
    std::uint64_t system = 0;
};

int expansionVolumeRegister(double percent) {
    const long value = std::lround(percent * 128.0 / 100.0);
    return static_cast<int>(std::clamp(value, 0L, 255L));
}

namespace {

// What the cart mirror's system's FIFO is fed, in the order the kernel stage the kernel node replaced fed it: its MIDI,
// then its bytes, each in queue order. An empty message is skipped, as that stage skipped it. It needs the engine's
// host I/O, so it does not activate without it.
struct CartMirror {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.n8.cart-mirror";
    static constexpr const char* name = "N8 Cart Mirror";
    static constexpr const char* category = "host";
    using Settings = CartMirrorSettings;
    // Its settings change nothing it does (the engine reads them off the document), so a change is a swap, and its
    // prepare reads nothing a commit writes.
    static constexpr bool stateless_prepare = true;
    struct {
        rp::events_in midi;
        rp::bytes_in  bytes;
    } inputs;

    const EngineHostIo* io = nullptr;
    void bind_host(const rp_host* h) noexcept {
        io = static_cast<const EngineHostIo*>(h->get_interface(h, RP_ENGINE_HOST_IO_INTERFACE));
    }
    bool activate(double, std::uint32_t) { return io != nullptr; }

    static std::optional<std::string> validate(const Settings& s) {
        if (s.system == 0 || s.system > UINT32_MAX) return "system names the system the cart mirrors: 1 to 4294967295";
        return std::nullopt;
    }

    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        for (const rp_message& m : inputs.midi.messages()) {
            const auto data = inputs.midi.data(m);
            if (!data.empty()) io->cartBytes(io->ctx, m.frame, data.data(), data.size(), false);
        }
        for (const rp_message& m : inputs.bytes.messages()) {
            const auto data = inputs.bytes.data(m);
            if (!data.empty()) io->cartBytes(io->ctx, m.frame, data.data(), data.size(), (m.flags & RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH) != 0);
        }
    }
};

using ExpansionVolumeParam =
    rp::int_param<"Expansion volume", rp::range{kExpansionVolumeMin, kExpansionVolumeMax, kExpansionVolumeDefault}, "%">;

// The real cart, a node of its own (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 4). It borrows the host's cart link
// for the life of its plan: acquired in activate, kept across a reactivate, released in its destructor (the reclaim's,
// on the control thread). Placed by a setting rather than by the device's state, so it always activates: in a host with
// no cart, or with the cart unplugged, the link reads disconnected and takes every push nowhere, and nothing in the
// graph changes when the cart comes or goes.
struct N8Nes {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.n8.nes";
    static constexpr const char* name = "NES (N8 cart)";
    static constexpr const char* category = "device";
    // Its device runs threads of its own (the link's serial thread, which a job's transfer runs on), so a target with
    // none (the Pico) refuses the type.
    static constexpr bool threads = true;
    // rp.mesen.nes's two inputs the cart's FIFO is fed from, shaped as that node's are, so a source wired to one wires
    // to the other.
    struct {
        rp::events_in midi;
        rp::bytes_in  bytes;
    } inputs;
    struct { rp::control_out connected; } outputs;
    struct { ExpansionVolumeParam expansionVolume; } params;

    const HostDevices* devices = nullptr;
    CartLink*          cart = nullptr;
    // What the node presents as rp.system.sram/1 and rp.system.rom/1: every job goes to the link, the node its owner.
    DeviceJobs jobs{this, &submitJob};
    // The volume the link was last given, in whole percent (NaN: none yet, so the first block gives it), and whether
    // the link read connected in the last block, so a reconnect gives it again.
    double volumeSent = std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN();
    bool   wasConnected = false;
    // The notes the cart was sent a note-on for and no note-off yet (a channel's 128 notes a channel, 16 channels), and
    // of those, the ones whose note-off the link dropped (it was down, or a job held it). An owed note-off goes out at
    // the start of the next block the link reads connected in: a pause drops what is pushed while it lasts, and a
    // note-off lost there would leave the console holding the note for good.
    std::bitset<16 * 128> sounding, owed;

    void bind_host(const rp_host* h) noexcept {
        devices = static_cast<const HostDevices*>(h->get_interface(h, RP_HOST_DEVICES_INTERFACE));
    }
    bool activate(double, std::uint32_t) {
        if (!devices) return false;
        // A reactivate runs activate again on this instance: the handle already held is kept, one acquire to one
        // release.
        if (!cart) cart = devices->acquireCart(devices->ctx, kCartDeviceName);
        return cart != nullptr;
    }
    ~N8Nes() {
        if (!devices || !cart) return;
        // A job this node submitted that is still running fails now, and the link reports into its record no more, so
        // the engine may free the record; the device stops at its next safe point.
        cart->abandonJobs(this);
        devices->releaseCart(devices->ctx, cart);
    }

    const void* get_interface(std::string_view id) noexcept {
        return id == RP_SYSTEM_SRAM_INTERFACE || id == RP_SYSTEM_ROM_INTERFACE ? &jobs : nullptr;
    }
    static bool submitJob(void* ctx, const JobRequest& request, Job& job, std::string* error) {
        auto* self = static_cast<N8Nes*>(ctx);
        if (!self->cart) {
            if (error) *error = "not connected";
            return false;
        }
        return self->cart->submitJob(request, job, self, error);
    }

    void process(const rp::Block& b) noexcept {
        const double rate = b.transport().sample_rate;
        const bool   connected = cart->connected();
        // `connected` holds 1 or 0 from frame 0: a change at frame 0 on the block it flips, since a stream's start
        // value is the last block's end.
        const double flag = connected ? 1.0 : 0.0;
        if (flag != outputs.connected.queue->start) outputs.connected.push(0, flag);
        if (connected && !wasConnected) volumeSent = std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN();  // every connect again
        wasConnected = connected;
        applyVolume();
        if (connected && owed.any()) payOwed(rate);
        // The cart's FIFO is fed as the emulated NES's is: the MIDI, then the bytes, each in queue order, an empty
        // message skipped, the bytes' flush flag carried.
        for (const rp_message& m : inputs.midi.messages()) {
            const auto data = inputs.midi.data(m);
            if (!data.empty()) pushMidi(m.frame, data.data(), data.size(), rate);
        }
        for (const rp_message& m : inputs.bytes.messages()) {
            const auto data = inputs.bytes.data(m);
            if (!data.empty()) cart->push(m.frame, data.data(), data.size(), (m.flags & RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH) != 0, rate);
        }
    }

    // The param's latest value, as the emulated NES takes it (clamped, whole percent), to the link when it moved or the
    // link came back: the link keeps the value and its serial thread writes it, so this neither blocks nor allocates.
    void applyVolume() noexcept {
        const double latest = params.expansionVolume.latest();
        if (latest != latest) return;  // NaN reaches a param only over a wire, and moves nothing
        const double percent = static_cast<double>(std::lround(
            std::clamp(latest, static_cast<double>(kExpansionVolumeMin), static_cast<double>(kExpansionVolumeMax))));
        if (percent == volumeSent) return;
        cart->setExpansionVolume(expansionVolumeRegister(percent));
        volumeSent = percent;
    }

    // One MIDI message to the link, keeping the books on its notes. Whether the push went out is read off the link's
    // own drop count around it, which only the block thread moves.
    void pushMidi(std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, double rate) noexcept {
        const std::uint64_t before = cart->dropped();
        cart->push(frame, data, size, false, rate);
        const bool sent = cart->dropped() == before;
        if (size < 3) return;
        const std::uint8_t kind = data[0] & 0xF0;
        const std::size_t  note = static_cast<std::size_t>(data[0] & 0x0F) * 128 + (data[1] & 0x7F);
        const bool         on = kind == 0x90 && data[2] != 0;
        const bool         off = kind == 0x80 || (kind == 0x90 && data[2] == 0);
        if (on && sent) {
            sounding.set(note);
            owed.reset(note);
        } else if (off) {
            if (sent) {
                sounding.reset(note);
                owed.reset(note);
            } else if (sounding.test(note)) {
                owed.set(note);
            }
        }
    }

    // The note-offs the link dropped for notes the cart is holding, at frame 0, before anything this block carries. One
    // the link still cannot take stays owed for the next block.
    void payOwed(double rate) noexcept {
        for (std::size_t note = 0; note < owed.size(); ++note) {
            if (!owed.test(note)) continue;
            const std::uint8_t off[3] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0x80 | (note / 128)),
                                         static_cast<std::uint8_t>(note % 128), 0};
            const std::uint64_t before = cart->dropped();
            cart->push(0, off, sizeof off, false, rate);
            if (cart->dropped() != before) return;
            owed.reset(note);
            sounding.reset(note);
        }
    }
};

}  // namespace

const rp_package* n8Package() {
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<CartMirror>(), rp::node_type<N8Nes>()};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.n8","version":"1.0.0"})",
                                     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::size(kTypes)), kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

std::optional<std::uint32_t> cartMirrorSystem(std::string_view settings) {
    const rp_settings s{settings.data(), settings.size(), RP_SETTINGS_JSON};
    const auto parsed = rp::detail::parseSettings<CartMirror>(&s);
    if (!parsed) return std::nullopt;
    return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(parsed->system);  // validate kept it to 1..UINT32_MAX
}

}  // namespace rp::host
````

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <optional>
#include <string_view>

#include "graph/rp_node.h"

namespace rp::host {

// The rp.n8 package: the real NES an Everdrive N8 Pro cart is plugged into.
//
//   rp.n8.cart-mirror  (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md section 3.5), {"system": <id>}: everything on its midi
//                      input, then everything on its bytes input (each with its flush flag), handed to the physical N8
//                      the engine feeds, in queue order. The system it names is the one the cart mirrors, which the
//                      engine reads off the plan: a NES of the document's, one mirror at most.
//   rp.n8.nes          (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 4): the cart as a node of its own, through the
//                      host's cart link (rp.host.devices/1, "n8"). The same `midi` and `bytes` inputs as rp.mesen.nes,
//                      so a system's protocol nodes feed both by fan-out, pushed at the link with their frames, its
//                      MIDI then its bytes; a `connected` control output, 1 while the cart is attached and streaming (0
//                      in a host with no cart, and while a job holds the link); the `expansionVolume` param, rescaled
//                      onto the cart's master-volume register; and the battery file and ROM as capability jobs
//                      (rp.system.sram/1, rp.system.rom/1) run on the link's thread. No audio: the console makes it.
const rp_package* n8Package();

// The system a cart mirror's settings (JSON) name, read as the node reads them, so the engine and the node accept
// the same settings: a field the node does not know is ignored, a missing or out-of-range system refused (nullopt).
std::optional<std::uint32_t> cartMirrorSystem(std::string_view settings);

// rp.n8.nes's `expansionVolume` (whole percent of unity, as the emulated NES's) as the cart's master-volume register:
// 128 is unity, clamped to the register's 0..255. The same rounding as the UI's expVolToN8 (n8Devices.ts), so the
// node and the host's own Settings > N8 row write the same byte for one value.
int expansionVolumeRegister(double percent);

}  // namespace rp::host
````

````diff
+// reports reach nothing, and the record may be freed without waiting for the device to finish. The lock is held for a
+// store or a copy, never across device I/O, and never by the block thread.

+        clear();

+        job_->failure.store(Job::Removed, std::memory_order_relaxed);

+    }

+    }
+    bool abandoned() const { return abandoned_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }

+private:
+    void clear() {

+        job_ = nullptr;
+        owner_ = nullptr;
+    }

+    std::atomic<bool>  abandoned_{false};
+};
````

- [ ] **Step 3: Pause the link in its thread, and run the cart's jobs**

`N8Link` gains `AfterJob {Resume, Stop}`, `PausedJob`, `runPaused`, the `streamLoop` split and the exit that runs an
orphaned job with a null Edio, `drainForJob`, `runJob`, `stopStreaming` and the job mutex and flags. `N8Host` gains
`submitCartJob`, `abandonCartJobs`, `cartJobBusy`, the job slot and the loaded ROM and name under a mutex; the port,
connect, lookahead and the SD-worker starts refuse while a cart job holds the cart. Each job reads the config block
first (map_idx 255 is the menu). A dump lists `EDN8/gamedata/<rom>` and reads `bram.srm` in 512-byte blocks; a restore
writes it in 4 KB ones with `FS_MAKEPATH`, reports `{"path":..., "created":...}`, and closes an incomplete file on
failure; both are refused on a running game and bound to 1 byte to 1 MB. An upload writes `usb-games/<name>` in 8 KB
chunks, installs and boots it, applies the expansion volume, clears `enabled` and returns `Stop`; an abandoned or
failed upload deletes its file. `rom.header` and `rom.title` answer from the image this host booted and are forgotten
when the running map changes or the port changes. `N8CartLink` forwards the job seam; the RPCs and TS carry `name` and
the `rom.upload` result.

````diff
+                // 288 KB took 2.8 s on the real cart, so a battery takes well under a second).
+                const std::uint32_t n = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(srm.size());
+                edio->fileOpen(path, Edio::FA_WRITE | Edio::FA_CREATE_ALWAYS | Edio::FS_MAKEPATH);
+                open = true;
+                constexpr std::size_t CHUNK = 4096;
+                cartJob_.progress(0, n);
+                for (std::size_t off = 0; off < n; off += CHUNK) {
+                    const std::size_t c = std::min<std::size_t>(CHUNK, n - off);
+                    edio->fileWrite(srm.data() + off, c);  // each 1 KB acknowledged by the cart, then its status
+                    cartJob_.progress(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(off + c), n);
+                }
+                edio->fileClose();
+                open = false;
+                const std::string json =
+                    "{\"path\":\"" + path + "\",\"created\":" + (created ? "true" : "false") + "}";
+                outcome->bytes.assign(json.begin(), json.end());
+                outcome->ok = true;
+            } catch (const std::exception& e) {
+                outcome->error = e.what();
+                if (open) {
+                    // The open emptied the file there was: what is on the card now is neither save. Closed best-effort,
+                    // so the cart does not keep the handle.
+                    outcome->error = "the battery file " + path + " was replaced and is incomplete: restore again (" +
+                                     e.what() + ")";
+                    try {
+                        edio->fileClose();
+                    } catch (const std::exception&) {
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            return AfterJob::Resume;
+        };
+    } else {
+        paused.run = [this, outcome, checkStop, atMenu, image = r.bytes, name = r.name](Edio* edio) {
+            if (!edio) {
+                outcome->error = "the link went down before the job ran";
+                return AfterJob::Resume;
+            }
+            const std::string bootPath = "usb-games/" + name;
+            int  mapIndex = -1;
+            bool created = false, opened = false;
+            try {
+                // A running game has no menu, and the menu's own probe would put '*t' into its MIDI stream.
+                if (!atMenu(*edio))
+                    throw std::runtime_error("the cart is running a game, which has no menu to load a ROM: power-cycle "
+                                             "the console to its menu first");
+                N8Menu menu(*edio);
+                menu.test();  // clear error if the menu does not answer
+                edio->fileOpen(bootPath, Edio::FA_WRITE | Edio::FA_CREATE_ALWAYS | Edio::FS_MAKEPATH);
+                created = opened = true;
+                constexpr std::size_t CHUNK = 8192;
+                for (std::size_t off = 0; off < image.size(); off += CHUNK) {
+                    checkStop();
+                    const std::size_t n = std::min(CHUNK, image.size() - off);
+                    edio->fileWrite(image.data() + off, n);
+                    cartJob_.progress(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(off + n), static_cast<std::uint32_t>(image.size()));
+                }
+                checkStop();  // the last point that leaves the cart as it was: past it, the cart boots the image
+                edio->fileClose();
+                opened = false;
+                mapIndex = menu.appInstall(bootPath);  // the menu parses iNES and sources the mapper core from SD
+                menu.appStart();
+            } catch (const std::exception& e) {
+                // Nothing booted: the cart is as it was, and streaming resumes to it, as a failed SD op leaves it. A
+                // file this job created goes with it, so the cart's browser never lists a partial image (best-effort).
+                outcome->error = e.what();
+                if (opened) {
+                    try {
+                        edio->fileClose();
+                    } catch (const std::exception&) {
+                    }
+                }
+                if (created) {
+                    try {
+                        edio->fileDelete(bootPath);
+                    } catch (const std::exception&) {
+                    }
+                }
+                return AfterJob::Resume;
+            }
+            // The game runs. The mapload reloaded the OS's stored master_vol, so set ours on the ROM we hold, whose
+            // header names the mapper outright; best-effort, as every expansion-volume write is.
+            try {
+                applyExpVol(*edio, inesMapper(image));
+            } catch (const std::exception&) {
+            }
+            {
+                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> l(loadedMutex_);
+                loadedRom_      = image;
+                loadedName_     = name;
+                loadedMapIndex_ = mapIndex;
+                lastBootedName_ = name;
+            }
+            // The old stream died with the previous ROM, so streaming stops here and the enabled toggle clears and is
+            // persisted, as startLoadRom does. save() reads port_ on this thread: no config writer runs while a job
+            // holds the cart (setPort, connect and setLookahead refuse while cartJobBusy()), so it cannot move here.
+            enabled_.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+            save();
+            const std::string json = "{\"path\":\"" + bootPath + "\",\"mapIndex\":" + std::to_string(mapIndex) +
+                                     ",\"streaming\":\"stopped\"}";
+            outcome->bytes.assign(json.begin(), json.end());
+            outcome->ok = true;
+            return AfterJob::Stop;
+        };
+    }
+    paused.done = [this, outcome] {
+        if (outcome->ok) cartJob_.succeed(std::move(outcome->bytes));
+        else cartJob_.fail(std::move(outcome->error));
+    };
+    if (!link_.runPaused(std::move(paused))) {
+        cartJob_.unclaim();  // the link went down between the check and the hand-over
+        return refuse("not connected");
+    }
+    return true;
 }
 
 }  // namespace retroplug

+void N8Link::writeChunk(const TimedChunk& chunk) {
+    if (rel_) {
+        std::vector<std::uint8_t> out;
+        std::vector<int> seqs;
+        rel_->send(chunk.data, chunk.len, [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t k, int seq) {
+            if (seq >= 0) seqs.push_back(seq);
+            out.insert(out.end(), d, d + k);
+        });
+        writeFramed(out, seqs, nowNs(), false);
+    } else {
+        if (writeLog_) writeLog_(chunk.data, chunk.len, nowNs(), false);
+        edio_->fifoWR(chunk.data, chunk.len);
+        bytesForwarded_.fetch_add(chunk.len, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    }

+
+void N8Link::drainForJob(TimedChunk& chunk, bool& have) {
+    // What was pushed before the pause goes out first, each chunk at its own release time: at most the lookahead and a
+    // block away, and a note-off among it must reach the cart.
+    while (running_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
+        if (rel_) serviceLink();
+        if (!have) have = ring_.tryPop(chunk);
+        if (!have) break;
+        const std::int64_t now = nowNs();
+        if (now < chunk.targetNs) {
+            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::nanoseconds(std::min<std::int64_t>(chunk.targetNs - now, 200'000)));
+            continue;
+        }
+        have = false;
+        writeChunk(chunk);
+    }
+    // And with the reliable link, until the ROM has acknowledged every frame, so the job does not sit on a frame a
+    // DMC-DMA halt ate and only a re-send would deliver. Bounded: a cart that has stopped answering gets its re-sends
+    // after the job, from the sequence state the pause kept.
+    if (!rel_) return;
+    const std::int64_t until = nowNs() + 250'000'000;
+    while (running_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) && rel_->outstanding() > 0 && nowNs() < until) {
+        serviceLink();
+        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(200));
+    }
+}
+
+void N8Link::runJob(TimedChunk& chunk, bool& have) {
+    PausedJob job;
+    {
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> l(jobMutex_);
+        job = std::move(job_);
+    }
+    // From here the job owns the port: a producer drops (and counts) what it pushes until streaming resumes. A push
+    // that read the flag just before this store can still land in the ring after the drain below; it goes out late,
+    // after the job, which for a note-off is the better of the two.
+    connected_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
+    bool portOk = true;
+    try {
+        drainForJob(chunk, have);
+    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
+        setError(std::string("serial write failed (N8 unplugged?): ") + e.what());
+        portOk = false;
+    }
+    AfterJob after = AfterJob::Stop;
+    if (portOk && running_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
+        try {
+            // Whatever the back-channel still holds (a late ack) would read as the first bytes of the job's reply.
+            serialPort_->flushInput();
+            after = job.run(edio_.get());
+            serialPort_->flushInput();
+            edio_->setReadTimeout(2000);  // a menu command raises it; streaming's own reads never wait on it
+        } catch (const std::exception&) {
+            // The job reports its own failure; one that escapes it leaves the link as a failed op does: streaming.
+        }
+    } else {
+        try {
+            job.run(nullptr);
+        } catch (const std::exception&) {
+        }
+    }
+    if (after == AfterJob::Resume && portOk && running_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
+        connected_.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
+    } else if (portOk) {
+        stopStreaming();
+    } else {
+        running_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);  // a failed write, as streamLoop's: the UI can reconnect
+    }
+    jobPending_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
+    try {
+        job.done();
+    } catch (const std::exception&) {
+        // A throw here would end the serial thread through its entry point, taking the process with it.
+    }
+}
+
+void N8Link::stopStreaming() {
+    // The job asked for streaming to stop (a ROM boot), or a disconnect came during it: the thread ends here, and
+    // closes the port itself, so another process (the CLI's tools) can open it while nothing streams. disconnect()
+    // joins and finds it closed.
+    running_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
+    connected_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
+    // A push that read `connected` just before the pause began reached the ring after its drain; the stream it was for
+    // is gone, so it is thrown away here, and counted (the next connect would clear it uncounted).
+    TimedChunk left;
+    while (ring_.tryPop(left)) {
+        chunksDiscarded_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        pushesDropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    }
+    rel_.reset();
+    reliable_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
+    edio_.reset();
+    serialPort_.reset();
+}
+
 }  // namespace retroplug

+    // What a paused job tells the link once it has run: resume streaming, or stop it (a ROM boot: the old stream is
+    // stale, and a running game has no menu to come back to). Stop closes the port, as a disconnect does.
+    enum class AfterJob { Resume, Stop };
+    // A job the serial thread runs with streaming paused (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 6). The pause

+    // first, each chunk at its own release time, and the reliable link waits until the ROM has acknowledged every frame
+    // (bounded), so a note-off already on its way is not lost; the job then has the port's Edio to itself, and
+    // streaming picks up where it was. `run` gets the link's own Edio, or null when the link went down before the job
+    // could run (it then only says so); `done` runs once streaming has resumed or stopped. Each runs exactly once, on
+    // the serial thread, so a job's completion is posted after the link is back. A job checks stopRequested() between
+    // its steps, and those are its only stop points: a disconnect() (or the owner's destructor) that lands inside a
+    // step waits for it: a 512-byte block of a file read (about half a second on the real cart), a battery file's whole
+    // write once it has begun (under a second), an upload's 8 KB chunk, up to the Edio timeout (2 s) for a cart that
+    // stops answering, plus the drain's bounded wait for acks.
+    struct PausedJob {
+        std::function<AfterJob(Edio*)> run;
+        std::function<void()>          done;

     // run it too).

+    // Hand the serial thread a job to run with streaming paused (see PausedJob). False, and nothing runs, while the

+    // reads false and push() drops (and counts) what it is given.
````

````bash
rp.system.sram/1 goes through the battery file the N8 OS keeps on the SD card, EDN8/gamedata/<rom>/bram.srm, never
the cart's own battery: on the real cart one read of the battery wedged a running BlipToaster and one at the menu left
the menu deaf until a power-cycle. Both run at the menu only, <rom> being the job's `name` or the ROM this host last
booted (forgotten when the port changes), and both keep one bound, 1 byte to 1 MB. A dump reads the file in 512-byte
blocks, each a progress report and a stop point (the menu's file read moves about a kilobyte a second whatever the
block: 62 s for a 64 KB battery). A restore writes it for the game's next boot, making the ROM's folder when there is
none and saying so in its result ({"path":..., "created":...}); the Edio subset has no rename, so once the file is
opened the write runs to the end, and one that fails there closes the file and says the battery file is incomplete.
N8Host's SD-worker battery transfers (startDumpSram, startRestoreSram) now refuse through the worker's error channel,
pointing at the jobs.
````

### Task 4: `rp.launchpad.surface-in` / `-out`, the control surface as nodes

Design section 5 and section 8 item 4. The `rp.launchpad` package holds two node types over the host's one surface
link. `surface-in` drains the link into an `in` events output at the start of its block, each message at frame 0,
follows the device with a `connected` control output from frame 0, and discards what the link held when it bound it.
`surface-out` hands every message of its `out` events input to `pushOutput` in queue order. The event ports are the
shapes the controller session reads and writes, so the session wires to the nodes with no adapter. Both declare
`threads` and `unique`, acquire the link in `activate`, keep it across a reactivate and release it in destroy. Two nodes
rather than one because a surface that both feeds a session and follows it is a node-level cycle; the only wire that
breaks a cycle is a feedback wire, which would deliver the previous block. With two nodes the protocol suite reproduces
the recorded `Sent` in full, digest included, block for block.

**Files:**
- Create: `packages/native/src/host/graph/LaunchpadNodes.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/graph/LaunchpadNodes.hpp`, `packages/native/test/engine-graph/FakeSurfaceLink.hpp`, `packages/native/test/engine-graph/Surface.test.cpp`
- Modify: `packages/native/CMakeLists.txt`, `packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake`, `packages/native/src/graph/Descriptor.cpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/Descriptor.hpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/Planner.cpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/node.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/devices/DeviceRegistry.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/engine/Engine.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/graph/N8Nodes.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/launchpad/LaunchpadLink.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/launchpad/LaunchpadLink.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/launchpad/LaunchpadSurfaceLink.hpp`, `packages/native/test/engine-graph/Devices.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/engine-graph/NodeRig.hpp`, `packages/native/test/engine-graph/ProtocolNodes.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/graph/Descriptor.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/launchpad/LaunchpadLink.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/launchpad/LaunchpadSurfaceLink.test.cpp`, `packages/retroplug/src/graph/defineNode.ts`, `packages/retroplug/src/graph/descriptor.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/define-node.test.ts`

Create `packages/native/test/engine-graph/FakeSurfaceLink.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// Stage 1's fake control-surface link, shared by the cases that drive a node over rp.host.devices/1: it scripts what
// the device sent, records what a node handed it, and counts the nodes holding it. A message it records lives in its
// own slot, so a case that counts allocations reserves the room it needs before counting.

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <vector>

#include "host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp"

namespace rp::host::test {

// One message in storage the caller owns, as a test scripts the device's input.
inline DeviceMessage deviceMessage(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& bytes) {
    DeviceMessage m;
    m.size = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(bytes.size());
    std::copy(bytes.begin(), bytes.end(), m.data);
    return m;
}

class FakeSurfaceLink final : public SurfaceLink {
public:
    struct Out {
        std::uint16_t size = 0;
        std::uint8_t  data[kMaxDeviceMessage] = {};
    };

    void reserve(std::size_t in, std::size_t out) {
        input.reserve(in);
        outputs.reserve(out);
    }

    std::size_t drainInput(DeviceMessage* out, std::size_t capacity) override {
        std::size_t n = 0;
        while (next < input.size() && n < capacity) out[n++] = input[next++];
        return n;
    }
    void pushOutput(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) override {
        if (!attached) {
            ++drops;
            return;
        }
        Out m;
        m.size = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(std::min(size, kMaxDeviceMessage));
        std::memcpy(m.data, data, m.size);
        outputs.push_back(m);
    }
    bool connected() const override { return attached; }
    std::uint64_t dropped() const override { return drops; }
    void acquire() override { ++acquires; }
    void release() override { ++releases; }

    bool                       attached = true;
    std::uint64_t              drops    = 0;
    int                        acquires = 0;
    int                        releases = 0;
    std::vector<DeviceMessage> input;    // scripted: what the device sent, drained oldest first
    std::size_t                next = 0;  // how much of it a node has drained
    std::vector<Out>           outputs;
};

}  // namespace rp::host::test
````

Create `packages/native/test/engine-graph/Surface.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// rp.launchpad.surface-in / -out, a Novation Launchpad as a control surface on nodes of its own
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 5): the device's MIDI drained from the host's surface link into the
// input node's `in`, a `connected` control output that follows the device, and what a session writes into the output
// node's `out` handed back to the link in the block it queued it. The nodes bind the link by name through
// rp.host.devices/1, as rp.n8.nes binds the cart's, so a host with no surface plans and runs the same document. Two
// nodes rather than one because a session is fed by the device and feeds it: one node would be a cycle the planner
// refuses, and breaking it on a feedback wire would deliver the LED stream a block late.
//
// The link here is stage 1's fake: what it was scripted to send, what a node handed it, and the nodes holding it.
// ProtocolNodes.test.cpp holds the session behind these nodes to the digests it sends through rp.host.controller-in and
// -out; these cases hold the nodes themselves, their acquire and release, the missing device, the uniqueness rule the
// types declare, and a warmed block's allocation count.
//
// Run via `pnpm test:plugin engine-graph`, or `build/bin/retroplug-engine-graph-test "[launchpad]"`.

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <iterator>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "../graph/CountingAllocator.hpp"
#include "FakeSurfaceLink.hpp"
#include "GraphDocs.hpp"
#include "NodeRig.hpp"
#include "graph/node.hpp"
#include "host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp"
#include "host/graph/LaunchpadNodes.hpp"

namespace {

using rp::host::kMaxDeviceMessage;
using rp::host::kSurfaceInBytes;
using rp::host::test::deviceMessage;
using rp::host::test::DocExtras;
using rp::host::test::docNode;
using rp::host::test::docWire;
using rp::host::test::FakeSurfaceLink;
using rp::host::test::Feed;
using rp::host::test::Message;
using rp::host::test::NodeRig;
using rp::host::test::Probe;
using Bytes = std::vector<std::uint8_t>;

constexpr double        kRate   = 48000.0;
constexpr std::uint32_t kFrames = 64;

void block(NodeRig& rig) { rig.host->processBlock(kFrames, rp_transport{kRate, 120.0, 0.0, 0}); }

// The plan the rig made, or the reasons it refused it.
void plan(NodeRig& rig, const std::string& document) {
    const auto r = rig.set(document);
    for (const auto& e : r.errors) UNSCOPED_INFO(e.code << " at " << e.nodeId << "." << e.port << ": " << e.message);
    REQUIRE(r.ok);
}

// Both surface nodes beside whatever a case adds, wired as the case's wires say: a case uses the input node's ports or
// the output node's, and the other runs with nothing wired to it.
std::string surfaceDocument(const std::vector<std::string>& nodes, const std::vector<std::string>& wires) {
    std::vector<std::string> all{docNode("surface-in", "rp.launchpad.surface-in"),
                                 docNode("surface-out", "rp.launchpad.surface-out")};
    all.insert(all.end(), nodes.begin(), nodes.end());
    return rp::host::test::docs_detail::document(all, wires);
}

std::string plainDocument(const std::vector<std::string>& nodes) {
    return rp::host::test::docs_detail::document(nodes, {});
}

// A node that writes the same two messages into its one output every block, from its own storage: a counted block
// must exercise the surface's out without a test node's own vectors freeing their payloads (Devices.test.cpp's probe
// pattern, cut to what a surface's out needs).
struct ScriptedOut {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.test.surface-out";
    struct { rp::events_out::sized<rp::capacity{.messages = 4, .bytes = 2048}> out; } outputs;

    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        static constexpr std::uint8_t kShort[] = {0xB0, 0x10, 0x7F};
        static const std::array<std::uint8_t, kMaxDeviceMessage> kWide = [] {
            std::array<std::uint8_t, kMaxDeviceMessage> bytes{};
            bytes.fill(0x22);
            return bytes;
        }();
        outputs.out.push(0, kShort);
        outputs.out.push(4, kWide);
    }
};

const rp_package* surfaceTestPackage() {
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<ScriptedOut>()};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.test.surface"})",
                                     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::size(kTypes)), kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

// The node type a package registers, so a case can read its descriptor without planning it.
const rp_node_type* type(const rp_package* package, const char* id) {
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < package->node_type_count; ++i)
        if (std::string(package->node_types[i]->id) == id) return package->node_types[i];
    return nullptr;
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("a surface's in carries what the device sent, in order, every message at frame 0", "[launchpad]") {
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    NodeRig         rig(kRate);
    rig.devices.install(nullptr, &surface);
    plan(rig, surfaceDocument({docNode("probe", "rp.test.probe")}, {docWire("surface-in.in", "probe.events")}));

    // More than one drain batch, and one message at the link's widest, so the node's drain loop and a full-size slot
    // are both exercised in one block. The device's traffic carries no frame of its own: every message lands at frame
    // 0, where rp.host.controller-in places the host's staged pad traffic.
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> wide(kMaxDeviceMessage, 0x5A);
    surface.input.push_back(deviceMessage(wide));
    for (int i = 0; i < 40; ++i)
        surface.input.push_back(deviceMessage({0x90, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(11 + i), 100}));
    block(rig);

    const std::vector<Message>& events = rig.node<Probe>("probe").events;
    REQUIRE(events.size() == surface.input.size());
    CHECK(events[0].data == wide);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < events.size(); ++i) {
        INFO("message " << i);
        CHECK(events[i].frame == 0);
        if (i > 0) CHECK(events[i].data == Bytes{0x90, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(10 + i), 100});
    }
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a surface's out reaches the link in queue order, and a detached link takes nothing", "[launchpad]") {
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    NodeRig         rig(kRate);
    rig.devices.install(nullptr, &surface);
    plan(rig, surfaceDocument({docNode("feed", "rp.test.feed")}, {docWire("feed.midi", "surface-out.out")}));

    Feed& feed = rig.node<Feed>("feed");
    feed.next[Feed::Midi] = {{0, {0xB0, 0x10, 0x7F}}, {9, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x01, 0xF7}}, {63, {0x90, 0x51, 0x00}}};
    block(rig);
    REQUIRE(surface.outputs.size() == 3);
    CHECK(Bytes(surface.outputs[0].data, surface.outputs[0].data + surface.outputs[0].size) == Bytes{0xB0, 0x10, 0x7F});
    CHECK(Bytes(surface.outputs[1].data, surface.outputs[1].data + surface.outputs[1].size) ==
          Bytes{0xF0, 0x7D, 0x01, 0xF7});
    CHECK(Bytes(surface.outputs[2].data, surface.outputs[2].data + surface.outputs[2].size) == Bytes{0x90, 0x51, 0x00});

    // Unplugged: the same messages go nowhere, and the link counts them itself - the node has nothing to send them to
    // but the link, so the count is the link's.
    surface.outputs.clear();
    surface.attached = false;
    feed.next[Feed::Midi] = {{0, {0x90, 0x51, 0x7F}}};
    block(rig);
    CHECK(surface.outputs.empty());
    CHECK(surface.dropped() == 1);
    CHECK(rig.host->faultCount() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a surface's connected follows the link, from frame 0", "[launchpad]") {
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    NodeRig         rig(kRate);
    rig.devices.install(nullptr, &surface);
    plan(rig, surfaceDocument({docNode("probe", "rp.test.probe")}, {docWire("surface-in.connected", "probe.control")}));
    surface.attached = false;
    block(rig);
    const Probe& probe = rig.node<Probe>("probe");
    CHECK(probe.controlStart == 0.0);
    CHECK(probe.controlChanges.empty());

    // Attached: the flag flips at frame 0 of that block, as rp.host.controller-in's does, so a session reading it
    // takes the device on the block it appears.
    surface.attached = true;
    block(rig);
    CHECK(probe.controlStart == 0.0);
    CHECK(probe.controlAtZero == 1.0);
    CHECK(probe.controlChanges == std::vector<double>{1.0});
    block(rig);  // held: no second change
    CHECK(probe.controlStart == 1.0);
    CHECK(probe.controlChanges.empty());

    surface.attached = false;
    block(rig);
    CHECK(probe.controlChanges == std::vector<double>{0.0});
}

TEST_CASE("the surface nodes in a host with no device plan and run with connected 0", "[launchpad]") {
    // The registry answers a name its host never installed with a handle that is never connected, so the same document
    // plans in the plugin, the CLI and every harness, and nothing needs a null check.
    NodeRig rig(kRate);  // no devices.install at all
    plan(rig, surfaceDocument({docNode("probe", "rp.test.probe")},
                              {docWire("surface-in.in", "probe.events"),
                               docWire("surface-in.connected", "probe.control")}));
    block(rig);
    CHECK(rig.node<Probe>("probe").events.empty());
    CHECK(rig.node<Probe>("probe").controlAtZero == 0.0);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 0);
    CHECK(rig.host->faultCount() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a surface's in drops what its queue has no room for, and counts it", "[launchpad]") {
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    NodeRig         rig(kRate);
    rig.devices.install(nullptr, &surface);
    plan(rig, surfaceDocument({docNode("probe", "rp.test.probe")}, {docWire("surface-in.in", "probe.events")}));

    // 1100 messages of 20 bytes against rp.launchpad.surface-in's 1024 messages and 16384 bytes: the byte bound binds
    // first, at 819 messages (16380 bytes), and the 281 the queue cannot hold are dropped and counted there. The link
    // is drained either way, so nothing accumulates behind a full queue.
    const Bytes twenty(20, 0x11);
    for (int i = 0; i < 1100; ++i) surface.input.push_back(deviceMessage(twenty));
    block(rig);
    const std::size_t held = kSurfaceInBytes / twenty.size();
    CHECK(held == 819);
    CHECK(rig.node<Probe>("probe").events.size() == held);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages("surface-in") == 1100 - held);

    // The next block starts afresh: the queue is emptied by the plan, and the link has nothing left to give.
    block(rig);
    CHECK(rig.node<Probe>("probe").events.empty());
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages("surface-in") == 1100 - held);
}

TEST_CASE("a plan holds one surface input node and one surface output node", "[launchpad]") {
    // One device, one link: a second input node would drain the one ring its twin drains (and the device would answer
    // two sessions), and a second output node would split the LED frames, so both types declare themselves unique and
    // the planner refuses the document.
    const rp_package* package = rp::host::launchpadPackage();
    const rp_node_type* surfaceIn = type(package, "rp.launchpad.surface-in");
    const rp_node_type* surfaceOut = type(package, "rp.launchpad.surface-out");
    REQUIRE(surfaceIn != nullptr);
    REQUIRE(surfaceOut != nullptr);
    for (const rp_node_type* t : {surfaceIn, surfaceOut}) {
        const std::string descriptor(t->descriptor(t));
        INFO(t->id);
        CHECK(descriptor.find(R"("unique":true)") != std::string::npos);
        CHECK(descriptor.find(R"("threads":true)") != std::string::npos);
    }
    // A type that declares neither spells neither.
    const rp_node_type* probeType = type(rp::host::test::testPackage(), "rp.test.probe");
    REQUIRE(probeType != nullptr);
    CHECK(std::string(probeType->descriptor(probeType)).find("unique") == std::string::npos);

    NodeRig rig(kRate);
    for (const char* id : {"rp.launchpad.surface-in", "rp.launchpad.surface-out"}) {
        INFO(id);
        const auto two = rig.set(plainDocument({docNode("one", id), docNode("two", id)}));
        REQUIRE_FALSE(two.ok);
        CHECK(two.errors.at(0).code == "unique");
        CHECK(two.errors.at(0).nodeId == "two");
        CHECK(two.errors.at(0).message.find(id) != std::string::npos);
    }

    // rp.n8.nes carries the same rule (the design's own device, placed by stage 5's setting), so a document that
    // drives the cart twice is refused for the same reason.
    const auto carts = rig.set(plainDocument({docNode("cart-a", "rp.n8.nes"), docNode("cart-b", "rp.n8.nes")}));
    REQUIRE_FALSE(carts.ok);
    CHECK(carts.errors.at(0).code == "unique");

    // One of each is the plan buildGraph makes when both settings are on.
    CHECK(rig.set(plainDocument({docNode("surface-in", "rp.launchpad.surface-in"),
                                 docNode("surface-out", "rp.launchpad.surface-out"), docNode("cart", "rp.n8.nes")}))
              .ok);
}

TEST_CASE("the surface types declare threads, so a target with none refuses them", "[launchpad]") {
    NodeRig pico(kRate, 8192, rp::graph::Target::Pico);
    for (const char* id : {"rp.launchpad.surface-in", "rp.launchpad.surface-out"}) {
        INFO(id);
        const auto refused = pico.set(plainDocument({docNode("surface", id)}));
        REQUIRE_FALSE(refused.ok);
        CHECK(refused.errors.at(0).code == "capability");
        CHECK(refused.errors.at(0).message.find("threads") != std::string::npos);
    }
}

TEST_CASE("the surface nodes take the link once each, keep it across a reactivate, and give it back once",
          "[launchpad]") {
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    NodeRig         rig(kRate);
    rig.devices.install(nullptr, &surface);
    plan(rig, surfaceDocument({}, {}));
    // Two nodes, two holds on the one link: the registry forwards every acquire a node makes, so an unbalanced one is
    // visible only here.
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 2);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 0);

    // A sample-rate change and a block growth each deactivate and activate every instance again
    // (GraphHost::reactivate). A node that already holds its handle keeps it, so neither takes the link again.
    std::string why;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->reactivate(44100.0, 8192, &why));
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 2);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 0);
    REQUIRE(rig.host->reactivate(44100.0, 16384, &why));
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 2);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 0);

    // The plan's reclaim runs both destructors, each giving its handle back once, and only once.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(plainDocument({})).ok);
    rig.host->reclaim();
    CHECK(surface.acquires == 2);
    CHECK(surface.releases == 2);
}

TEST_CASE("a warmed block of the surface nodes allocates and frees nothing", "[launchpad]") {
    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
    NodeRig         rig(kRate);
    std::string     why;
    REQUIRE(rig.registry.addPackage(surfaceTestPackage(), &why));
    rig.devices.install(nullptr, &surface);
    // A source writing the output node's out, so the counted block covers both halves of the link: the drain into the
    // input node's `in`, which no probe reads (a probe allocates its copies), and the hand-off of what the source
    // queued.
    plan(rig, surfaceDocument({docNode("out", ScriptedOut::id)}, {docWire("out.out", "surface-out.out")}));

    // Room for the block's work exists before the window: the fake's input and the slots it records in.
    surface.input = {deviceMessage({0x90, 0x51, 0x7F}), deviceMessage({0x90, 0x51, 0x00})};
    block(rig);
    REQUIRE(surface.outputs.size() == 2);
    surface.outputs.clear();
    surface.reserve(0, 2);
    surface.next = 0;
    surface.input = {deviceMessage({0x90, 0x51, 0x7F}), deviceMessage({0x90, 0x51, 0x00})};

    rp::test::beginCountingAllocations();
    block(rig);
    const auto counted = rp::test::endCountingAllocations();
    CHECK(counted.allocations == 0);
    CHECK(counted.frees == 0);
    CHECK(surface.outputs.size() == 2);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 0);
}
````

````diff
+// The same session driven through the host's controller nodes and through rp.launchpad.surface-in / -out, held
+// together: the recorded digests hold the host wiring, and the surface run is held to the same session behaviour -
+// every system input and every host MIDI message, block for block - and to the same LED and page stream, delivered in
+// the block the session sent it, since the link's two directions are two nodes and neither wire is a feedback wire.
+// So every value of the run matches, both digests included, and `outByBlock` shows it block by block.
+void throughSurface(ProtocolRig& host, ProtocolRig& viaSurface, const Sent& recorded) {
+    host.matches(recorded);
+    host.finish();
+    // The same device, the same pad stream in and the same LED stream out in the same block, so the surface run sends
+    // exactly what the host wiring sends: the digest folds in the host MIDI out and the controller out as well.
+    viaSurface.matches(recorded);
+    INFO("via the surface " << text(viaSurface.sent) << ", through the host " << text(host.sent));
+    CHECK(viaSurface.sent == host.sent);
+    REQUIRE(viaSurface.outByBlock.size() == host.outByBlock.size());
+    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < host.outByBlock.size(); ++i) {
+        INFO("block " << i);
+        CHECK(viaSurface.outByBlock[i] == host.outByBlock[i]);
+    }
+    viaSurface.finish();
````

- [ ] **Step 2: Add the two surface nodes and the `unique` flag**

`LaunchpadNodes.hpp/.cpp` hold a shared `SurfaceNode` base (bind, activate that keeps a handle it already holds,
destroy that releases once, the `fresh` flag) and the two types over it. `surface-in` drains in 16-message batches
until short, places every message at frame 0 and forwards nothing on its first block after binding; `surface-out`
pushes in queue order. `TypeDescriptor` gains `bool unique`, written only when set; `parseDescriptor` refuses anything
but true or absent; `node.hpp` gains `uniqueOf<T>()`; `Planner::structure` refuses a second node of a unique type with
code `unique`. `rp.n8.nes` sets it too, and `Engine.cpp` registers the package. TS's `defineNode` and
`TypeDescriptor.unique?: true` follow, emitted only when declared.

Create `packages/native/src/host/graph/LaunchpadNodes.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "host/graph/LaunchpadNodes.hpp"

#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <iterator>
#include <span>

#include "graph/node.hpp"
#include "host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp"
#include "host/graph/HostServices.hpp"

namespace rp::host {

namespace {

// The messages one drain hands back. The link keeps what a batch had no room for (it never drops on the consumer's
// behalf), so the node drains again until the link has nothing left, in its own storage: a block neither allocates nor
// grows the stack by the ring's whole depth.
constexpr std::size_t kSurfaceDrainBatch = 16;

// What both surface nodes share: the host's one surface link, borrowed for the life of the plan. It is acquired in
// activate, kept across a reactivate (activate runs again on the same instance, so a handle already held is not taken
// twice), and released in the destructor, the plan's reclaim, on the control thread. Placed by a setting rather than by
// the device's state, so both always activate: in a host with no surface, or with one unplugged, the link reads
// disconnected and takes every push nowhere, and nothing in the graph changes when the device comes or goes.
struct SurfaceNode {
    const HostDevices* devices = nullptr;
    SurfaceLink*       surface = nullptr;

    void bind_host(const rp_host* h) noexcept {
        devices = static_cast<const HostDevices*>(h->get_interface(h, RP_HOST_DEVICES_INTERFACE));
    }
    bool activate(double, std::uint32_t) {
        if (!devices) return false;
        if (!surface) surface = devices->acquireSurface(devices->ctx, kSurfaceDeviceName);
        return surface != nullptr;
    }
    ~SurfaceNode() {
        if (!devices || !surface) return;
        devices->releaseSurface(devices->ctx, surface);
    }
};

// The device's side of a controller session (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 5): what the Launchpad sent
// since the last block, and whether it is attached. It only ever reads the link, so a session reading it runs before
// the node that follows it, and the plan holds no cycle and no feedback wire.
struct SurfaceIn : SurfaceNode {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.launchpad.surface-in";
    static constexpr const char* name = "Launchpad In";
    static constexpr const char* category = "device";
    // The host's MIDI backend delivers on a callback thread of its own and the link sends on the main loop, so a target
    // with no threads (the Pico) refuses the type.
    static constexpr bool threads = true;
    // One device, one link: the planner refuses a second node of this type in a plan.
    static constexpr bool unique = true;

    // Named rather than spelled inline so the two ports below declare flush, as rp.host.controller-in's do.
    using InQueue = rp::events_out::sized<rp::capacity{.messages = kSurfaceInMessages, .bytes = kSurfaceInBytes}>;
    struct {
        InQueue         in;
        rp::control_out connected;
    } outputs;
    // What one drain returns, in the node's own storage.
    std::array<DeviceMessage, kSurfaceDrainBatch> batch{};

    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        // `connected` holds 1 or 0 from frame 0: a change at frame 0 on the block the flag flips, since a stream's
        // start value is the last block's end.
        const double flag = surface->connected() ? 1.0 : 0.0;
        if (flag != outputs.connected.queue->start) outputs.connected.push(0, flag);
        // What the device sent since the last drain goes into `in` at frame 0, as rp.host.controller-in places the pad
        // traffic the host stages. A message the queue has no room for is dropped and counted by the queue
        // (rp_queue::dropped), never allocated for, and the link stays drained either way: each call takes what it
        // answers, so a full batch means the ring may hold more.
        for (;;) {
            const std::size_t n = surface->drainInput(batch.data(), batch.size());
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                outputs.in.push(0, std::span<const std::uint8_t>(batch[i].data, batch[i].size));
            if (n < batch.size()) break;
        }
    }
};

// The session's side: everything it sends the device, handed over in queue order in the block it queued it.
struct SurfaceOut : SurfaceNode {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.launchpad.surface-out";
    static constexpr const char* name = "Launchpad Out";
    static constexpr const char* category = "device";
    // As the input node's: the host's MIDI backend delivers on a callback thread of its own and the link sends on the
    // main loop, so a target with no threads refuses both types.
    static constexpr bool threads = true;
    // As the input node's: two output nodes would split the device's LED frames.
    static constexpr bool unique = true;

    struct { rp::events_in out; } inputs;

    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        // The link owns the send ring, and counts (in dropped()) a push that went nowhere: nothing attached, or no room
        // left in its ring.
        for (const rp_message& m : inputs.out.messages()) {
            const auto data = inputs.out.data(m);
            surface->pushOutput(data.data(), data.size());
        }
    }
};

}  // namespace

const rp_package* launchpadPackage() {
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<SurfaceIn>(), rp::node_type<SurfaceOut>()};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.launchpad","version":"1.0.0"})",
                                     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::size(kTypes)), kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

}  // namespace rp::host
````

Create `packages/native/src/host/graph/LaunchpadNodes.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

#include "graph/rp_node.h"

namespace rp::host {

// The rp.launchpad package: a Novation Launchpad as a control surface on nodes of its own
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 5), through the host's surface link (rp.host.devices/1,
// "launchpad").
//
//   rp.launchpad.surface-in   in: the device's MIDI, drained from the link at the start of the block, each message at
//                             frame 0 (a control surface's timing is not musical, and this is where
//                             rp.host.controller-in places the pad traffic the host stages); connected: 1 while the
//                             device is attached, from frame 0 of the block, as rp.host.controller-in's is.
//   rp.launchpad.surface-out  out: every message handed to the link, in queue order, in the block it was queued.
//
// The two event ports are what a controller session reads and writes, so a session wired to these nodes runs as it
// does behind the host's controller nodes. Two nodes rather than one because a surface both feeds a session and
// follows it: one node with both directions would be a node-level cycle the planner refuses, and the only wire that
// breaks a cycle is a feedback wire, which delivers the block before. Split in two, every stream is in its own block
// and the plan holds no feedback wire.
//
// One device, one link: at most one node of either type per plan (the types are unique; the planner refuses a second).
// Two input nodes would drain the one receive ring between them, and two output nodes would split the device's LED
// frames, so the second is a refusal rather than a silently split stream.
const rp_package* launchpadPackage();

// rp.launchpad.surface-in's `in` output: a Launchpad's pad traffic and its replies, the same traffic and the same
// bound the control-surface input node has, so a session reads the same through either wiring.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kSurfaceInMessages = 1024;
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kSurfaceInBytes = 16384;

}  // namespace rp::host
````

````bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(launchpad): rp.launchpad.surface-in / -out, the control surface as nodes

The rp.launchpad package holds two node types over the host's one surface link (rp.host.devices/1,
"launchpad"), which is what a controller session needs, since it reads the device and writes to it.
rp.launchpad.surface-in drains the link into an `in` events output at the start of its block, each
message at frame 0, where rp.host.controller-in places the pad traffic the host stages, and follows the
device with a `connected` control output from frame 0; rp.launchpad.surface-out hands every message of
its `out` events input to the link's pushOutput in queue order, in the block it was queued. The event
ports are the shapes the controller session reads and writes, so a session wires to the nodes with no
adapter. Both declare threads (the MIDI backend's callback thread and the link's main-loop pump) and
both acquire the link in activate, keep it across a reactivate and release it in the plan's destroy.
The `in` queue is sized as the controller input node's, and a message past its messages or bytes bound
is dropped and counted by the queue, nothing allocated; the drain's own batch lives in the node, so a
block neither allocates nor grows the stack by the ring's depth.

Two nodes rather than one because a surface both feeds a session and follows it: one node with both
directions is a node-level cycle the planner refuses, and the only wire that breaks a cycle is a
feedback wire, which delivers the block before. That would put the LED and page stream one block late
and leave the last block's LEDs in the front at teardown, and it would make the recorded session
digests, which fold the controller-out stream in, unreachable from a surface document without a
feedback flag on a device sink. Split in two, every stream is in its own block and no document carries
a feedback wire.

A node type can now declare itself unique. The descriptor carries `unique` only when a type sets it,
the planner refuses a second node of such a type in a plan, and both the C++ authoring layer and TS's
defineNode carry the flag. Both surface types and rp.n8.nes set it (one device, one link: two inputs
would drain the one receive ring between them and two outputs would split the LED frames; the second
gains the rule stage 3's report asked for), which puts the rule in the planner rather than another
type name in Engine.cpp. An existing descriptor cannot spell `false` for it: parseDescriptor refuses
anything but true or absent, matching defineNode and keeping descriptorJson(parseDescriptor(x)) == x.
The engine's own checks for the host I/O nodes and the cart mirror stay until the deletions stage.

The protocol node suite runs its three controller cases a second time with the session wired to the
two surface nodes over a fake link fed the same traffic, the rewired document built from buildGraph's
role goldens with no golden re-recorded. With no cycle and no feedback wire the surface run reproduces
the recorded `Sent` in full, block for block: every system input, every host MIDI out message, the LED
and page stream, and the digest over all of them. The rig records that stream as the output node hands
it to the link, which is the same thing rp.host.controller-out's sink records, so a device that is not
attached does not hide what the session sent. That answers the design's last prototype question: the
digest does stay identical through the surface, and stage 5's wiring is the 1:1 rename of the host's
two controller nodes.

The surface cases split along the ports they use and add the nodes' one lifetime claim: two acquires
at the plan, none on a sample-rate change or a block growth, two releases at the reclaim. A detached
push is now counted by the real link and by a host with no device, and SurfaceLink exposes the count as
dropped() the way CartLink does, so the tests assert the number a node would read.
EOF
````

### Task 5: the TS switch-over: placement, fan-out, stage-to-a-node and the cart menu

Design section 8 item 5, and section 9's third, fourth and fifth questions. This stage stops using the old engine
paths; Task 6 deletes them. `buildGraph` places one `rp.n8.nes` for the first NES in slot order whose `driveRealCart`
setting is on (the setting is a NES role field, additive and default ON, so a saved project keeps its behaviour), wires
it from the same protocol-node outputs that feed that system's `midi` and `bytes`, carries the system's expansion
volume as its param, and stops placing `rp.n8.cart-mirror`. The controller session reads and writes the two surface
nodes, which are placed whenever the controller setting is on and neither when it is off. Staging addresses a node:
`backend.stageNodeMidi(nodeId, bytes)` rides the ring as an owning payload and at the drain asks the running plan's node
for `rp.stage/1`. The UI's cart menu submits `rom.upload`, `sram.dump` and `sram.restore` against the driven cart's
node, with progress, the busy rows and the refusal text. The hosts stop installing the core byte sink and the raw-MIDI
fallbacks, the SDL stops staging controller traffic, and the harness seam becomes `HarnessSurfaceLink`. The role goldens
are re-recorded here, and only here; parity is never re-recorded.

````cpp
// Staging a message at ONE node of the running graph (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 4): the command
// names a node by the id its document gives it, and the engine hands the bytes to the node the plan RUNNING at that
// point of the drain places under it, through rp.stage/1 - a system node's core ingress, a device node's device. So the
// UI's settings message reaches the cart whose menu it is whatever the project's musical routing does with channels,
// and the engine reads no node's type: it asks by an interface id and never by a type name.
//
// What is held here is the delivery: the emulated NES's core accepts the bytes the engine stages at its node, the fake
// cart records the push a stage at its node makes (at frame 0, with the block's rate), an id the running plan does not
// place takes nothing, and the id resolves against the plan that runs rather than the one that ran when the command was
// pushed. The RPC that pushes one is the TS harness's (test-native/stage-node-midi.test.ts, end to end).
//
// Run via `pnpm test:plugin engine-graph`, or `build/bin/retroplug-engine-graph-test "[stage]"`.

#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "GraphDocs.hpp"
#include "NodeRig.hpp"
#include "host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp"
#include "host/engine/Engine.hpp"
#include "host/engine/EngineInvoker.hpp"
#include "host/graph/HostIoNodes.hpp"
#include "host/graph/N8Nodes.hpp"
#include "system/mesen/MesenNesSystem.hpp"

namespace {

using rp::host::test::docNode;
using rp::host::test::DocExtras;
using rp::host::test::DocSystem;
using rp::host::test::docWire;
using rp::host::test::graphRequest;
using rp::host::test::kNesType;
using rp::host::test::stereoDocument;
using Bytes = std::vector<std::uint8_t>;

constexpr double kRate = 48000.0;

// A cart link that records what reaches the device: a stage at the cart's node is one push.
class FakeCart final : public rp::host::CartLink {
public:
    struct Push {
        std::uint32_t frame = 0;
        bool          flush = false;
        double        rate  = 0.0;
        Bytes         data;
    };
    void push(std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, bool flush, double rate) override {
        pushes.push_back({frame, flush, rate, Bytes(data, data + size)});
    }
    bool          connected() const override { return true; }
    std::uint64_t dropped() const override { return 0; }
    void          setExpansionVolume(int) override {}

    std::vector<Push> pushes;
};

// The document: a NES at sys-1 and, unless `cart` is false, an rp.n8.nes at `cart`, with nothing wired between them
// (a stage needs no wire at all: that is the point of it).
Engine::GraphRequest document(std::vector<DocSystem>& systems, bool cart = true) {
    DocExtras extras{};
    if (cart) extras.nodes.push_back(docNode("cart", "rp.n8.nes"));
    extras.nodes.push_back(docNode("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in"));
    return graphRequest(stereoDocument(systems, extras), {1});
}

// A settings SysEx, longer than four bytes: the shape the UI's rows send, and the one the ring carries as an owning
// payload.
const Bytes kSysEx{0xF0, 0x7D, 0x42, 0x03, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0xF7};

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("a staged message reaches the node the running plan places under its id", "[engine-graph][stage]") {
    FakeCart         cart;
    Engine           e(kRate);
    QueuedInvoker    invoker{e};
    rp::host::test::Roms roms;
    std::vector<DocSystem> systems{{1, kNesType}};
    rp::host::test::withRoms(e, systems, roms);
    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, nullptr);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(document(systems)).ok);

    // The cart's node: the link records the message as a frame-0 push at the engine's rate, exactly as its `midi` input
    // would have carried it in the block.
    invoker.stageNodeMidi("cart", kSysEx);
    invoker.drainInto(e);
    REQUIRE(cart.pushes.size() == 1);
    CHECK(cart.pushes[0].frame == 0);
    CHECK(cart.pushes[0].data == kSysEx);
    CHECK_FALSE(cart.pushes[0].flush);
    CHECK(cart.pushes[0].rate == kRate);

    // The system's node: the emulated NES's FIFO ingress accepts the same bytes, uncapped, as the engine's per-system
    // staging did (rp.stage/1's other implementation).
    auto* core = static_cast<MesenNesSystem*>(e.findSystem(1));
    REQUIRE(core != nullptr);
    const std::uint64_t accepted = core->acceptedBytes();
    invoker.stageNodeMidi("sys-1", kSysEx);
    invoker.drainInto(e);
    CHECK(core->acceptedBytes() - accepted == kSysEx.size());
    CHECK(cart.pushes.size() == 1);  // the system's node is not the cart's

    // An id the running plan does not place takes nothing, and neither does a node whose type stages nothing (the host's
    // MIDI input answers no rp.stage/1). Both are silent: the command's contract is optimistic, like pressButton's.
    invoker.stageNodeMidi("nope", kSysEx);
    invoker.stageNodeMidi("midi-in", kSysEx);
    invoker.drainInto(e);
    CHECK(cart.pushes.size() == 1);
    CHECK(core->acceptedBytes() - accepted == kSysEx.size());

    // An empty message is refused before it is ever pushed (`EngineRpcService::stageNodeMidi` refuses it the same way).
    invoker.stageNodeMidi("cart", {});
    invoker.drainInto(e);
    CHECK(cart.pushes.size() == 1);
    CHECK(e.faultCount() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a node the plan adds later under the same id takes a stored message", "[engine-graph][stage]") {
    FakeCart                cart;
    Engine                  e(kRate);
    QueuedInvoker           invoker{e};
    rp::host::test::Roms    roms;
    std::vector<DocSystem>  systems{{1, kNesType}};
    rp::host::test::withRoms(e, systems, roms);
    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, nullptr);
    // A plan with no cart: staging at "cart" has nowhere to go.
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(document(systems, false)).ok);
    invoker.stageNodeMidi("cart", kSysEx);
    invoker.drainInto(e);
    CHECK(cart.pushes.empty());
    // The cart's node from here on, under the same id: the same command lands, so the id is resolved at the drain.
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(document(systems, true)).ok);
    invoker.stageNodeMidi("cart", kSysEx);
    invoker.drainInto(e);
    REQUIRE(cart.pushes.size() == 1);
    CHECK(cart.pushes[0].data == kSysEx);
    CHECK(e.faultCount() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a staged id resolves against the plan that runs, not the one that ran when it was pushed",
          "[engine-graph][stage]") {
    FakeCart                cart;
    Engine                  e(kRate);
    QueuedInvoker           invoker{e};
    rp::host::test::Roms    roms;
    std::vector<DocSystem>  systems{{1, kNesType}};
    rp::host::test::withRoms(e, systems, roms);
    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, nullptr);
    // The plan that runs places the cart's node.
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(document(systems, true)).ok);
    // The audio thread owns the drain, so nothing applies inline: the swap and the message wait in the ring.
    invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    // A plan without the cart is published while the old one still runs, then the message is staged: the swap is
    // ahead of it, so at the push "cart" IS a node of the plan that runs and at the drain it no longer is. The id is
    // resolved there, against the plan just adopted, so the node that ran when the command was pushed takes nothing.
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(document(systems, false)).ok);
    invoker.stageNodeMidi("cart", kSysEx);
    invoker.drainInto(e);
    CHECK(cart.pushes.empty());
    CHECK(e.faultCount() == 0);
    invoker.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/stage-node-midi.test.ts`:

````ts
// backend.stageNodeMidi - control MIDI aimed at ONE node of the document, delivered straight to its core's
// ingress and NEVER through the routing node.
//
// The bypass IS the feature, so that is what this proves rather than mere delivery. Two identical BlipToaster
// carts boot side by side; a theme CC goes to the first only; the first's screen changes and the second's does
// not. Through the musical path neither outcome would hold: the project's default routing is `sendToAll` (both
// carts would change), and CC 16 is global on the cart (any channel), so no channel trick could have separated
// them either. That leaves the direct ingress as the only way a UI knob can address the cart whose menu it is.
//
// Runs on the real Mesen core through the real backend, and SKIPS when the BlipToaster ROM isn't built.
import { test, expect, skip } from "../testing/harness";
import { createRealBackend } from "../src/realBackend";
import { createAudioDriver } from "../src/audioDriver";
import { directGraph } from "../src/graph/directGraph";

// Structure for this file's directly built systems (docs/modular-graph-phase-b2-design.md section 2.4).
const graph = directGraph();

declare const __REPO_RESOURCES_DIR__: string;
const ROM = __REPO_RESOURCES_DIR__ + "/roms/bliptoaster.nes";
// The cart's rig message (F0 7D 42 03 …): baseCh, ppu, curve, theme, font. Channel-less BY DESIGN, so no
// channel trick could have separated two instances - only the per-system inject can.
const sxSettings = (theme: number): number[] => [0xf0, 0x7d, 0x42, 0x03, 0, 1, 0, theme, 0, 0xf7];

/** The cart polls its FIFO from the main loop, and boots for ~1s before it gets there. */
const WARMUP_MS = 1300;

function framePixels(be: ReturnType<typeof createRealBackend>, id: number): Uint8Array | null {
  const f = be.getFrame(id);
  return f ? new Uint8Array(f.pixels) : null;
}
const same = (a: Uint8Array, b: Uint8Array): boolean => {
  if (a.length !== b.length) return false;
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) if (a[i] !== b[i]) return false;
  return true;
};

test("stageNodeMidi reaches the system node it names, and only that one", () => {
  const be = createRealBackend();
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  if (!be.fileExists(ROM)) skip(`stageNodeMidi: no ROM at ${ROM}`);
  const spec = { romPath: ROM, platform: "nes" as const, core: "mesen" as const, embeddedRom: "", savPath: null, statePath: null };
  expect(graph.add(spec, 1)).toBeTruthy();
  expect(graph.add(spec, 2)).toBeTruthy();

  // Same ROM, same start, no input: the two cores run in lockstep, so any later difference is the message's doing.
  audio.renderAudio(WARMUP_MS);
  const before1 = framePixels(be, 1)!;
  const before2 = framePixels(be, 2)!;
  expect(before1.length > 0).toBeTruthy();
  expect(same(before1, before2)).toBeTruthy();

  // Theme 9 (MONO) on instance 1 only. Accepted optimistically - it is queued to the audio thread. Ten bytes,
  // so this also covers the OWNING-payload half of the command: a rig block does not fit inline.
  expect(be.stageNodeMidi("sys-1", sxSettings(9))).toBeTruthy();
  audio.renderAudio(400);

  const after1 = framePixels(be, 1)!;
  const after2 = framePixels(be, 2)!;
  expect(same(after1, before1)).toBe(false); // it landed: instance 1 repainted in the new theme
  expect(same(after2, before2)).toBeTruthy(); // and stayed off instance 2 entirely
  console.log(`[stageNodeMidi] rig SysEx (theme 9) changed instance 1's screen, left instance 2 byte-identical`);

  // The one guard left: nothing to deliver. There is no upper bound any more - the raw ingress has no cap,
  // which is the whole reason a SysEx can get through at all.
  expect(be.stageNodeMidi("sys-1", [])).toBe(false);
  expect(be.stageNodeMidi("sys-4242", sxSettings(3))).toBeTruthy(); // queued optimistically; no such node
  // The cart node the document places for system 1 (its "drive the real cart" setting defaults on) takes the same
  // message: with no cart attached in this host the link drops it, which is a device's business, not the node's.
  expect(be.stageNodeMidi("cart-1", sxSettings(3))).toBeTruthy();

  graph.remove(1);
  graph.remove(2);
});
````

````diff
+TEST_CASE("a surface's in discards what the link held when it bound it, and a reactivate keeps delivering",
+          "[launchpad]") {
+    FakeSurfaceLink surface;
+    NodeRig         rig(kRate);
+    rig.devices.install(nullptr, &surface);
+    // Presses sent while no node read the device wait in the link (a project with the controller off drains nothing):
+    // a session that starts now would replay them, so the node's first block drains the link and forwards none of it.
+    surface.input.push_back(deviceMessage({0x90, 0x33, 100}));
+    plan(rig, surfaceDocument({docNode("probe", "rp.test.probe")}, {docWire("surface-in.in", "probe.events")}));
+    block(rig);
+    CHECK(rig.node<Probe>("probe").events.empty());
+    // Drained, not kept: the block after has nothing to deliver either.
+    block(rig);
+    CHECK(rig.node<Probe>("probe").events.empty());
+    // A press after the first block is delivered, as every one after it is.
+    surface.input.push_back(deviceMessage({0x90, 0x34, 100}));
+    block(rig);
+    REQUIRE(rig.node<Probe>("probe").events.size() == 1);
+    CHECK(rig.node<Probe>("probe").events[0].data == Bytes{0x90, 0x34, 100});
+    // A reactivate that keeps the handle (the new rate and size a sample-rate change re-plans for) is not a first
+    // block: the instance already read the link before and after it, so what arrived is delivered.
+    surface.input.push_back(deviceMessage({0x90, 0x35, 100}));
+    std::string why;
+    REQUIRE(rig.host->reactivate(kRate, 8192, &why));
+    CHECK(surface.acquires == 2);  // the handle it bound is the one it keeps
+    block(rig);
+    REQUIRE(rig.node<Probe>("probe").events.size() == 1);
+    CHECK(rig.node<Probe>("probe").events[0].data == Bytes{0x90, 0x35, 100});
+    CHECK(rig.host->faultCount() == 0);
+}
````
