-// backend.stageSystemMidi — control MIDI aimed at ONE system, delivered straight to its ingress and NEVER
-// through the routing node.
-//
-// The bypass IS the feature, so that is what this proves rather than mere delivery. Two identical BlipToaster
-// carts boot side by side; a theme CC goes to the first only; the first's screen changes and the second's does
-// not. Through the musical path neither outcome would hold: the project's default routing is `sendToAll` (both
-// carts would change), and CC 16 is global on the cart (any channel), so no channel trick could have separated
-// them either. That leaves the direct ingress as the only way a UI knob can address the cart whose menu it is.
-//
-// Runs on the real Mesen core through the real backend, and SKIPS when the BlipToaster ROM isn't built.
-import { test, expect, skip } from "../testing/harness";
-import { createRealBackend } from "../src/realBackend";
-import { createAudioDriver } from "../src/audioDriver";
-import { directGraph } from "../src/graph/directGraph";
-
-// Structure for this file's directly built systems (docs/modular-graph-phase-b2-design.md section 2.4).
-const graph = directGraph();
-
-declare const __REPO_RESOURCES_DIR__: string;
-const ROM = __REPO_RESOURCES_DIR__ + "/roms/bliptoaster.nes";
-// The cart's rig message (F0 7D 42 03 …): baseCh, ppu, curve, theme, font. Channel-less BY DESIGN, so no
-// channel trick could have separated two instances - only the per-system inject can.
-const sxSettings = (theme: number): number[] => [0xf0, 0x7d, 0x42, 0x03, 0, 1, 0, theme, 0, 0xf7];
-
-/** The cart polls its FIFO from the main loop, and boots for ~1s before it gets there. */
-const WARMUP_MS = 1300;
-
-function framePixels(be: ReturnType<typeof createRealBackend>, id: number): Uint8Array | null {
-  const f = be.getFrame(id);
-  return f ? new Uint8Array(f.pixels) : null;
-}
-const same = (a: Uint8Array, b: Uint8Array): boolean => {
-  if (a.length !== b.length) return false;
-  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) if (a[i] !== b[i]) return false;
-  return true;
-};
-
-test("stageSystemMidi reaches the system it names, and only that one", () => {
-  const be = createRealBackend();
-  const audio = createAudioDriver();
-  if (!be.fileExists(ROM)) skip(`stageSystemMidi: no ROM at ${ROM}`);
-  const spec = { romPath: ROM, platform: "nes" as const, core: "mesen" as const, embeddedRom: "", savPath: null, statePath: null };
-  expect(graph.add(spec, 1)).toBeTruthy();
-  expect(graph.add(spec, 2)).toBeTruthy();
-
-  // Same ROM, same start, no input: the two cores run in lockstep, so any later difference is the message's doing.
-  audio.renderAudio(WARMUP_MS);
-  const before1 = framePixels(be, 1)!;
-  const before2 = framePixels(be, 2)!;
-  expect(before1.length > 0).toBeTruthy();
-  expect(same(before1, before2)).toBeTruthy();
-
-  // Theme 9 (MONO) on instance 1 only. Accepted optimistically - it is queued to the audio thread. Ten bytes,
-  // so this also covers the OWNING-payload half of the command: a rig block does not fit inline.
-  expect(be.stageSystemMidi(1, sxSettings(9))).toBeTruthy();
-  audio.renderAudio(400);
-
-  const after1 = framePixels(be, 1)!;
-  const after2 = framePixels(be, 2)!;
-  expect(same(after1, before1)).toBe(false); // it landed: instance 1 repainted in the new theme
-  expect(same(after2, before2)).toBeTruthy(); // and stayed off instance 2 entirely
-  console.log(`[stageSystemMidi] rig SysEx (theme 9) changed instance 1's screen, left instance 2 byte-identical`);
-
-  // The one guard left: nothing to deliver. There is no upper bound any more - the raw ingress has no cap,
-  // which is the whole reason a SysEx can get through at all.
-  expect(be.stageSystemMidi(1, [])).toBe(false);
-  expect(be.stageSystemMidi(0xdead, sxSettings(3))).toBeTruthy(); // queued optimistically; no such system
-
-  graph.remove(1);
-  graph.remove(2);
-});

+test("driving a real cart is placement, not a knob: its edit publishes the document and moves the cart node", () => {
+  const { be, p, sys } = project();
+  const a = sys.addSystem("/roms/a.gb")!;
+  const c = sys.addSystem("/roms/c.nes")!;
+  // A NES drives the cart by default: buildGraph places its rp.n8.nes, fed from the same protocol nodes its core is.
+  expect(be.graphNode(`cart-${c}`)?.type).toBe("rp.n8.nes");
+  const n = be.graphRequests.length;
+  const publishes = countPublishes(p.graph);
+  expect(sys.setRoleConfig(c, "mesen", { driveRealCart: false })).toBe(true);
+  // A document of its own, not a live param: nothing is set on a node, the graph is republished.
+  expect(since(be, n).length).toBe(1);
+  expect(publishes.n).toBe(1);
+  expect(be.graphNode(`cart-${c}`)).toBe(undefined);
+  expect(be.lastDocument()!.wires.some((w) => w.to.startsWith(`cart-${c}`))).toBe(false);
+  // The emulated node stays and keeps its own wiring (a "real cart only" system is later work).
+  expect(be.graphNode(`sys-${c}`)?.type).toBe("rp.mesen.nes");
+  // An expansion-volume edit now reaches only the emulated node: no cart node is placed, so none is set (the shared
+  // predicate gates both the placement and the live copy).
+  const calls = be.paramCalls.length;
+  expect(sys.setRoleConfig(c, "mesen", { expansionVolume: 30 })).toBe(true);
+  expect(be.paramCalls.slice(calls)).toEqual([{ nodeId: `sys-${c}`, paramId: "expansionVolume", value: 30 }]);
+  // Back on: the node returns, and nothing is set live by either edit.
+  expect(sys.setRoleConfig(c, "mesen", { driveRealCart: true })).toBe(true);
+  expect(be.graphNode(`cart-${c}`)?.type).toBe("rp.n8.nes");
+  expect(a).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+});
+

Expected: the TS tests fail before this stage's implementation: `driveRealCart`, the cart placement and fan-out and the surface wiring are absent from `buildGraph`, `stageNodeMidi` is absent from the backend, and the mock backend does not model the cart. Report the failures this tree prints.

- [ ] **Step 2: Add `rp.stage/1` and the native staging**

`HostServices.hpp` gains `RP_STAGE_INTERFACE "rp.stage/1"`; `GraphHost::runningNode(id)` answers the plan the drain
last adopted (only the draining thread writes it). `DspCommand` gains `StageNodeMidi` with an owning
`StagedNodeMessage`, `EngineInvoker::stageNodeMidi` queues it, and `Engine::stageNodeMidi` resolves the id against the
running plan, asks the node for `rp.stage/1` and hands it the bytes. The system node reproduces `stageSystemMidi`'s
body (raw `pushCoreBytes` where the core has one, the framed door otherwise, uncapped bytes refused); the cart node
pushes at frame 0 with the block's rate and its note bookkeeping. `EngineRpcService` and the registration expose
`stageNodeMidi`; `stageControllerIn` and `renderBlocks`' controller field stage into `HarnessSurfaceLink` (new: an
SPSC ring, position 0, `connected()` false, pushes counted not stored), and a harness host with none refuses.
`src/main.cpp` installs the harness link before the engine.

Create `packages/native/src/host/rpc/HarnessSurfaceLink.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The control surface a headless host stages into: a SurfaceLink with no device behind it, so the RPC harness can drive
// a controller session with no Launchpad attached (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 5). The plugin and the
// SDL standalone install their real links on the engine; the test host (src/main.cpp, retroplug-host) installs this one
// instead, so stageControllerIn and renderBlocks' controller field still put a pad press where a session reads it,
// now through the surface nodes the document places rather than through an engine-owned staging arena.
//
// Nothing is ever connected, so a session runs unattached exactly as it did when the harness staged into that arena
// (it decodes presses and sends its LED diff, without the Programmer-mode handshake a link first reporting one brings).
// What the session sends back is counted, not stored: no headless test reads a Launchpad's LED stream, and counting
// keeps pushOutput allocation-free as a link's must be.

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <span>

#include "transport/SpscRing.hpp"
#include "host/devices/DeviceLinks.hpp"

namespace rp::host {

class HarnessSurfaceLink final : public SurfaceLink {
public:
    // The messages one host may stage before a block drains them, and the bytes each may hold: the node's own drain
    // batch and the message bound (kMaxDeviceMessage) are what a real link's ring holds too.
    static constexpr std::size_t kStagedMessages = 256;

    // [control] Stage one message as the device would have sent it, at frame 0 of the next block. False (and the
    // message dropped, and counted in dropped()) for an empty one, one wider than kMaxDeviceMessage, or a full ring.
    bool queueInput(std::span<const std::uint8_t> bytes) {
        if (bytes.empty() || bytes.size() > kMaxDeviceMessage) return false;
        DeviceMessage m;
        m.size = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(bytes.size());
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < bytes.size(); ++i) m.data[i] = bytes[i];
        if (staged_.tryPush(m)) return true;
        dropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        return false;
    }

    // [control] Discard everything waiting: a render run starts from an empty ring, so a press staged by an earlier run
    // (or with no surface node in the plan to read it) is never replayed as one this run's session pressed.
    void clearInput() {
        DeviceMessage m;
        while (staged_.tryPop(m)) {
        }
    }

    // ---- SurfaceLink ----
    std::size_t drainInput(DeviceMessage* out, std::size_t capacity) override {
        std::size_t n = 0;
        while (n < capacity && staged_.tryPop(out[n])) ++n;
        return n;
    }
    void pushOutput(const std::uint8_t* /*data*/, std::size_t /*size*/) override {
        pushed_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    bool connected() const override { return false; }
    // As a real link's: the messages this one had no room for (queueInput's return value is the caller's too).
    std::uint64_t dropped() const override { return dropped_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }

    // How many messages the session has sent the device since the link was made: a test's proof that the wiring reaches
    // the surface at all, without storing LED frames nothing reads.
    std::uint64_t pushed() const { return pushed_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }

private:
    SpscRing<DeviceMessage, kStagedMessages> staged_;
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t>                          pushed_{0};
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t>                          dropped_{0};
};

}  // namespace rp::host
````

- [ ] **Step 3: Place the hardware, wire the surface, stage at nodes**

`coreRoles.ts` gains `driveRealCart: boolField(true)`; `buildGraph.ts` gains `cartNodeId`, `drivesRealCartOf`, the
cart placement and fan-out, the `rp.n8.cart-mirror` removal and the session wired to `surface-in.in` /
`surface-in.connected` / `surface-out.out` with both surface nodes placed only when the controller is on.
`systemsStore.ts` publishes a document when `driveRealCart` moves and copies a live `expansionVolume` edit to the cart
node. `backend.ts`, `realBackend.ts` and `cli/sdk-types.d.ts` carry `stageNodeMidi` (the mock backend's copy landed
with the tests). The menu gains Drive Real Cart, the cart rows over capability jobs and the busy and progress state;
`n8SdOps.ts`, `useN8SdWatch.ts` and `n8Devices.ts` move onto it; `App.tsx` stops pushing the volume. The plugin and
SDL stop installing the byte sink and the raw fallbacks, the SDL stops per-block controller staging and draining, and
`HostServices.hpp`'s staging comment says the engine asks the node the running plan places under the id.

- [ ] **Step 4: Re-record the goldens, here and nowhere else**

The role goldens' documents move with the surface nodes and the cart, and their digests do not; the B1 file's
documents move the same way, and no test writes that file once the B1 translator is gone. This step re-records both,
here and nowhere else, with the small tool below: its `rewrite` maps each of the B1 file's 840 case models through
this tree's `buildGraph` and deduplicates the documents in first-seen order, which is the procedure that file's header
gives and what B3a, B3b, C2 and C3 did, and its `compare` prints what moved and holds everything else still. The role

````ts
// C5's golden tooling. `rewrite <build-graph.json>` re-records the B1 golden file's documents by mapping each case's
// model through buildGraph, the procedure build-graph-goldens.test.ts's header gives: the model already carries the
// platform, the ROM resource and its name C3 added, and C5 adds nothing to a model (a NES's "drive the real cart"
// setting rides inside the core config the model already has), so the documents are simply rebuilt and deduplicated in
// first-seen order. This file only writes build-graph.json: the role goldens' cases carry core configs their role
// schema fills, and their own test re-records them (`RP_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1 pnpm test graph/build-graph-role-goldens`).
// `compare <old> <new>` holds every case of the new file to the old one by name: the same slots and tap, the models the
// same but for the "drive the real cart" the role schema now defaults, and the documents differing only in the moves
// C5 makes - the host controller pair leaves (a controller's session reads and writes surface-in / surface-out
// instead, and no controller means no surface node at all), the plan-level cart mirror becomes a NES's rp.n8.nes
// named cart-<id>, and the wires into and out of them follow - then "nothing else moved".
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import {
  buildGraph,
  type GraphModel,
} from "@REPO@/packages/retroplug/src/graph/buildGraph";
import { canonicalJson } from
  "@REPO@/packages/retroplug/src/graph/canonicalJson";

type Node = { id: string; type: string; settings?: Record<string, unknown>; params?: Record<string, unknown> };
type Doc = { nodes: Node[]; wires: { from: string; to: string }[] };
type System = { id: number; type: string; coreConfig?: Record<string, unknown> };
type Case = { name: string; model: GraphModel; document: number; slots: number[]; tapArm: unknown };
type File = { documents: Doc[]; cases: Case[] };

const read = (path: string): File => JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"));

function rewrite(path: string): void {
  const file = read(path);
  const documents: string[] = [];
  const index = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const c of file.cases) {
    const built = buildGraph(c.model);
    const doc = canonicalJson(built.document);
    if (!index.has(doc)) {
      index.set(doc, documents.length);
      documents.push(doc);
    }
    c.document = index.get(doc) as number;
    c.slots = built.slots as number[];
    c.tapArm = built.tapArm;
  }
  const cases = file.cases.map((c) => canonicalJson(c));
  writeFileSync(path, `{"documents":[\n${documents.join(",\n")}\n],"cases":[\n${cases.join(",\n")}\n]}\n`);
  console.log(`rewrote ${documents.length} documents of ${file.cases.length} cases in ${path}`);
}

// The wire ends the two host controller nodes had, as the surface nodes the session reads and writes: the input pair
// keeps its name, the output node is the session's one output.
const REWIRED: Record<string, string> = {
  "controller-in.midi": "surface-in.in",
  "controller-in.connected": "surface-in.connected",
  "controller-out.midi": "surface-out.out",
};

function compare(oldPath: string, newPath: string): void {
  const before = read(oldPath);
  const after = read(newPath);
  const problems: string[] = [];
  let changedDocs = 0;
  let movedIndices = 0;
  let pairs = 0;
  let carts = 0;
  let surfaces = 0;
  let rewired = 0;
  // What the model carries beyond the "drive the real cart" the role schema now defaults on every mesen config: that
  // field alone may appear, and nothing else may move.
  const stripModel = (m: GraphModel) => ({
    ...m,
    systems: (m.systems as unknown as System[]).map((s) => {
      if (s.coreConfig === undefined) return s;
      const { driveRealCart: _d, ...core } = s.coreConfig;
      return Object.keys(core).length > 0 ? { ...s, coreConfig: core } : { ...s, coreConfig: undefined };
    }),
  });
  const byName = (f: File, name: string) => f.cases.find((c) => c.name === name);
  const names = new Set([...before.cases.map((c) => c.name), ...after.cases.map((c) => c.name)]);
  for (const name of names) {
    const o = byName(before, name);
    const n = byName(after, name);
    if (!o || !n) {
      problems.push(`${name}: only in ${o ? "old" : "new"}`);
      continue;
    }
    if (canonicalJson(stripModel(o.model)) !== canonicalJson(stripModel(n.model))) {
      problems.push(`${name}: the model moved beyond the cart setting`);
    }
    if (canonicalJson(o.slots) !== canonicalJson(n.slots) || canonicalJson(o.tapArm) !== canonicalJson(n.tapArm)) {
      problems.push(`${name}: slots or tap moved`);
    }
    if (o.document !== n.document) movedIndices++;
    const od = before.documents[o.document];
    const nd = after.documents[n.document];
    const systems = (n.model.systems ?? []) as unknown as System[];
    const hasController = (n.model as { controller?: unknown }).controller !== null &&
      (n.model as { controller?: unknown }).controller !== undefined;
    const cartOf = (system: number) => systems.find((s) => s.id === system);
    // The nodes the old document's, with C5's moves applied: the host pair becomes the surface nodes when a controller
    // is on (and is gone when it is not), and the cart mirror becomes the NES's node named cart-<system>.
    const expected: Node[] = [];
    for (const node of od.nodes) {
      if (node.type === "rp.host.controller-in") {
        if (hasController) expected.push({ id: "surface-in", type: "rp.launchpad.surface-in" });
        continue;
      }
      if (node.type === "rp.host.controller-out") {
        if (hasController) expected.push({ id: "surface-out", type: "rp.launchpad.surface-out" });
        continue;
      }
      if (node.type === "rp.n8.cart-mirror") {
        const system = node.settings?.system as number;
        const cart = cartOf(system);
        const volume = cart?.coreConfig?.expansionVolume;
        const params = typeof volume === "number" && Number.isFinite(volume) ? { expansionVolume: volume } : undefined;
        expected.push({ id: `cart-${system}`, type: "rp.n8.nes", ...(params ? { params } : {}) });
        continue;
      }
      expected.push(node);
    }
    // The wires, with the old ends that moved mapped onto the new ones, the cart mirror's id following its node.
    const mirror = od.nodes.find((node) => node.type === "rp.n8.cart-mirror");
    const cartId = mirror ? `cart-${mirror.settings?.system as number}` : null;
    const moved = (end: string): string => {
      const fixed = REWIRED[end];
      if (fixed !== undefined) return fixed;
      if (cartId !== null && end.startsWith("cart.")) return cartId + end.slice("cart".length);
      return end;
    };
    const wires = od.wires.map((w) => ({ from: moved(w.from), to: moved(w.to) }));
    // Count what moved, so the report says how much of each kind of move the file holds.
    pairs += od.nodes.filter((node) => node.type.startsWith("rp.host.controller-")).length;
    carts += od.nodes.filter((node) => node.type === "rp.n8.cart-mirror").length;
    surfaces += nd.nodes.filter((node) => node.type.startsWith("rp.launchpad.surface-")).length;
    rewired += od.wires.filter((w) => moved(w.from) !== w.from || moved(w.to) !== w.to).length;
    if (expected.length !== nd.nodes.length) {
      problems.push(`${name}: ${nd.nodes.length} nodes, was ${expected.length}`);
    } else {
      expected.forEach((want, i) => {
        const got = nd.nodes[i];
        if (want.id !== got.id || want.type !== got.type) {
          problems.push(`${name}: node ${i} is ${got.id} (${got.type}), expected ${want.id} (${want.type})`);
          return;
        }
        if (canonicalJson(want) !== canonicalJson(got)) {
          problems.push(`${name}: ${want.id} (${want.type}) moved beyond its cart params`);
        }
      });
    }
    if (canonicalJson(wires) !== canonicalJson(nd.wires)) problems.push(`${name}: wires moved beyond the surface and cart`);
    if (canonicalJson(od) !== canonicalJson(nd)) changedDocs++;
  }
  console.log(
    `${newPath}: ${names.size} cases, ${changedDocs} with a changed document, ${movedIndices} whose document index ` +
      `moved; over those cases: ${pairs} host controller nodes removed, ${carts} cart mirrors retyped, ${surfaces} ` +
      `surface nodes placed, ${rewired} wires rewired`,
  );
  if (problems.length) {
    console.log(`  PROBLEMS (${problems.length}):`);
    for (const p of problems.slice(0, 40)) console.log(`    ${p}`);
    process.exitCode = 1;
  } else {
    console.log(
      "  nothing else moved: every other node, wire, slot, tap and model field is as it was",
    );
  }
}

const [mode, a, b] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (mode === "rewrite") rewrite(a);
else if (mode === "compare") compare(a, b);
else throw new Error("usage: rewrite <file> | compare <old> <new>");
````

feat(graph): the cart and the control surface are placed as nodes, and buildGraph wires them

The TS switch-over (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 8, commit 5): buildGraph places the hardware,
TS stages at nodes instead of at systems, the UI's cart menu rides the capability jobs, and the hosts stop feeding
the old engine paths. Nothing of the old machinery is deleted here (stage 6 does that); this stage stops using it.

Placement is by setting. A NES's core config gains `driveRealCart` (additive, default ON: it is what every project
did before the setting existed, when the first NES's traffic reached the cart whether or not one was plugged in).
buildGraph places ONE rp.n8.nes - for the first NES in slot order whose setting is on (the type is unique, one cart
one link) - and fans it out from the same protocol-node outputs that feed that system's rp.mesen.nes `midi` and
`bytes` inputs, with the system's expansion-volume knob as its param (the value the emulated node gets), and stops
placing rp.n8.cart-mirror. A NES whose setting is off hands the cart to the next NES that drives one. The System
menu gains the row; the store publishes a document when it moves (placement, not a live knob).

Staging addresses a node. `Engine::stageNodeMidi(nodeId, bytes)` rides the invoker's ring as an owning payload and,
at the drain, hands the bytes to whatever the plan RUNNING then places under that id through a new node interface,
rp.stage/1: a system node gives them to its core's ingress (the raw door where the core has one, so a rig SysEx is
not capped), a device node to its device (rp.n8.nes pushes to the cart's FIFO at frame 0, note bookkeeping
included). The id resolves at the drain, not at the push, so a plan that adds or removes the node under it is
handled. The engine reads no node's type. TS's `backend.stageNodeMidi` replaces `stageSystemMidi`; the BlipToaster
settings rows stage at `sys-<id>` and at `cart-<id>` when one is placed, and the test-native case moved with it.

The session reads and writes the surface. buildGraph wires rp.controller.session to rp.launchpad.surface-in (`in`,
`connected`) and rp.launchpad.surface-out (`out`) instead of rp.host.controller-in / -out, places both whenever the
controller setting is on (and neither when it is off), and stops placing the host controller nodes. The role goldens
are re-recorded; ProtocolNodes.test.cpp now runs the one wiring and its digests are unchanged, block for block.
The SDL standalone stops staging controller MIDI and draining controller output per block; the harness's
stageControllerIn and renderBlocks controller field wait in a HarnessSurfaceLink the test host installs, and a host
with none refuses a controller message rather than dropping it.

The cart menu rides capabilities. n8SdOps.ts submits rom.upload / sram.dump / sram.restore against the driven cart's
node, reading and writing the local file itself, keeping the busy state, the progress row and the error text; the
Settings > N8 port, Connect and lookahead rows wait while a job holds the cart. The module remembers the ROM this
session booted so a battery job names the same card folder (else the driven system's own ROM file). The UI stops
calling __rp_setN8ExpVol: the cart node's param is the one writer.

The hosts: the plugin and the SDL standalone stop installing the core byte sink and the raw-MIDI fallbacks gated on
cartMirrorSystemId. A project with no NES no longer forwards DAW MIDI straight to the cart (a MENU/DBG pattern no
longer has a path); a NES system driving the cart is the one way now, and it also runs an emulated core ("real cart
only" is later work).

Tests: buildGraph's placement and fan-out tables (one node for two driving NESes, the expansion param, the surface
placed with the controller and not without), the setting's publish, stage-to-a-node on the engine (a real NES's
accepted bytes, a fake cart's pushes, an unknown id, the id resolving against the running plan), the cart menu over
the mock tier's capability model (load, dump, restore, busy, progress, refusal), and the goldens re-recorded
(build-graph.json rebuilt from its own cases through buildGraph; build-graph-roles.json re-recorded by its test).

Review fixes. A live Expansion Volume edit now also sets the driven cart node's param (a live param publishes no
document, so the cart's own copy is the only thing that moves the real console's register), gated by the one
`drivesRealCartOf` predicate buildGraph places by, which the menu now reads too instead of re-deriving the default. The
surface's input node discards what its link holds on its first block after binding it, so presses queued while no
session read the device are dropped rather than replayed; a reactivate that keeps the handle is not a first block,
an engine-graph case pins both halves, and renderBlocks clears the harness link before a run. A staging case pins the
in-flight drain (the audio thread owning the queue) the old case's name claimed, the System menu's Drive Real Cart row
is pinned with the other NES rows (and absent on a Game Boy), and the comments on the paths the hosts stopped using say
so and name the next change.

### Task 6: the cart mirror and the controller channel leave the engine

Design section 3 and section 8 item 6. Everything the two nodes made userless goes: the cart mirror
(`coreByteSink_`, `setCoreByteSink`, `cartMirrorSystemId`, `SystemTable::cartMirror`, the mirror rules in `setGraph`,
and with them the engine's last console-by-kind check, `rp::host::systemNodeType`, and the `rp.n8.cart-mirror` type);
`stageSystemMidi` (its `DspCommand` kind and `freePending` arm, `QueuedInvoker`'s method, `EngineRpcService`'s method
and registration, and `Engine`'s own, since `rp.stage/1` reaches the same core); the controller channel
(`pendingControllerMidi_`, `controllerConnected_` / `setControllerConnected`, `controllerOut_` and its accessors,
`DspCommand::Kind::StageControllerMidi`, `rp.host.controller-in` / `-out` and their halves of `rp.engine.host-io`, which
moves from `/2` to `/3`); and the N8 host's SD worker (`N8SdWorker`, `controlJob`, `startLoadRom`, `startDumpSram`,
`startRestoreSram`, `sdStatus`) with the five `__rp_n8*` operation and volume hooks. The tests of the deleted paths go
with them, and the behaviours the nodes keep are pinned where they live now. The manual N8 hardware harness is
re-pointed through `submitCartJob`, not deleted. Package versions stay `1.0.0`.

-// A Game Boy (sys-1, MI.OUT capture armed) and a NES (sys-2) that the cart mirror names, the Game Boy's serialOut
-// wired to the mirror's bytes input: the core-byte sink sees every byte the port carries. The Game Boy's core.
-SameBoySystem* serialOutToCart(Engine& e) {
+// A cart link, always attached, that keeps every push in a slot of its own.
+class RecordingCart final : public rp::host::CartLink {
+public:
+    struct Push {
+        std::uint32_t frame = 0;
+        bool          flush = false;
+        std::uint16_t size  = 0;
+        std::uint8_t  data[rp::host::kMaxDeviceMessage] = {};
+    };
+
+    void push(std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, bool flush, double) override {
+        Push p;
+        p.frame = frame;
+        p.flush = flush;
+        p.size  = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(std::min(size, rp::host::kMaxDeviceMessage));
+        std::memcpy(p.data, data, p.size);
+        pushes.push_back(p);
+    }
+    bool              connected() const override { return true; }
+    std::uint64_t     dropped() const override { return 0; }
+    void              setExpansionVolume(int) override {}
+    std::vector<Push> pushes;
+};
+
+// A Game Boy (sys-1, MI.OUT capture armed) with its serialOut wired to a NES's bytes input (sys-2) and to an
+// rp.n8.nes, as buildGraph fans one system's generated bytes out to its emulated node and its cart: the link sees
+// every byte the port carries. The Game Boy's core.
+SameBoySystem* serialOutToCart(Engine& e, RecordingCart& cart) {
     std::vector<DocSystem> systems{{1, kGb, 0, R"("model":"dmgB","serialOutCapture":"drive")"},
                                    {2, kNes}};
     rp::host::test::Roms roms;  // this document's puts: its caller publishes nothing else
     withRoms(e, systems, roms);
-    DocExtras extras{{docNode("cart", "rp.n8.cart-mirror", R"({"system":2})")}, {docWire("sys-1.serialOut", "cart.bytes")}};
+    DocExtras extras{{docNode("cart", "rp.n8.nes")},
+                     {docWire("sys-1.serialOut", "sys-2.bytes"), docWire("sys-1.serialOut", "cart.bytes")}};
+    e.setDeviceLinks(&cart, nullptr);
     REQUIRE(e.setGraph(graphRequest(stereoDocument(systems, extras), {1, 2})).ok);
     return dynamic_cast<SameBoySystem*>(e.findSystem(1));
 }

Run: `sed -n '14830,15965p' docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-plan.md | git apply --check`
Expected: nothing: the range is this block's diff and it applies cleanly. Run the same range without `--check` to apply it, which keeps trailing whitespace in context lines exactly as the prototype has it.

No build here: the adapted tests use the two-pointer `EngineHostIo` Step 2 lands (`NodeRig.hpp`,
`ProtocolNodes.test.cpp` and `ScriptBench.test.cpp` initialize it), and the two test files Step 2 deletes are still
listed in `tests.cmake`, so this step's tree is a test half by design. Step 4 builds and runs everything, after the
production deletions and the SD worker's own files have landed.

- [ ] **Step 2: Delete the cart mirror, the staging RPC and the controller channel**

`Engine` loses the cart-mirror members, rules and accessor, the controller fields, the command kinds and the staging
method; `SystemTable` loses `cartMirror`; `DspCommand` leaves holes at 13 and 15 (kinds are never serialised);
`EngineInvoker` and `EngineRpcService` lose their methods and `BackendRpcRegistration.hpp` its line. `HostIoNodes`
loses `rp.host.controller-in` / `-out` and its controller and cart halves of `rp.engine.host-io`, whose id moves to
`/3` with a comment recording what left. `HostServices.hpp`'s comment names the two surface nodes that replaced the
members. `SystemNodes.hpp/.cpp` loses `systemNodeType` and its now-unused include. The comments in `DeviceLinks.hpp`,
`LaunchpadNodes`, `LaunchpadLink`, `LaunchpadScanner`, `LaunchpadHost`, `N8Link`, `N8Menu`, `N8CartLink` and the two
controller TS files stop naming the removed engine paths. `HostServices.hpp` and `BackendRpcRegistration.hpp` are the
only code comments whose counts move (the RPC union is 89, the emulator facet 15). The two test files and the
`tests.cmake` entries that list them are deleted here too, so the unlisting lands in the same step; there is no run
here, because `N8Host` still uses `N8SdWorker.cpp` until the next step deletes it, and the next step's tree builds.

-// Guards what a connected physical N8 is fed: the cart MIRRORS the one emulated system the running plan's
-// rp.n8.cart-mirror names (Engine::cartMirrorSystemId; TS wires it from the first NES in slot order, buildGraph.ts),
-// and gets exactly what that system's emulated FIFO gets from its protocol nodes: its MIDI after the project's routing
-// and its generated bytes. Nothing from any other system reaches it, and a message staged straight at the mirrored
-// system (a UI setting) reaches it too, judged against the plan the drain has just adopted.
-//
-// Why it matters: until the kernel fed the cart, the plugin also pushed the DAW's raw MIDI straight to it, BEFORE the
-// kernel. The kernel's MIDI routing then reached the emulator only: a message routed to another instance, or given
-// another channel (midiChannelToInstance), reached the cart as the DAW sent it. Now the hosts skip that raw forward
-// while cartMirrorSystemId() != 0, and fall back to it with no NES system to mirror.
-//
-// Real cores placed by a graph document, as TS places them (a system node takes only a core of its own type, so a
-// fake one cannot be placed), wired as buildGraph wires them: rp.host.midi-in into the MIDI routing script node, each
-// system's routed MIDI into its rp.n8.midi-to-fifo node and on to the system, risa's host sync from its rp.risa.sync
-// node, and the mirror from the mirrored system's protocol nodes. Run via `pnpm test:plugin`.
-

-namespace {
-
-constexpr double kRate = 48000.0;
-constexpr std::uint32_t kFrames = 256;
-
-using Bytes = std::vector<std::uint8_t>;
-
-struct Sent {
-    std::uint32_t frame;
-    Bytes         bytes;
-    bool          flush;
-    bool operator==(const Sent&) const = default;
-};
-
-// Two NES systems, 1 and 2, in `slots` order, each running the NES's MIDI forward, and `synced` (0 for neither)
-// risa's host sync too, under midiChannelToInstance routing (channel n to the system in slot n, rewritten to channel
-// 1); the cart mirrors `mirrored`, or nothing when it is 0: what its forward sends, and what its host sync sends when
-// it has one, as buildGraph wires a cart.
-Engine::GraphRequest twoNes(std::uint32_t rom, std::vector<SystemId> slots, SystemId mirrored, SystemId synced = 0) {
-    std::string ids;
-    for (const SystemId id : slots) ids += (ids.empty() ? "" : ",") + std::to_string(id);
-    DocExtras extras;
-    extras.nodes = {docNode("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in"),
-                    docNode("routing", "rp.midi.route", R"({"mode":"midiChannelToInstance","systems":[)" + ids + "]}")};
-    extras.wires = {docWire("midi-in.midi", "routing.midiIn")};
-    for (const SystemId id : slots) {
-        const std::string sys = "sys-" + std::to_string(id), forward = sys + "/nes-n8-midi", sync = sys + "/risa-sync";
-        extras.nodes.push_back(docNode(forward, "rp.n8.midi-to-fifo"));
-        extras.wires.push_back(docWire("routing." + sys, forward + ".midiIn"));
-        extras.wires.push_back(docWire(forward + ".midi", sys + ".midi"));
-        if (id == synced) {
-            extras.nodes.push_back(docNode(sync, "rp.risa.sync"));
-            extras.wires.push_back(docWire(sync + ".bytes", sys + ".bytes"));
-        }
-        if (id != mirrored) continue;
-        extras.nodes.push_back(docNode("cart", "rp.n8.cart-mirror", R"({"system":)" + std::to_string(mirrored) + "}"));
-        extras.wires.push_back(docWire(forward + ".midi", "cart.midi"));
-        if (id == synced) extras.wires.push_back(docWire(sync + ".bytes", "cart.bytes"));
-    }
-    std::vector<DocSystem> nodes;
-    for (const SystemId id : slots) nodes.push_back({id, kNesType, rom});
-    return graphRequest(stereoDocument(nodes, extras), slots);
-}
-
-struct Rig {
-    Engine        eng{kRate};
-    std::uint32_t rom;  // the NES ROM both systems' nodes build from: one resource, two nodes
-    std::vector<Sent> cart;
-    Rig() { rom = putRom(eng, kNesType); }
-    void sink() {
-        eng.setCoreByteSink([this](std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, bool flush) {
-            cart.push_back({frame, Bytes(d, d + n), flush});
-        });
-    }
-    void block() {
-        float l[kFrames] = {}, r[kFrames] = {};
-        float* outs[2] = {l, r};
-        eng.processBlock(kFrames, outs, 2);
-    }
-};
-
-} // namespace
-
-TEST_CASE("the cart mirrors its system's protocol nodes - routed MIDI and generated bytes - and nothing else",
-          "[audio][engine][n8]") {
-    // Only system 2 runs risa's host sync, so neither system's output can pass for the other's: what the cart gets is
-    // pinned whole, and a byte from the system it does not mirror is one too many.
-    Rig rig;
-    REQUIRE(rig.eng.setGraph(twoNes(rig.rom, {1, 2}, 1, 2)).ok);
-    CHECK(rig.eng.cartMirrorSystemId() == 1);
-    rig.sink();
-    rig.eng.setTransport(true);             // system 2's sync arms and starts: none of it the cart's
-    rig.eng.stageMidi(3, {0x90, 60, 100});  // channel 1: slot 0, the cart's system
-    rig.eng.stageMidi(4, {0x91, 62, 100});  // channel 2: slot 1, not the cart's
-    rig.block();
-    CHECK(rig.eng.droppedMessages() == 0);
-    CHECK(rig.cart == std::vector<Sent>{{3, {0x90, 60, 100}, false}});
-
-    // System 2 mirrored instead, the transport stopped: its note, with its channel rewritten as its FIFO gets it, then
-    // its sync's stop, all the MIDI before the bytes as rp.n8.cart-mirror sends them. System 1's note stays off it.
-    rig.cart.clear();
-    REQUIRE(rig.eng.setGraph(twoNes(rig.rom, {1, 2}, 2, 2)).ok);
-    CHECK(rig.eng.cartMirrorSystemId() == 2);
-    rig.eng.setTransport(false);
-    rig.eng.stageMidi(5, {0x91, 64, 100});
-    rig.eng.stageMidi(6, {0x90, 65, 100});
-    rig.block();
-    CHECK(rig.cart == std::vector<Sent>{{5, {0x90, 64, 100}, false}, {0, {0xFC}, false}});
-
-    // And started again: the arm at the start of the song (flushing what the FIFO held), then the start. The block
-    // ends before the first clock after the armed one.
-    rig.cart.clear();
-    rig.eng.setTransport(true);
-    rig.block();
-    CHECK(rig.eng.droppedMessages() == 0);
-    CHECK(rig.cart == std::vector<Sent>{{0, {0xF9, 0x52, 0, 0, 0}, true}, {0, {0xFA}, false}});
-}
-
-TEST_CASE("no mirror node, or no sink: nothing to mirror, so the hosts forward raw MIDI instead", "[audio][engine][n8]") {
-    SECTION("no mirror node (TS places none without a NES)") {
-        Rig rig;
-        REQUIRE(rig.eng.setGraph(twoNes(rig.rom, {1, 2}, 0)).ok);
-        rig.sink();
-        CHECK(rig.eng.cartMirrorSystemId() == 0);
-        rig.eng.stageMidi(0, {0x90, 60, 100});
-        rig.block();
-        CHECK(rig.cart.empty());
-    }
-    SECTION("no sink (the CLI / tests)") {
-        Rig rig;
-        REQUIRE(rig.eng.setGraph(twoNes(rig.rom, {1, 2}, 1)).ok);
-        rig.eng.stageMidi(0, {0x90, 60, 100});
-        rig.block();  // the mirror must not touch a null std::function
-        QueuedInvoker inv(rig.eng);
-        inv.stageSystemMidi(1, {0xB0, 1, 2});  // nor must a message staged at the mirrored system
-    }
-}
-
-TEST_CASE("a message staged straight at the cart system (a UI setting) reaches the cart too", "[audio][engine][n8]") {
-    Rig rig;
-    REQUIRE(rig.eng.setGraph(twoNes(rig.rom, {1, 2}, 1)).ok);
-    rig.sink();
-    const Bytes sx{0xF0, 0x7D, 0x42, 0x03, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0xF7};

-    inv.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
-    inv.stageSystemMidi(1, sx);
-    inv.stageSystemMidi(2, sx);   // not the cart system
-    CHECK(rig.cart.empty());      // nothing until the drain
-    inv.drainInto(rig.eng);
-    inv.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
-    REQUIRE(rig.cart.size() == 1);
-    CHECK(rig.cart[0].bytes == sx);
-}
-
-TEST_CASE("a message staged at the cart is judged against the plan adopted ahead of it in the same drain",
-          "[audio][engine][n8]") {
-    // The ring carries a plan and the commands pushed after it in push order, and a command is applied against the
-    // plan current at its point of the drain. So a reorder that moves the mirror from system 1 to system 2, and a

-    // when they were staged.

-    inv.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
-    REQUIRE(rig.eng.setGraph(twoNes(rig.rom, {2, 1}, 2)).ok);  // queued: the audio thread adopts it at its next drain
-    CHECK(rig.eng.cartMirrorSystemId() == 1);           // still the running plan's
-    inv.stageSystemMidi(1, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x01, 0xF7});
-    inv.stageSystemMidi(2, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x02, 0xF7});
-    inv.drainInto(rig.eng);
-    CHECK(rig.eng.cartMirrorSystemId() == 2);
-    inv.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
-    REQUIRE(rig.cart.size() == 1);
-    CHECK(rig.cart[0].bytes == Bytes{0xF0, 0x7D, 0x02, 0xF7});
-}

-// Guards the N8 SD / menu control ops (Settings > N8 Pro) without hardware. Two layers:
-//   - N8SdWorker in isolation: the single-in-flight threading (busy / reject-while-busy / done / progress /
-//     error), with trivial jobs that never touch serial.
-//   - N8Host driving the load over a scripted fake ISerialPort that IGNORES writes and serves the exact reply bytes
-//     each Edio op reads (traced from Edio.cpp), the connection manager that pauses N8Link streaming around a control
-//     op and resumes it after, and the battery transfers it refuses (the capability jobs reach the battery file).

-// A serial port that ignores writes and pops pre-scripted reply bytes off `toRead`. An empty queue returns
-// 0 (Edio then throws a read timeout) - so a mis-counted script surfaces as a job error, not a hang.
-struct ScriptedFake : ISerialPort {
-    std::deque<std::uint8_t> toRead;
-    std::size_t write(const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t n) override { return n; }
-    std::size_t read(std::uint8_t* b, std::size_t n, int) override {
-        std::size_t i = 0;
-        while (i < n && !toRead.empty()) { b[i++] = toRead.front(); toRead.pop_front(); }

- [ ] **Step 3: Delete the N8 host's SD worker and its hooks**

`N8SdWorker.hpp/.cpp` are deleted, with `controlJob`, `startLoadRom`, `startDumpSram`, `startRestoreSram`, `sdStatus`,
the worker member and the factory member; `cartJobBusy()` alone gates the config writers and `submitCartJob`.
`N8Hooks.cpp` and `ui/host/nativeHooks.ts` lose `__rp_n8LoadRom`, `__rp_n8DumpSram`, `__rp_n8RestoreSram`,
`__rp_getN8SdStatus` and `__rp_setN8ExpVol`; four config hooks remain. `packages/native/CMakeLists.txt`,
`cmake/plugin.cmake` and `cmake/tests.cmake` lose their entries and stale comments, and the manual `n8-sd-hwtest`
submits through `submitCartJob`.

-// A single-in-flight background runner for the blocking N8 SD / menu control ops (ROM upload, 64 KB SRAM

-// the UI polls status() each frame. Lifecycle modeled on N8Link: a busy flag + a std::thread member LAST,
-// joined in the dtor (and before the next start). The job closure (built by N8Host) borrows the serial
-// port from N8Link, drives a C++ Edio, and reports progress through the Progress handle; throwing marks the
-// job failed.
-class N8SdWorker {
-public:
-    // Progress-reporting handle passed to a running job. Thread-safe (the UI reads the same fields).
-    class Progress {
-    public:
-        void phase(const std::string& p);   // short status label; bumps version
-        void total(std::uint64_t n);         // set bytesTotal
-        void advance(std::uint64_t n);       // bytesDone += n
-        void result(const std::string& r);   // success summary
-
-    private:
-        friend class N8SdWorker;
-        explicit Progress(N8SdWorker& w) : w_(w) {}
-        N8SdWorker& w_;
-    };
-
-    // A unit of work. Runs on the worker thread; a thrown std::exception becomes the job's error.
-    using Job = std::function<void(Progress&)>;
-
-    N8SdWorker() = default;
-    ~N8SdWorker();

-

-    N8SdStatusDto status();
-
-private:
-    void bump() { version_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_release); }
-
-    std::atomic<bool>          busy_{false};
-    std::atomic<std::uint64_t> bytesDone_{0};
-    std::atomic<std::uint64_t> bytesTotal_{0};
-    std::atomic<bool>          done_{false};
-    std::atomic<std::uint64_t> version_{0};

-    std::string        op_;
-    std::string        phase_;
-    std::string        error_;
-    std::string        result_;

+## 5. `rp.launchpad.surface-in` and `rp.launchpad.surface-out`
+
+**Two nodes, one each way.** One node that both fed a session and followed it is a node-level cycle, and the only wire a
+cycle breaks on is a feedback wire, which delivers the previous block. So the device's two directions are two nodes over
+the one link, each `unique` and each `threads`:
+
+- **`rp.launchpad.surface-in`**: `in`, an events output (the device's MIDI drained from the link's receive ring at the
+  start of the node's block, at frame 0: the device's traffic is not timed against the block); `connected`, a control
+  output. Its first block discards what the link held when it bound it, so traffic the device sent before the plan
+  existed is not replayed into a session.
+- **`rp.launchpad.surface-out`**: `out`, an events input written to the link's send ring.
+
+**Wiring**: the controller session script node reads `surface-in`'s `in` and `connected` and sends its LED and page
+output to `surface-out`'s `out`; its handshake (Programmer mode and a repaint on the block the link first reports
+connected) is unchanged. `buildGraph` places both whenever the controller setting is on, beside the session, and
+neither when it is off (a surface-in no session reads would drain the device's traffic nowhere).
+
+**They replace** the engine's controller staging, output buffer, connected flag and command kind, the controller halves
+of the two host I/O nodes, and the SDL standalone's per-block controller staging and drain. The host keeps scanning,
+pairing and the farewell; the config, pages and MI.MAP override stay TypeScript's. The session's recorded input and
+output digests and its per-block LED stream are identical through the two nodes, block for block.

+### Section 9's questions, answered
+
+- **How does a node reach a host-owned device across hosts, and what does a host with no device give it?** It binds
+  `rp.host.devices/1` once in `bind_host` and acquires by name in `activate` [control], releasing in its destroy. The
+  engine holds the pointers its host installed with `Engine::setDeviceLinks` before its first graph: the plugin passes
+  its `N8CartLink` and no surface (its DAW MIDI seam cannot carry SysEx, so it still owns no Launchpad), the SDL
+  standalone passes both, and the CLI, the Node addon, the render host and the UI harness install nothing. A name with
+  no device answers the never-connected handle above, so the same document plans and runs everywhere.
+- **Does pausing N8Link's streaming for a job need a change in the link, and what happens to bytes the graph pushes
+  meanwhile?** Yes, and the pause is inside the serial thread (stage 3 above). A disconnect loses the last lookahead's
+  chunks (note-offs among them), destroys the reliable sender's state, and lets another process take the port; the
+  pause writes what the ring holds, waits for the acks, keeps the port and the sequence, and runs the job on its own
+  Edio. Pushes during the pause are dropped and counted, and the node re-sends the note-offs it lost.
+- **Where does the UI-staged MIDI enter, and does stage-to-a-node cover every caller?** The BlipToaster rig SysEx from
+  the cart menu was the one production caller; it now stages at `sys-<id>` and at `cart-<id>` for the system that
+  drives the cart, and the harness's system-addressed callers moved to `stageNodeMidi`. The device-facing calls in the
+  SDL standalone and the harness's controller staging were not system-addressed staging at all and moved to the
+  surface nodes and the harness link. So yes: every caller is covered, and the system-addressed RPC could go.
+- **What does the UI's cart menu need from the capability API, and does the ROM load's lifecycle survive as a job?**
+  Progress (`onProgress`), a busy state (every row disabled while a job runs, Connect included), the refusal reason
+  verbatim in the row, and the result's own account of what happened: a restore reports the file and whether it created
+  the folder, an upload reports the card path, the mapper index and "streaming: stopped", with `enabled` cleared. Both
+  battery jobs run only at the N8 menu, and a running game refuses them; a restore goes before the `rom.upload` that
+  boots the game, whose rows say the game picks the battery file up at its next boot.
+- **Does the session's message digest stay identical through the surface, block for block?** Yes, with the two nodes;
+  the one-node version was refused as a cycle, and its only way through (a feedback wire) delivered the LEDs a block
+  late. Through `surface-in` / `surface-out` the session reads the same input queues, and its per-block LED stream and
+  every digest are the recorded ones; no golden was re-recorded for the rewiring (the role goldens' documents moved,
+  their digests did not).
+

+
+Each correction is in place; this is the list.
+
+- **Section 3**: "reconnecting after a reset or an SD operation" is a reset, or a job that stops the link (an upload);
+  the engine's losses gained `stageSystemMidi` itself, and the two devices bind through a typed acquire each.
+- **Section 4**: the staging command addresses a node, not its input (`rp.stage/1` chooses the door); the node
+  declares `unique` as well as `threads`; a removed node abandons its job at reclaim; a pause never leaves a note
+  sounding; the expansion volume is a standing value the link's serial thread applies.
+- **Section 5**: one `rp.launchpad.surface` became `rp.launchpad.surface-in` / `-out` (the cycle), each unique, with
+  the first-block discard.
+- **Section 6**: `sram/1` on the cart reads and writes the SD card's save file at the menu, not the cart's memory (the
+  DMA wedge); an emulated `sram.restore` is refused; `rom.header` / `rom.title` answer from what this host booted;
+  `rom.upload` ends with streaming stopped; the CLI's battery dump is the one cart-memory read left, and the menu's
+  battery jobs go through the SD card's save file.

+### Found while building
+
+The findings that changed a section are in it: the two surface nodes in section 5; the SD file's battery and the
+upload's stopped streaming in section 6. The ones worth naming on their own:
+
+- **One surface node is a cycle, and the session's digests are the cost of getting it wrong** (section 5). A surface
+  that feeds a session and follows it cannot be one node; the only wire a cycle breaks on is a feedback wire, so the
+  LEDs would have gone one block late. Two nodes cost the one-block latch nothing and no digest moved, which the
+  protocol cases hold block for block.
+- **A cart's battery cannot be read over USB on this hardware** (section 6). The direct cart-memory path this phase
+  tried first froze a running game, and at the menu a read left the menu deaf to its commands until a power-cycle: the
+  game's ROM is mid-DMA and nothing reinitialises the cart's file layer. Chunking did not help (16 x 4 KB reads took
+  16 s and wedged it too), so the SD card's own save file is the only path, and it exists only at the menu: a dump
+  takes about a minute.
+- **`postControl` was not needed, and neither is any call from the block into the link's thread** (section 4). The
+  expansion volume is a value the host holds with a generation counter: the block only clamps, stores and bumps, and
+  the serial thread applies the standing value at the top of its turn, so a failed write retries and no lock or
+  `std::function` is on the audio path.
+- **A project with no NES no longer forwards DAW MIDI to the cart** (section 4). The fallback existed for "no emulated
+  NES to mirror"; the cart is placed by a setting now, a raw copy beside the fan-out would arrive twice, and a user who
+  drove a MIDI cart with no NES system in the project (a MENU or debug pattern) loses that. Restoring it would be a rule
+  of the same shape as the one this phase removed, so it is noted rather than invented.
+- **The harness's controller seam only works where a host installs a surface link** (section 6, stage 5).
+  `stageControllerIn` and `renderBlocks`' controller field now queue into `HarnessSurfaceLink`, which only the test host
+  installs, and a harness-facet host without one refuses them rather than staging into nothing: a consumer suite built
+  on the old seam is a trap.
+- **`unique` is planner-wide** (section 5). A document with two surface-in, surface-out or cart nodes is refused with
+  code `unique` at plan time in every host, and a TS node type can declare it too.
+- **The engine's host I/O service moved to `/3`** (stage 6). A node built against `/2` reads a struct three members past
+  its end; every node is in tree, so nothing serialises the id and no shim was written.
+- **A package's version never gates** (stage 6). `rp.n8` keeps `1.0.0` after losing `rp.n8.cart-mirror`, and
+  `rp.host.io` keeps `1.0.0` after losing two node types: the planner refuses a removed type as `unknown-type` at any

+  (`N8Node.test.cpp`: the fan-out, `connected`, the expansion volume, owed note-offs, the jobs and their refusals,
+  abandonment, `threads`, a warmed block), `[launchpad]` (`Surface.test.cpp`: the drain, the output, `connected`, the
+  queue's bound, the first-block discard, uniqueness, `threads`, acquire balance, a warmed block) and `[stage]`
+  (`StageNode.test.cpp`: a staged message reaching the node the running plan places under the id, and one added later).
+  The protocol cases run the surface wiring and hold their recorded digests; the goldens' documents moved with the
+  fan-out and the surface nodes.
+- `retroplug-n8-test` gained `[cart-jobs]` (`N8CartJobs.test.cpp`: the pause and its ack bound, battery file dumps and
+  restores with their refusals, the upload and its `Stop`, a game's refusals, an abandoned dump), and the two link
+  adapters have their own files (`N8CartLink.test.cpp`, `LaunchpadSurfaceLink.test.cpp`).
+- TS: `test/capability/capability.test.ts` (the promises, the refusals, a close rejecting pending, progress), and on
+  the real host `test-native/capability.test.ts` and `test-native/stage-node-midi.test.ts`;
+  `test/graph/build-graph.test.ts` holds the placement and the fan-out,
+  `test/systems/store-graph.test.ts` the setting and the live expansion copy, and
+  `test/menu/n8-sd-ops.test.ts` the cart menu over the mock's capability model.
+

   own back-channel.

+### Device nodes, their links and capability jobs
+
+`rp.n8.nes` and `rp.launchpad.surface-in` / `-out` are the hardware nodes
+([N8Nodes.cpp](../packages/native/src/host/graph/N8Nodes.cpp),
+[LaunchpadNodes.cpp](../packages/native/src/host/graph/LaunchpadNodes.cpp)). Each binds the host-owned device it

+message (frame, bytes, the flush flag, the block's rate), the link's connected state and drop count, the
+expansion-volume register and `submitJob` / `abandonJobs`; a `SurfaceLink` for the pad, with a drain into the node's
+own array, a push, the connected state and its drop count. A host installs its links with

+standalone both, the test host a `HarnessSurfaceLink`, and the CLI, the Node addon and the render host neither), and a
+name it has no device for answers a handle that is never connected and that drops and counts everything, so a
+document plans and runs in every host. A node keeps its handle across a reactivate and gives it back once in destroy,
+which runs at reclaim on the control thread while the links are still installed: a host tears its plans down first
+(`Engine::clearGraph`), then uninstalls its links.
+
+A capability job ([CapabilityJobs.hpp](../packages/native/src/host/engine/CapabilityJobs.hpp)) is what `submitJob`
+takes: a request for a node of the last published plan, answered with an id or a refusal. A system node's job goes to the
+`memory()` / `sram()` / `rom()` accessor its core presents: a memory read is the published copy and a ROM header the
+core's immutable image, both at once, a write rides the command ring and completes once the block after its apply has
+published the region, and an emulated `sram.restore` is refused (a battery is a seed on a rebuild). A device node's
+job goes to its link, on the device's own thread: one at a time ("busy"), none while the device is not attached ("not
+connected"), progress reported per drain, and a node leaving the plan abandons the job it still runs. The engine keeps
+at most `kMaxJobs` (64) outstanding, engine-wide back-pressure that leaves room for every completion, and a request
+names a capability from the one reserved id space (`rp.system.memory/1`, `rp.system.sram/1`, `rp.system.rom/1`), so the
+engine asks a node only by an id it knows and never casts an answer.
+

+  each `rp.lsdj.serial-out`'s in slot order, and `surface-out` (`rp.launchpad.surface-out`), fed from the
   controller's `controllerOut`.
 
+The surface is two nodes because one that both feeds a session and follows it is a node-level cycle, and the
+only wire a cycle breaks on delivers the previous block; the two keep the session's recorded digests, and its
+per-block LED stream, unchanged.

 `publish({ systems, routing, midiRouting, controller }, { rearmTap })` makes that its model, builds the document at
 its host shape and sends it, skipping the send when the document's canonical text and slots match the

+    wedges it and leaves the menu deaf), and a restore goes before a `rom.upload` so the game loads it at its next

+    work only where a host installs `HarnessSurfaceLink` (the test host), and a harness-facet host with none refuses
+    them rather than staging into nothing.
+  - **The CLI's n8 tools keep their own raw serial path**, the battery dump among them: it is the one cart-memory
+    read left, and the capabilities deliberately offer no peek, poke, sniffer or FIFO reads.

**MIDI through `rp.n8.nes` in a real host.** The SDL standalone is the host that can do this: it owns an `N8Host` and
installs an `N8CartLink`, so a document that places `rp.n8.nes` gets a live link. It runs with no display or audio
device (`SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy`, the pair `tools/run-sdl-smoke.sh` uses), and
`RETROPLUG_USER_CONFIG_DIR` gives it a scratch config directory: an `n8.cfg` there enables the link on the
auto-detected port (three lines: an empty port line, `10`, `1`), `RETROPLUG_AUTOLOAD_PROJECT=build/nes.rplg.zip` loads
BlipToaster as an emulated NES whose default `driveRealCart` places `cart-1`, and the app always opens its virtual
`RetroPlug In` MIDI port. The cart menu's own Load ROM row cannot be driven headlessly (the smoke's hooks are fixed
and the row needs the native file dialog or mouse input), so the ROM comes from `retroplug-n8-hwtest load` above, the
same re-pointed job seam; this leg therefore proves the node's MIDI push, not the UI's job submission, and
`Engine::submitDeviceJob` and the TS capability promise remain covered only by the fakes. Say so in the report. If the
app's virtual port cannot be reached in this container, fall back to a CLI `build/bin/retroplug-cli n8-play on:1:69
wait:2000 off:1:69` against the running BlipToaster: that proves the ROM, the FIFO and the capture, but not
`rp.n8.nes`, so say then that the node's MIDI push is covered only by the fakes as well.

Run: `/workspaces/.nes-power.sh reset; sleep 40; fuser /dev/ttyACM0; build/bin/retroplug-n8-hwtest load resources/roms/bliptoaster.nes`
Expected: no process holds the port, and the upload reports `usb-games/bliptoaster.nes`, the mapper its header names and `streaming: stopped`: the console is at a fresh menu and BlipToaster now runs on the real cart, uploaded through the same job seam.

Run: `node tools/author-nes-rplg.js`
Expected: `authored build/nes.rplg.zip`: the scratch NES project, with BlipToaster embedded and Drive Real Cart on by default (the same fixture Task 8 Step 4 authors for the Reaper suite).

Run: `mkdir -p /tmp/c5-hw-cfg && printf '\n10\n1\n' > /tmp/c5-hw-cfg/n8.cfg && printf '\x4d\x54\x68\x64\x00\x00\x00\x06\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x60\x4d\x54\x72\x6b\x00\x00\x00\x14\x00\xff\x51\x03\x07\xa1\x20\x00\x90\x45\x64\x83\x00\x80\x45\x40\x00\xff\x2f\x00' > /tmp/c5-hw-a4.mid`
Expected: nothing printed: the scratch config dir enables the cart link (`n8.cfg`), and `/tmp/c5-hw-a4.mid` is a one-track MIDI file at 120 bpm holding A4 (note 69, channel 1) for 2 s and then its note-off.

Run: `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy RETROPLUG_USER_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/c5-hw-cfg RETROPLUG_AUTOLOAD_PROJECT=build/nes.rplg.zip RETROPLUG_SDL_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES=1200 build/bin/retroplug-sdl > /tmp/c5-hw-sdl.log 2>&1 & sleep 8; arecord -D hw:L6,0 -f S32_LE -r 48000 -c 12 -d 5 /tmp/c5-hw-midi.wav & sleep 0.5; aplaymidi -p "$(aplaymidi -l | awk '/RetroPlug In/ {print $1; exit}')" /tmp/c5-hw-a4.mid; wait`
Expected: the app logs `MIDI: virtual ports 'RetroPlug In' / 'RetroPlug Out' open`, the autoloaded project and the N8 restore line; `aplaymidi -l` lists the `RetroPlug In` port before the note is sent (if it names it as a `RetroPlug` client with an `In` port instead, pass that client:port explicitly; if no port is listed, the app has not finished booting: wait longer and resend); the note lands in the 5 s capture and the app exits on its frame budget.

Run: `build/bin/retroplug-cli analyze-capture /tmp/c5-hw-midi.wav --channel 3 --trim 0.5:2.5 --expect-hz 440`
Expected: a sounding window on channel 3 at A4 with a small cents error, and silence after the note-off. The prototype measured `A4 at 440.30 Hz` on this PAL console; if the note lands elsewhere in the capture, move the `--trim` window to it rather than changing the note.

Run: `pgrep -af build/bin/retroplug-sdl; sleep 1`
Expected: no process printed: the app exited on its frame budget. If one is listed, close it (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL if it is still there after 2 s) before any `n8-load` command: it holds `/dev/ttyACM0`.
